# Manuscript Binding

->[Front Cover]<-

The volume is bound in a reddish-brown leather <note>likely calfskin or goatskin, common for durable scholarly bindings of the period</note>. The front cover is decorated with a simple **blind-tooled** <term>blind-tooled: a technique where heated brass tools are pressed into dampened leather to create a design without using gold leaf</term> double-line border.

The leather shows significant signs of age and historical use, including several scratches, scuffs, and small patches of missing material near the top-left edge and top-right corner.

<column-break/>

->[Spine]<-

The spine, located on the right side of this view, features six **raised bands** <term>raised bands: horizontal ridges across the spine covering the cords used to sew the pages together</term> which divide the spine into seven distinct compartments.

In the third compartment from the top, there are faint remnants of gold-stamped lettering, though the title is now largely illegible due to wear. At the very bottom of the spine, there is a small, worn white paper label <note>likely a shelf-mark or library cataloging number added by a later collector</note>.

<summary>This page describes the physical exterior of the manuscript, a worn reddish-brown leather binding featuring blind-tooled borders and a spine with six raised bands. It represents the initial state of the artifact before the text begins.</summary>

<keywords>binding, leather, blind-tooling, spine, raised bands, manuscript conservation</keywords>

--- Page 8 ---
<meta>This page continues the introduction to the *Kitāb al-Bulhān* (The Book of Wonders). While the previous page provided the formal title and ownership history, this page serves as the author's formal preface, known as a *muqaddimah*. It establishes the philosophical framework of the book, focusing on the "Chain of Being"—the idea that all creation is interconnected from minerals up to humans.</meta>

->### My Lord, make it easy and complete it with goodness<-
<note>original: "Rabbi yassir wa-tammim bi-l-khayr" – A traditional pious formula used by scribes at the beginning of a task to seek divine assistance.</note>

In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. Thus says the weakest of God’s servants and the one most in need of His mercy and forgiveness:
**Abd al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan**, originally of **Isfahan**, born in **Baghdad**, and known as **al-Burhani**.

Praise be to God, who brought all beings into existence and created all that is found. He raised the high heavens and spread out the leveled earths, steadying them with firm-rooted mountains. He caused flowing springs to run through them and carved the channels of the streams. Through these, He brought forth varieties of plants and the creatures of the surging seas. He draped the traveling ships upon the surface of the waters. Glory be to Him, the Exalted, for the noble gifts He has granted His servants—precious rarities and abundant favors. In every created thing, He deposited unique <term>properties</term> and benefits, governing them through the spirits that dwell within otherwise lifeless bodies.
<term>properties</term> <note>original: "khawass" – In medieval science, this refers to the hidden "occult" qualities of substances (like the magnetism of a lodestone) that cannot be explained by the four elements alone.</note>

Reflect, O possessor of intellect, upon the solid minerals: those dense bodies with radiant colors. <unclear>From</unclear> among them are liquid bodies and others that are solid. It is enough to consider the **coral**, which is the **intermediary** between the mineral and the plant kingdoms.
<unclear>For</unclear> it is like a tree with spreading branches, yet He categorized it among the solid bodies. Glory be to the Wise One, who by His power dazzled the insights of <unclear>the</unclear> perceiving minds! He is the one who made plants a sustaining food for animals through nutrition, and made them into substances <unclear>in</unclear> which various types of nourishment are "cooked" <note>referring to the biological process of digestion/metabolism</note>. This is seen especially in the **date palm**, which—through its unique qualities—stands as the **intermediary** between trees and animals.

<unclear>He</unclear> is the one who diversified their various forms and distinguished their differing natures, setting some to prevail over others in the wilderness. <unclear>He</unclear> distinguished some animals with a sense capable of being taught, so that they understand gestures—specifically the **ape**, which is the **intermediary** between <unclear>the</unclear> "silent" animals and the subtle human being. It has even been taught certain crafts and understands most <unclear>ex</unclear>pressions regarding the handling of tools; in its physical makeup, it resembles the arrangement of a human more than any other creature.

<unclear>We</unclear> praise Him with much praise and thank Him with great thanks for the encompassing blessings He has bestowed, <unclear>and</unclear> for the magnificent gifts He has specifically granted to humanity. He distinguished the human being with "subtle arrivals" <note>spiritual or intellectual inspirations</note> and inspired him with the intellects by <unclear>which</unclear> the perfection of life is achieved. He taught him knowledge—the very substance of life and the means of living after death—and gave him the power of speech in various languages <unclear>to</unclear> express the intentions within his heart. He aided him through the arrangement of the tongue, teeth, and lips. In every <unclear>th</unclear>ing, there is a sign for Him, testifying that He is One, the very essence and pure cream of humanity.

<summary>This preface by Abd al-Hasan al-Isfahani establishes a "Chain of Being," describing how God created intermediaries like coral (between mineral/plant), the date palm (between plant/animal), and the ape (between animal/human).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the formal preface (muqaddimah) of the Kitāb al-Bulhān. While the previous page discussed the creation of the physical world and the "Chain of Being" from minerals to plants, this page moves to the spiritual realm, the role of the Prophet Muhammad, and the specific purpose of this book as a remedy for the weary soul. It introduces the concept of the human being as a "Microcosm."</meta>

...the prophets, the masters of miracles, especially our Prophet Muhammad—the one sent with <term>comprehensive speech</term> to all nations with clear signs and decisive proofs. He was for us the greatest purifier, by which our souls, stained by the cloak of worldly habits, are cleansed, and through which our spirits are colored with the hues of perfection. He ordained the **pillars of worship**, consisting of **fasting, prayer, pilgrimage, and almsgiving**, so that they might harmonize with the celestial spirits and the angels. <insert>May God grant him a pure blessing</insert> <unclear>...</unclear> his love for those of pure essences at all times, and upon his Family <unclear>...</unclear> and upon his Companions, the people of affection and obedience.

<term>comprehensive speech</term> <note>original: "jawami‘ al-kilam" – A traditional description of the Prophet Muhammad's eloquence, meaning the ability to express vast, profound meanings in very few words.</note>

**As for what follows:** 

Since the soul, in certain states, grows weary and deviates from its balance due to various boredoms, I have devised for it "strange movements" and "rare tales" of diverse kinds. This is a book I have designed, encompassing some of these indications through **illustrated depictions** and **categorized forms**. It contains subtleties of both the serious and the humorous, as well as beneficial lessons <unclear>...</unclear> guidance and safety from afflictions. I sought protection for it from the "slip of the pen" and the "stumble of the foot" <unclear>...</unclear> for He is the Knower of what is best for His servants and the different degrees they deserve. 

<unclear>...</unclear> in the name of the dear brother, the "Tongue of the Age," possessor of virtues and crafts <unclear>...</unclear> **Sunqur al-Arjali** <note>The name is partially obscured; "Sunqur" was a common name for high-ranking military or administrative officials in the Mamluk era.</note>, may his shadow endure and his station be exalted. He may read it from time to time, use it when needs arise, or store it away for important matters. 

I ask whoever reads this to be forgiving of any oversights or slips they may see, and to drape over it the veil of pardon and generosity, for that is more fitting for people of noble character. For what book is more beneficial to study than the book of **your own form**, which gathers all the realities of existence and the intricacies of all beings? As it has been said:

*And you are the <term>Manifest Book</term> whose letters*
*Reveal what is hidden...* <unclear>...</unclear>
*And from you, the news is told.*
*You claim to be but a small body,*
*Yet within you, the **Greater World** is folded.*

<term>Manifest Book</term> <note>original: "al-Kitab al-Mubin" – A term often used for the Qur'an, but here used metaphorically to describe the human being as a living text that reflects God's creation.</note>

<note>This poem is famously attributed to Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. It expresses the concept of the Microcosm: that the human being contains the entirety of the universe (the Macrocosm) within themselves.</note>

He who possesses such a quality, how could he need anything external to guide him? <unclear>...</unclear>

And may God bless our master Muhamm— <unclear>...</unclear>

# Discourse on the Iconography of the First Sign: Aries

->[Aries and the Planet Mars]<-

<image-desc>
A large central circular miniature set within a red square frame. It depicts a man with a mustache and a white pointed cap riding a white ram with black spots—the symbol of the zodiac sign Aries. The man, representing the planet Mars (the ruler of this sign), wears a red short-sleeved tunic over long sleeves and purple trousers. In a display of martial power, he holds a sword over his right shoulder and carries a severed human head by its long hair in his left hand. The dark blue background is decorated with nine discs, likely representing the stars or planetary bodies.
</image-desc>

# Discourse on the Second Sign, which is the Sign of Taurus

The person born under this face <note>In medieval astrology, a "face" or decan refers to a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign that refines the individual's character traits.</note> will be ruddy in complexion, possessing a dignified presence and a sharp temperament. He will have a strong sexual drive and a love for adornment and courage. He asks nothing of God except to be granted happiness in the latter part of his life. He shall have a long life and his words will be listened to <note>This implies a person of influence or natural authority.</note>, though it is feared that he may face the danger of drowning in his youth, and God knows best.

-> **His wealth is governed by Jupiter and Venus** <-

The majority of his wealth will come from his relatives. He shall be granted sustenance through plowing and agriculture, and perhaps he will obtain wealth from a woman of great standing, and God knows best.

-> **His brothers, sisters, transitions, and movements are governed by Gemini and Mercury; his brothers shall be better for him than** <-

strangers, for strangers will loathe and envy him. He shall have a virtuous brother from whom he will receive goodness. He is quick in his movements and does not remain settled in a single state, and God knows best.

-> **His parents, property, and estate are governed by Cancer and the Moon; he shall have little luck from his parents, and the mother shall die before the father** <-

He will receive an inheritance from them, but it will not remain with him. The house in which he was born will fall into ruin, and he shall build a different house for himself, and God knows best.

<margin>
He shall see much goodness in his travels; perhaps he will travel by sea. He will have little luck regarding his enemies, but God Almighty will grant him victory over them.
</margin>

# The Second Face of Gemini under Mars

<margin>
It was also said that if his ascendant is Sagittarius at twenty-seven degrees, then his ascendant in the sign of Virgo is at eighteen degrees—and God knows best.
</margin>

The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A person born under this face will have bluish-grey eyes <note>original: "أشهل العينين" (ashhal al-'aynayn) - describing eyes with a mixture of colors, often grey or hazel</note> and a complexion leaning toward a reddish hue. He possesses a sharp temperament; a single word can make him pleased, and a single word can make him angry. He has a mark on his leg, a handsome beard, and a small head. There is a scar or mark on his flank. As he advances in years, his status shall grow great. He is able to extract what is in the hearts of others while never revealing his own secrets. He is eloquent and talkative, though he is prone to melancholy. He occupies himself with delicate and fine crafts, such as engraving, sewing, and similar works—and God knows best.

---

**His Wealth:** Under the influence of the Sultan and the Moon. He shall have good fortune in buying and selling, and he may come to own a servant or a bondwoman and receive provision through her—and God knows best.

---

**His Brothers and Sisters,** his movements, and his journeys: Under Leo and the Sun. He will have little luck in his livelihood from his siblings. He will receive provision from some of his brothers and pass it on to others. He shall be of great age—and God knows best.

---

**His Parents and Property:** Under Virgo and Mercury. He will have good fortune from his mother's side. He may lose one of his parents during his youth and receive an inheritance from them, but it will not remain in his possession; the remainder will be left after his lifetime—and God knows best.

---

**His House of Joys and Children:** Under Libra and Venus. Most of his children will be female. He may lose some of them, but he will find support and joy in them as they grow older—and God knows best.

---

**His Illnesses and Thoughts:** Under Scorpio and Mars. There is a fear that he may suffer an illness caused by "drinking iron" <note>likely referring to a medicinal preparation containing iron, or a metaphor for a wound from a metal weapon</note>. If he survives it, he will live a long life—and God knows best.

---

**His Women and Partnerships:** Under Sagittarius and Jupiter. He will be infatuated with women, loving sexual intercourse, with a sharp gaze and strong desire. He will marry several women and will inherit from one of his wives—and God knows best.

# Discourse on the Third Face, Ruled by the Sun

<margin>
It is consistent with the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Goodness is in me and in my community until the Day of Resurrection." Among the signs of happiness are sincerity of the heart and offering kindness to those one loves. Among the signs of wretchedness are hardness of the heart and offering kindness to those who do not deserve it. The person born under this Face will be happy in his life and beloved. God knows best what is right, and to Him is the return and the final home.
</margin>

**The person born under this Face** will be fair-skinned with a reddish tint, large-bodied, of good physique, with handsome eyes and a broad chest. He has a wide forehead and a mark or scar on his face and another on his leg. He is light-spirited and eloquent <note>original: "ذرب اللسان" (dharib al-lisan) - literally "sharp-tongued," but in this context meaning someone who is articulate or witty</note>. He socializes with all kinds of people and sits with leaders and state officials. In his youth, there is a fear of danger for him, but the end of his life shall be better than its beginning. He is not bothered by hardships and will be long-lived. There is a fear that he may suffer from inflammation of the eyes <note>original: "رمد" (ramad) - likely conjunctivitis or a similar ophthalmic condition</note> in his fifteenth year; if he survives it, he shall live for ninety-five years—and God knows best.

**His House of Wealth:** Cancer and the Moon. He will be granted wealth through service, and he will have good fortune in trade at certain times. He is quick in his movements, and silver coins or gold dinars hold no great value or worth in his hand—and God knows best.

**His House of Siblings,** his transfers, and his movements: Leo and the Sun. He will be a leader over his siblings, and they will receive more comfort and benefit from him than he receives from them—and God knows best.

**His House of Parents** and his properties: Virgo and Mercury. He will lose one of his parents in his youth, and because of this, he will experience some hardship in his adulthood. However, he will receive good things from his father, will be a blessing to them, and will eventually bury them all—and God knows best.

**His House of Joys** and children: Libra and Venus. Most of his children will be female, and there is a fear for the males among them. He will be granted a child from a slave-girl <note>original: "جارية" (jariya) - traditionally referring to a concubine or domestic servant in a historical household context</note> and will rejoice in him, seeing goodness, mercy, and blessing upon his face—and God knows best.

**His House of Illnesses:** Scorpio and Mars. Most of his ailments will arise from phlegm and excess moisture. There is fear for him regarding pain in the chest and kidneys. He should care for himself by taking medicinal drinks <note>original: "المشروب" (al-mashrub) - likely referring to herbal tonics or syrups</note> in every season to find relief—and God knows best.

**His House of Women** and partnership: Sagittarius and Jupiter. Most of his children from women will be female. He will marry a group of women and will experience much evil, worry, and grief from them—and God knows best.

**His House of Death:** Saturn. The cause of his death will be from a nasal medicine <note>original: "سعوط" (sa'ut) - a medicinal powder or liquid inhaled through the nose</note> or from bowel pain. Drinking infusions <note>original: "نقوع" (naqu') - an herbal infusion or cold-water maceration</note> will suit him. If the ascendant of the year is Capricorn and Saturn is in that direction, it will be because of a slave-girl—and God knows best.

**His House of Travel:** Aquarius and Saturn. He loves travel and will find abundant fortune in it. His best travels are toward the West, where he will find much good. He will have little luck in partnerships or acting as a guarantor for others—and God knows best.

**His House of Authority** and work: Pisces and Jupiter. He will be well-received by governors, but there is a fear for him from the Sultan <note>The "Sultan" here represents the highest state authority or the ruler</note> if he is positioned to the ruler's left—and God knows best.

**His House of Hope** and happiness: Aries and Mars. He will harbor many hopes and will achieve them through the direction of women. He will have little luck from men and friends; he is better to them than they are to him—and God knows best.

**His House of Enemies** and their remedy: Taurus and Venus. He will have enemies and envious people, but he will not care about them due to the strength of his rising sign. He should not eat anything from a hand he does not trust, as there is a fear of poisoned or harmful food from the hand of an enemy; may God keep him safe from them. His best day is Wednesday and his worst is Friday. His best clothes when traveling are his morning garments. His food should be hot and moist. His best colors are white and green. Among animals, sorrel horses are best. His direction is the West. Among ailments, he should watch for hemorrhoids. Among drinks, pomegranate juice is best. Among women and partners, his match is one whose rising sign is Sagittarius. When he enters before a ruler, he should stand on his right to have his needs met. When he sleeps, he should place his head toward the West. O you who read this house, remember God—and God alone knows best the unseen.

The sage Abu Ma’shar <note>original: "Abu Ma'shar" refers to the famous 9th-century Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar, whose works were central to both Islamic and European medieval astrology.</note> says: One born in this face <term>face: also known as a decan, this refers to a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> will be white-complexioned, with eyebrows that meet, a flat nose, and kohl-black eyes. He is of moderate stature and eloquent in speech. He is truthful in his dealings, though there are fears for him regarding rumors or speech spoken against him. Within himself, he is a person of great importance, yet silent and prone to holding a grudge. All his affairs are kept hidden. Time will turn against him; he may be absent-minded, but he will rise in status and live in luxury and happiness. However, he will be afflicted by some harm in the middle of his life, or thereabouts—and God knows best.

**His Wealth:** Leo and the Sun. He will have a good life but will not be granted wealth except through great effort. He will have luck in trade, and traveling by sea will bring him benefit—and God knows best.

**His Brothers and Sisters:** Virgo and Mercury. He will have siblings and will spend much on their account, yet he will have little luck from them. A stranger will be better for him than his own family. The best course for him is to distance himself from his family and remain independent—and God knows best.

**His Fathers and Mothers:** Libra and Venus. He will be a blessing to his parents. He may be the firstborn of his mother and father, and he might be nursed by a group of different women. He will practice a craft other than that of his father—and God knows best.

**His Joys and Children:** Scorpio and Mars. Most of his children will be female, and he will see goodness and blessing through them. His children will be righteous. It is decreed for him that a child will be born to him from a maidservant, and he will care for an orphan—and God knows best.

**His Illnesses and Thoughts:** Sagittarius and Jupiter. Most of his illnesses arise from phlegm and dampness <note>In medieval medicine, health was governed by four "humors"; phlegm was associated with cold and moist qualities.</note>. There is a fear for him regarding kidney pain, and eating salty foods will harm him—and God knows best.

**His Women and Partnership:** Capricorn and Saturn. He will marry three women. He will acquire wealth because of women, but he will also experience hardship through them. He will marry a woman of humble origins <note>original: "in her origin is slavery," likely referring to a lower social class or a formerly enslaved background common in medieval social structures</note>; he will have two children with her, and she will be of blessed countenance—and God knows best.

**His Fear and Death:** Aquarius and Saturn. He will be long-lived. The cause of his death will be pain in the chest or a chronic illness <note>original: "al-matraniyya," likely a corruption of a medical term for a persistent ailment</note>. Astringent medicines should be used. There is a fear of him falling from a high place, though he will survive it—and God knows best.

**His Travels:** Pisces and Jupiter. He will travel many leagues. His best travels will be toward the direction of the Qibla <note>The direction of Mecca; for the author, this likely implies southward or southeastward travel.</note>, and traveling by water is better for him than traveling by land—and God knows best.

**His Authority and Work:** Aries and Mars. He will be bold in his affairs; if he intends a matter, he executes it. He will be brought close to kings and nobles, gaining luck and acceptance from them—and God knows best.

**His Hopes and Happiness:** Taurus and Venus. He will triumph in all that he desires. He will be chosen by all his friends; they will have need of him, while he has no need of them—and God knows best.

**His Enemies and Beasts:** Gemini and Mercury. He will have enemies of wicked intent who will treat him poorly. We fear for him regarding his handiwork. He should not involve himself in the disputes of others. God will take his soul on a Monday, or ideally a Wednesday.

The month that suits him is July <note>original: "Tammuz"</note>, and the best direction is the South (Yemen). Of foods, he should eat everything hot and dry. His temperament is influenced by the dust of apples <note>possibly a specific medicinal preparation</note>. His best clothing is white, and his best mount is a piebald horse. His medicine should be cooked (decoctions). Among friends, his best companions are those whose star is in Taurus or Venus. Among women and partners, those with the star of Taurus are best. When he enters before a ruler, he should stand on his left side to have his needs met. When he sleeps, he should place his head toward the direction of the Qibla; he will then be safe from the evil of crawling things and pests. God knows best what is hidden and is the Most Wise.

His nature is feminine <note>original: "niswiyya," often used in astrology to describe the "passive" or "receptive" qualities of certain signs or planets</note>.

# Discourse on the Second Face of the Two Signs of Mercury

<margin>
The sage Abu Ma’shar the Astronomer <note>original: "Abu Ma'shar al-Falaki," the 9th-century scholar known in the West as Albumasar, whose work blended Persian, Indian, and Greek astrology.</note> says: One born in this face <term>face: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</term> will be tan in complexion, lean of body, with straight hair and a thin beard. He loves the pursuit of knowledge, jurisprudence <term>jurisprudence: the study of religious law (Fiqh)</term>, geometry, and fine crafts. He is known for his trustworthiness, piety, and devotion. He will be granted the opportunity for pilgrimage <term>Hajj: the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca</term> and religious struggle. He will be a jealous man whose words are obeyed, yet he is envied by everyone. He will live in perpetual grace and happiness, and the end of his life will be better than its beginning—and God knows best.
</margin>

<unclear>Said</unclear> <unclear>Ibn Arabi</unclear> <note>Likely referring to the famous Sufi mystic and scholar Muhyiddin ibn Arabi, who often integrated astrology into his cosmology.</note>: One born in this face will be wise, intelligent, and chaste. He is tan-colored and of average height among men, with straight hair, a lean body, and thin legs. He possesses a quick wit and cleverness. You love the pursuit of knowledge, jurisprudence, geometry, and delicate craftsmanship. He is called to trustworthiness, religion, and piety, and is granted the pilgrimage to the Sacred House of God and religious struggle. He will be prone to much anger and jealousy, yet his speech is followed. He is envied by everyone. He lives in grace and lasting happiness; his end is better than his beginning—and God knows best.

**The House** of his wealth is Leo and the Sun. His wealth will be abundant in his middle age; he will own land and real estate. He loves agriculture and will derive benefit from it—and God knows best. **The House** of his brothers, sisters, travels, and movements is Virgo and Mercury. He will be moderate in his movements but lack luck regarding his brothers and sisters. He will suffer harm from them and may experience hardship because of them—and God knows best. **The House** of his fathers and properties is Libra and Venus. He will bury his father before his mother. If he inherits anything from them, it will not remain with him; he will spend his money on those who neither praise nor thank him—and God knows best.

**The House** of his offspring and children is Scorpio and Mars. He will have many daughters. He will be granted a son by a servant girl, but he will lose one of his children, and one child will be born prematurely—and God knows best. **The House** of his illnesses and anxieties is Sagittarius and Jupiter. He will complain of pain in his back and kidneys, and there is a fear for him regarding this. He should take care of himself with medicinal drinks in every season to remain safe from pain and suffering—and God knows best. **The House** of his women and partnerships is Capricorn and Saturn. He will marry four women and love the company of women. He will receive an inheritance from one of his wives, but it will not last. One of them may have previously been a servant girl. Partnership, acting as a guarantor, or providing security for others does not suit him; if he guarantees or provides security for anyone, he will lose money—and God knows best.

**The House** of his death is Aquarius and Saturn. The cause of his death will be chest pain at the age of twenty-five. If he survives that, he will live a long life. There is a fear for him of falling from a high place, though he will be safe from it—and God knows best. **The House** of his travels is Pisces and Jupiter. He will be a lover of travel. If he travels toward the Qibla <note>original: "al-Qibla," the direction of Mecca, or generally Southward from the perspective of many Middle Eastern writers.</note>, he will earn much wealth. Sea travel is more favorable for him than land travel—and God knows best. **The House** of his authority and livelihood is Aries and Mars. He will be bold toward those in power and will seek help from a person of great stature, from whom he will receive much good—and God knows best.

**The House** of his hope and happiness is Taurus and Venus. He will triumph in all he hopes for and aspires to. It is decreed for him that he will receive sustenance through a woman of great stature. There is a fear of a person with a specific trait in his eyes <note>original: "sulb 'uyunihi"; likely referring to a hardness of the eyes, perhaps cataracts or a piercing, malevolent gaze</note> who may cause him harm—and God knows best. **The House** of his enemies is Gemini and Mercury. He will have many enemies among his own family and relatives; he should be wary of them and not associate with them. There is a fear for him of drowning in the days of his youth—and God knows best.

The best of his days are Monday, Thursday, and Wednesday. The most favorable month is July <note>original: "Tammuz"</note>, and the best direction is the East. Regarding food, he should eat anything hot and moist. His clothing should be red and white. For bloodletting <term>bloodletting: a common medical practice of the time believed to balance the humors</term>, use the basilic vein <note>original: "al-basiliq"</note>. Among women and partners, those whose star is in Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces are best. When he enters before a judge or ruler, he should stand before him, and if he looks at him, let him imagine a female face <note>This refers to a folk-magical practice believed to soften the heart of a harsh authority figure.</note>. When he sleeps, he should place his head toward the south to be safe from the evil of the crawling things of the earth—and God knows best.

# The Second Face

The sage Abu Ma’shar <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD) was the most influential astrologer of the Islamic Golden Age, known in the West as Albumasar.</note> said: The person born under this face—which is the ascendant of the Prophet Joshua <note>original: "Yusha' al-Nabi"</note>, peace be upon him—will be of a glistening complexion, broad-chested and broad-browed, with thick lips and thick hair. His teeth will be uneven, and he will be dominated by the humor of phlegm <note>In medieval medicine, phlegm was associated with a cold and moist temperament.</note>. He will have a mark on his neck or a scar on his face; his lot includes a burn from fire. He is a man of tricks, cunning, and shrewdness; he seeks nothing without attaining it. He will be granted the pilgrimage to the Sacred House of God and a visit to the tomb of the Prophet, upon whom be the best prayers and peace. He will endure much fatigue, toiling with his body for his livelihood, and will save nothing of his earnings. He shall live a long life, though time will turn against him with harm and misfortune; he has no great luck from his own efforts. And God knows best.

**His Earnings:** Leo and the Sun. He will have little wealth in the early part of his life, but as he grows older, his wealth will increase. If anything leaves his hand, it shall not return to him except with great difficulty. And God knows best.

<margin>Under this face, the newborn will be white-complexioned with large eyes and a wide forehead. He is broad-chested with bristly hair and nails. He is heavy in movement and possesses little wealth. He does not fulfill his promises; neither his word nor his oath is to be accepted, and he has no religion. He is among the people of "Rayn" <note>A Quranic term referring to a "stain" or "rust" on the heart due to sin.</note>, a liar who feels no shame before God Almighty. There will be a black mark on his chest and a fixed incisor tooth. And God knows best. End.</margin>

**His Movements <note>Referring to siblings and social interactions</note>:** Virgo and Mercury. He will have little luck from his brothers and sisters; he is better to them than they are to him. He fulfills their needs and favors them over himself. And God knows best. **His Parents:** Libra and Venus. He will have good fortune from both his father and his well-being. He will be nursed by someone other than his mother. If he inherits anything from his grandfathers, it will not be sold by him, but the house in which he was born will fall into ruin, and he will move to another. And God knows best. **His Children:** Scorpio and Mars. Most of his children will be female. He will be granted a child from a concubine <note>original: "jariya"</note> and will attain goodness because of him. However, if Mars witnesses for him <note>An astrological term for a planetary aspect</note>, his firstborn child will die. And God knows best.

**His Illness:** Sagittarius and Jupiter. You should fear for him regarding phlegm and moisture. He should eat everything cold and moist <note>This likely refers to balancing his temperament</note>. He should cleanse himself by vomiting once or twice every week; then he will be safe from all phlegmatic ailments and their harm. And God knows best.

**His Marriage:** Capricorn and Saturn. He will marry three women and will receive nothing but good from them. Yet he has little luck with them; they consume his wealth and neither praise nor thank him. And God knows best. **His Death:** Aquarius and Saturn. You should fear for him from a year whose ascendant is Aquarius. His illness may involve his hands or similar parts, and the cause of his death will be pains in the stomach and chest. Let him avoid eating cold things. And God knows best.

**His Travels:** Pisces and Jupiter. He will travel much in foreign lands. If he travels toward the direction of the Qibla <note>South/Southwest from a Persian/Mesopotamian perspective, toward Mecca</note>, he will earn much wealth. And God knows best. **His Honor:** Aries and Mars. He will be stout-hearted and bold in disputes. He has an abundant share of luck, but a craft or trade is better for him than being in service to others. And God knows best. **His Needs:** Taurus and Venus. He will triumph in all that he hopes and wishes for. He should avoid those of servile origin. He will attain happiness through a man of great stature. And God knows best. **His End:** Gemini and Mercury. He will have enemies and envious people, but he will not care about them, and God will grant him victory over his foes. His best day is Monday, and the most auspicious is Wednesday. Success is through God.

# On the Aspect of Jupiter

The sage <unclear>Abu Ma'shar</unclear> <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD) was a famous Persian astrologer and astronomer in the Abbasid court</note> said: One born under this face will be white-complexioned with an aquiline nose. He may have a slight squint or intense luster in his eyes, a loud voice, and slender legs. If he is born at night, his voice will be harsh; if born by day, his voice will be soft. He is a great eater of food and will be known by two names. He has a mole on his penis, a handsome face, a light spirit, and good character. There will be a wound or a mark on his arm, and a scar on his leg or head. He is quick to forgive, speaks whatever is in his soul, fears no one, and is afraid of nothing. He can live amongst all people; eyes are drawn to him, and he may be subject to magic <note>Likely referring to the "Evil Eye" or charms</note>. It is feared that he might drown in his youth, and God knows best.

<term>His distress is Virgo</term> <note>original: "wa-tahassuhu al-sunbulah"</note> and Mercury: He obtains wealth from the nobility, but if any of his wealth leaves his hand, it does not return to him except with great difficulty, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his brothers, his circumstances, and his movements</term> are Libra and Venus: He will have little luck regarding brothers and will suffer some harm from them. If they discover a flaw in him, they will expose it; he will eventually distance himself from them, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his fathers and his properties</term> are Scorpio and Mars: He will be beloved by his parents and will inherit the house in which he was born, though he will build others. He will be the head of his household, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his joys, pleasures, and Jupiter</term>: He will have little luck with children and may perhaps be sterile. If he is granted a child, there is fear for the child in their youth, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his illnesses and pains</term> are Capricorn and Saturn: Most of his illnesses will stem from the gall <note>referring to the "bitter" humor</note> and the heart. Heat dominates his temperament. Drinking medicine in every season will suit him and bring him relief, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his wives and partner</term> are Aquarius <note>original: "al-Dali"</note> and Saturn: He will marry several women and will be frequent in intercourse, for he loves marriage. A woman will deceive him and consume his wealth. Neither acting as a guarantor for others nor entering into business partnerships will suit him, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his death, his passing, and his punishment</term> are Pisces and Jupiter: There is fear for him when the ascendant of the year is Pisces and Jupiter, specifically from diarrhea <note>original: "intilaq al-batn"</note> or a wound from iron. There is also fear of drowning in his youth or at sea, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his travels</term> are Aries and Mars: Traveling by water suits him, but traveling by land is safer for him than traveling by sea. He will gain benefit during his travels from a man of great stature, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his authority and work</term> are Taurus and Venus: If he associates with a ruler or a leader, let him be cautious. He should beware of those who have a background of servitude. The outcome of his affairs will be praiseworthy, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his hopes and happiness</term> are Gemini and Mercury: He seeks nothing except that he attains it. As he grows older, his blessings and prosperity increase. All friends and companions will desire his company; they will need him, but he will not need them. His soul speaks to him of reaching a high rank, and God knows best.

<term>The house of his enemies and adversaries</term> are Cancer and the Moon: He will have enemies and envious people, but he will not care about them, and God will grant him victory over them. Those closest to him will be his enemies. His best day is Sunday and his most unlucky is Monday. Of the months, August <note>original: "Ab"</note> suits him; of the directions, the East; of clothing, yellow and silk; of food, everything cold; of bloodletting, the basilic vein <note>original: "al-akhal"</note>; of fruits, watermelon; and of animals, the reddish-blonde horse <unclear>and mules</unclear>.

# On Mercury’s Aspect with the Sun and the Discourse Thereon

According to the sage Abu Ma’shar <note>Abu Ma’shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar</note>, one born under this aspect will have a pearl-colored complexion leaning toward blondness, with thin cheeks and a handsome beard tinged with yellow. He has a small head and small eyes, and is graceful in his movements. He will have a mark on one of his forearms and scars on his face. He loves writing and science <note>The term "ilm" here refers to both religious and natural sciences</note>, possesses a good character and pure chivalry, and enjoys adornment and fine, detailed crafts. He shall find favor with the great, the powerful, and the noble. He will be long-lived and accepted by people with abundant luck, yet he will endure much fatigue and hardship. There is a fear of drowning for him in his youth, but in his final years, his life will be better than its beginning. And God knows best.

**His House of Wealth:** Libra and Venus. He will be granted wealth from the earth and soil <note>likely referring to agriculture or real estate</note>. He moves from one craft to another. It is judged for him that he will receive wealth from a woman of high standing. And God knows best. <margin>Ascendant</margin> **His House of Siblings and Movements:** Scorpio and Mars. He lives under the care of his siblings, though he may become isolated from them and suffer fatigue because of them. And God knows best. **His House of Parents and Properties:** Sagittarius and Jupiter. He will have little luck from his parents and will lose one of them in his youth. He may inherit an inheritance that does not last. The house in which he was born will fall into ruin, and he will build another house for himself. And God knows best. **His House of Joys and Children:** Capricorn and Saturn. A child will be born to him in his old age, but he will find no rest through him. If his first child is female, she will survive, but he will experience anxiety and grief on account of his children. He will be granted a child by a concubine. And God knows best. **His House of Illnesses:** Aquarius and Saturn. There is fear for him regarding pains of the rectum and the colon. Medicinal drinks suit him in every season and bring him relief. And God knows best. **His House of Women and Marriage:** Pisces and Jupiter. He marries three women and will experience evil and litigation with one of them. He will marry a foreign woman and die while with her, finding goodness and blessing through her. And God knows best. **His House of Fear and Death:** Aries and Mars. An injury from iron <note>likely a blade or tool</note>. There is fear for him regarding heart pain. He faces a critical period <term>qata'</term> <note>an astrological "cutting" or dangerous transition period</note> at ten years and at forty years; if he survives, he will live a long life. And God knows best. **His House of Travels and Relocation:** Taurus and Venus. He travels to a distant land and returns, gaining much wealth during his journey from a woman of high standing. There is fear that companions on the road may deceive or harm him. And God knows best. **His House of Hopes and Expectations:** Gemini and Mercury. There is fear of a ruler harming him, and his hopes may fail once. His origin is of service <note>original: "ubudiyya," implying a background of bondage or humble service</note>, and serving rulers does not suit him; practicing a craft is better for him. And God knows best. The Moon reveals some of what he desires. He will be a lover of friends, a keeper of secrets, and happy during the months because of his companions. And God knows best. **His House of Enemies and Envious Ones:** Leo and the Sun. People from his own family will be hostile toward him. There is fear of a ruler, and he possesses neither influence nor prestige. However, he will find goodness on his days: Wednesday, Thursday, and Sunday. The month that suits him is September, and the season is Autumn. Among women and partners, those whose star is Capricorn or Taurus suit him, as does anyone with a hot and moist temperament. Of rings, gold suits him. When he looks at the new crescent moon, let him look upon the face of a female. When he enters before a ruler, let him stand to his left, and when he sleeps, let him turn his face toward the West. <unclear>The last of his earthly structures</unclear>. And God knows best.

# Discourse on the Second Face of Venus

**The Sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar</note> said:** One born under this face will be white-complexioned, with a handsome face, almond-shaped eyes, medium stature, a rounded head, and black hair. He loves amusement, music, idleness, and pleasure. In the beginning of his life, there will be a mark on his chest and a mole on one of his sides. There will be a scar on his head from his childhood. The end of his life will be better than the beginning, for he is envied and burdens himself beyond his capacity. He is of good character, pleasant company, and a possessor of trustworthiness and chivalry <term>muru’ah: a traditional code of virtue and manliness</term>. He is neither spiteful nor envious. He lives in luxury and dresses well outside of his homeland. A skin blemish <note>original: "wadah"</note> appears on him at twenty years of age, and again at thirty; if he survives, he will live to eighty years. And God knows best.

**His House of Wealth and Residence:** Libra and Venus. In the beginning of his life, he will exert great effort and diligence in acquiring money. He will obtain something, but it will not stay with him; his sustenance will be consumed by those who neither praise nor thank him. And God knows best.

**His House of Brothers, Sisters, Travels, and Movements:** Scorpio and Mars. He will have little luck regarding his siblings. The West is better for him than the East. His movements are good in the beginning of his life, but his movements at the end of his life will bring fatigue and misery, and he will gain nothing from them. And God knows best.

**His House of Fathers and Mothers:** Sagittarius and Jupiter. He will be fortunate through his parents and receive goodness from them. He will be most dutiful toward his parents, and they will see goodness and blessing through him. He will receive an inheritance from them and will not die until he has buried them both. And God knows best.

**His House of Joys and Children:** Capricorn and Saturn. He will have many children; he will be granted four sons and five daughters. Some will die and some will live. He will receive sustenance through some of his children, but will suffer fatigue from the youth of the boys. And God knows best.

**His House of Illnesses and Pains:** Aquarius <note>original: "al-Dali"</note> and Saturn. Most of his illnesses will stem from coldness and moisture. In the beginning of his life, an internal disease is feared for him, but he will be saved from it by the mercy of God. And God knows best.

**His House of Women and Partners:** Pisces and Jupiter. There will be three women in his horoscope, or it is said five. Their origin is from his own roots <note>meaning his own social class or land</note>. It is decreed for him that he will inherit from one of his wives, but nothing stays with him. And God knows best.

**His House of Death and Ill Fortune:** Aries and Mars. Danger is feared for him in the years ruled by Aries and Mars, coming from the East. He will be affected by an iron instrument <note>a blade or tool</note> for a period of two months, or a great fright in his body, or the presence of a judge, but he will be saved from that. And God knows best.

**His House of Travels and Supplication:** Taurus and Venus. He will be a lover of travel. His best travels are toward the West. From his youth, a great difficulty is feared for him during travel, but God will deliver him from it. And God knows best.

**His House of Authority and Work:** Gemini and Mercury. His livelihood will be better from the labor of his own hand; if he serves others, he will tire and face harm. Trade suits him and is better for him than anything else. And God knows best.

**His House of Hopes and Friends:** Cancer and the Moon. Everything he hopes for will manifest. He will have many friends, and any friend he befriends will benefit him, except that his friendship may turn into enmity. God will grant him victory over those who are hostile to him. And God knows best.

**His House of Enemies and Envious Ones:** Leo and the Sun. An enemy is feared for him who is among his subordinates in service.

# The Third Face of Mercury

<margin>
**The Sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said:** One born under this face will be brown-complexioned, of good character, and sweet of speech. He is a lover of literature, science, and poetry; a writer, an accountant, and a skilled engineer. He is intelligent and discerning. On one of his thighs or legs, there is a mark; there is also a mark on his upper arm, and on his foot, the scar of a dog bite. In his early life, he survives a danger from water and a wound from iron. He will find good fortune with the great and the noble, and ultimately live in grace and happiness. In his youth, he will be envied for his circumstances; people will need him, yet he will not need them. He is never treacherous to his friend, being a person of chivalry and refinement. However, there are fears for him at the age of twenty and at forty; if he survives these, he will live for ninety-eight years. And God knows best.
</margin>

One born under this face will be brown-complexioned, of good character, and sweet of speech. He is a lover of literature, science, and poetry; a writer, an accountant, and a skilled engineer. He is intelligent and discerning. On one of his thighs or legs, there is a mark; there is also a mark on his upper arm, and on his foot, the scar of a dog bite. In his early life, he survives a danger from water and a wound from iron. He will find good fortune with the great and the noble, and ultimately live in grace and happiness. In his youth, he will be envied for his circumstances; people will need him, yet he will not need them. He is never treacherous to his friend, being a person of chivalry and refinement. However, there are fears for him at the age of twenty and at forty; if he survives these, he will live for ninety-eight years. And God knows best. <term>The House of Wealth and Earnings</term> <note>the 2nd astrological house</note> is Libra and Venus; he will be granted a good provision in his fifty-first year. He will give counsel and advice to his people, though he may not manage his own affairs well. And God knows best. <term>The House of Brothers, Sisters</term>, travel, and movement is Scorpio and Mars; he will have siblings but will not gain any benefit from them. He will move away from them early in life. In his sixty-fourth year, he can expect good provision from a deserted place, following a move there, and he will gain strength <unclear>through that</unclear>. And God knows best. <term>The House of Fathers and Mothers</term> <note>the 4th house</note> is Sagittarius and Jupiter; he will be a blessing to his family. He will receive an inheritance from them. He will be separated from his parents for a long time against his will, but will eventually return and be reunited with them. And God knows best. <term>The House of Joys and Children</term> <note>the 5th house</note> is Capricorn and Saturn; he can expect five daughters and three sons. He will be blessed with a righteous son through whom he will gain honor and high standing. He will love this child dearly and see goodness and blessing through him. And God knows best. <term>The House of Illnesses</term> <note>the 6th house</note> is Aquarius <note>original: "al-Dali," meaning the Bucket</note> and Saturn; his illnesses will stem from coldness, moisture, and phlegm. In his early life, he will suffer an illness so severe it brings him to the brink of death, but he will survive. Let him avoid eating cold foods. And God knows best. <term>The House of Wives and Partners</term> <note>the 7th house</note> is Pisces and Jupiter; he will have good fortune with women. The best of them for him will be one of humble or foreign origin <note>original: "origin of servitude"</note> or one who speaks a language other than Arabic. He can expect provision through her in his sixty-eighth year. And God knows best. <term>The House of Fear and Death</term> <note>the 8th house</note> is Aries and Mars; there is fear for him when the year ruled by Mars begins. The enemies who gossip about him to cause him harm will perish. And God knows best. <term>The House of Travels and Enemies</term> <note>here combining elements of the 9th and 12th houses</note> is Taurus and Venus; his travels will be toward the West. Land travel is better for him than sea travel. He can expect good provision in his thirty-eighth year, either alone or with a partner. And God knows best. <term>The House of Honor and Authority</term> <note>the 10th house</note> is Gemini and Mercury; serving the authorities suits him. He will attain high status and position at age forty-two. He should not serve anyone other than a "man of the pen" <note>an intellectual, scholar, or high-ranking scribe</note>, or he will grow weary. And God knows best. <term>The House of Hope and Friends</term> <note>the 11th house</note> is Cancer and the Moon; he will have great hopes and will achieve all that he aspires to. He has many friends, but should fear a false friend who might turn against him with enmity. Let him be cautious of everyone, even his own brother. And God knows best. <term>The House of Enemies and Envious Ones</term> <note>the 12th house</note> is Leo and the Sun; he will have many enemies and envious people, most of whom are from his own ancestors or predecessors.

# On the Zodiac Signs

<margin>
Regarding Jupiter: he is of good character... and shall hold a high rank among kings... he will be a deep thinker, possessing a mind that deliberates over matters... however, it is feared that he may suffer a fall from a high place...
</margin>

<margin>
From the book *The Lustrous Pearl on the Science of the Zodiac Signs and Crescents and the Twelve Signs* <note>original: "al-Durra al-Mudiyya fi 'Ilm al-Buruj wa al-Ahilla..."—a likely reference to a medieval astrological manual</note>... and God knows best what is right, and to Him is the return and the final home.
</margin>

**Jupiter in the sign of Aries:** The person born under this aspect will have an oily complexion, a long nose, be lean of flesh, and have long legs. He will have a blemish on his back or his head and a mark on his flank. He is deep-thinking, contemplative, well-spoken, and gains profit by boldly tackling matters. He loves the military and armies, and he will surpass his peers in his later years as his heart’s courage increases. He will be long-lived and live well, though time will turn against him and he will face a great hardship in the middle of his life, from which he will escape. Afterward, he shall rise above his peers. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Taurus:** And Mars <note>The mention of Mars here likely refers to its influence as a companion or opposing planet in this specific natal chart</note>. He shall have good fortune in trade and will obtain a livelihood from the ranks of soldiers and princes, particularly in the early part of his life. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Gemini:** If it is in Sagittarius and Jupiter <note>This implies a specific planetary relationship or "aspect" between Gemini and its opposite sign, Sagittarius</note>, he will have little luck with his brothers. Perhaps a brother will come to him from a different mother <note>i.e., a half-brother</note> and cause him some harm. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Cancer:** For Capricorn and Saturn in this house where he was born <note>referring to the astrological "House" or position</note>, he shall return from a land other than his own and will be granted wealth from his father, which he will spend. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Leo:** And the birth of Aquarius and Saturn. A child will be born to him in his youth, but he should fear for the child regarding smallpox and measles. If the child is female, she will not live long. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Virgo:** Pisces and Jupiter. He will suffer many pains caused by "coldness" <note>In medieval medicine, "cold" was one of the four humors/states that caused illness</note>. His treatment is phlebotomy <note>term: bloodletting—a common historical medical practice of draining blood to balance the humors</note> and medicinal drinks in every season. He will experience ailments in his head. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Libra:** Aries and Mars. He will marry three and a half women <note>original: "thalath niswa wa nisf"—the "half" often refers to a concubine or a woman of lower legal status than a wife</note> and will be inclined toward virgins. People will gossip about him because of his worries. Partnerships do not suit him; solitude is better for him than anything else. We judge for him that he will be joined with a woman who speaks a tongue other than Arabic, and he shall find great benefit and goodness through her. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Scorpio:** Taurus and Venus. He will face death twice and should fear a pain in his side at eight years of age. If he survives that, he will live a long life. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Sagittarius:** Mercury. While seen, he will inherit for a year. In his youth, he will not frequent people of religion, but he will be granted the pilgrimage <note>The Hajj to Mecca</note> to the Sacred House of God and the visiting of the Prophet Muhammad—upon him be the best of prayers and peace—at the end of his life. This is a good thing. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Capricorn:** Cancer and the Moon. His word will be listened to by the elders/great men, and he will possess various sciences without any defect in his mind. He will be saved from rare trials, and charity is better for him than anything else. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Aquarius:** Leo and the Sun. He will have many hopes and aspirations, but he will only achieve them through great hardship. He is a lover of friends and companions. And God knows best.

**Jupiter in the sign of Pisces:** And its animals are Virgo and Mercury. One under the status of a servant will show him enmity. Everyone who practices writing and accounting will rise in status, though he will not receive from them what is rightfully his. God will grant him victory over every enemy because of the strength of his rising sign. His best day is Friday, and specifically late Saturday. The months that suit him include October <note>original: "Tishrin al-Awwal"</note>; of the directions, the West; of the spirits, the East; and of the natures, animals and "pearls" <note>likely referring to gemstones/minerals associated with his nature</note>. The foods that suit him are hot and moist. Of the medicines: fumitory <note>original: "shahtaraj"—a medicinal herb</note>, anise, and *bashliq* <note>original: "al-bashliq"—likely a reference to a medicinal preparation or a variant of "basilicum" (basil)</note>. And God knows best.

# The Second Discourse on the Aspect of Saturn

<margin>If the influence was from Saturn, or it surged so that harm might reach him from it—and God knows best—it is better to gather his affairs and direct them toward kindness. His best month is October <note>original: "Tishrin al-Awwal"</note>. He might find grief through the death of his father in a foreign land. And God knows what is right; to Him is the return and the final home.</margin>
<margin>It is said he will be dominant in marriage. Among useful medicines and clothing, he should not be hasty. Among gems, green is best; among rings, crystal; and among beasts, the piebald. If he enters a valley, he should be cautious of his speech. As for the seekers of pleasure, some believe that if Saturn is in the sign of Virgo, he will face enemies.</margin>

The person born under this <term>Face</term> <note>A "Face" or decan is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, each ruled by a different planet</note>, which follows a daytime mention, has a <term>Bound</term> <note>The "Bounds" or "Terms" are specific degrees within a sign that belong to a particular planet</note> whose first four parts belong to Mercury and six to Jupiter. His appearance is that of a man with a handsome body, keen with hair <note>likely meaning he has thick or notable hair</note>, sweet and good in speech, often looking toward the ground, with small eyes and much hair. He is generous of soul, of a pleasant nature, noble in character, and a blessing to those who seek a blessing through him. He loves the master-craftsmen of known reputation, is a person of faith and honesty, and loves music and entertainment. 

The end of his life will be better for him than its beginning. He will have a mark or scar on his forehead, a mark on his thigh, and a mole on his shoulder. He will be brown-complexioned, merciful of heart, a distinguished believer, though sometimes having a troubled face. He is easy-going, quick to anger but quick to forgive. He will be granted the pilgrimage <note>The Hajj to Mecca</note> and attain much good. He will have a wound or mark on his head and a mole on his thigh. We fear for him regarding water and falling into it, and regarding iron <note>meaning weapons or sharp tools</note>. He will be proud of his child. In the middle of his life, he will face hardship, but he will find happiness at the end, reaching honor and a high station. And God knows best.

**His Wealth and Misfortune (Scorpio and Mars):** If Mars enters his house, his wealth may be ill-gotten or forbidden. Most of it will disappear. Being a guarantor for others or entering into partnerships will not suit him. He may preside over an inheritance, perhaps from one of his wives. And God knows best.

**His Brothers and Movements (Sagittarius and Jupiter):** He will have little luck with male siblings but loves his sisters. We fear for him regarding "the wind" <note>This likely refers to respiratory issues or "rheumatism," which were often attributed to "winds" in the body</note> if harm has already come to him from it. And God knows best.

**His Fathers and Grandfathers (Capricorn and Saturn):** He may be raised without his mother’s milk. He will bury his parents in his youth, and his mother may marry a man other than his father. The house in which he was born may fall into ruin. He will come to possess property and benefit from it. And God knows best.

**His Children and Concerns (Saturn):** He will have little luck with children, and we fear for them from "the followers" <note>Spiritual entities or "shadows" believed to afflict children in folk medicine</note>. If his first child is female, she may not thrive <note>original: "lam tu'ashir," possibly meaning she will not reach the age of ten or live long</note>. It is decreed that he will be granted a child from a handmaid, through whom he will see goodness and blessing. And God knows best.

**His Diseases and Ailments (Pisces and Jupiter):** He is prone to exhaustion and will be afflicted by pain stemming from heat and blood. His remedy is a drink of <term>Oxymel</term> <note>A medicinal syrup made of honey and vinegar</note>. We fear for him regarding phlegm and dampness in his old age. And God knows best.

**His Women and Wives (Aries and Mars):** He marries an older woman who may perform sorcery against him; let him beware for himself during "nights of idleness." He will have no luck with women in general, but he may marry a woman who speaks a non-Arabic language and find joy with her. And God knows best.

**His Dangers and Death (Taurus and Venus):** He will approach the brink of death two or three times. His passing will be caused by the pain of coldness and pain in the flank. We fear for him when the <term>Ascendant of the Year</term> <note>The sign rising on the horizon at the moment the year begins</note> is Taurus and Venus, for evil may reach him from princes or those of their ilk. And God knows best.

**His Travels and Movements (Gemini and Mercury):** Travel toward the West and the <term>Qibla</term> <note>The direction of prayer; here it likely signifies the South</note> suits him. The craft of parchment-making and writing will be favorable for him, bringing goodness and profit. And God knows best.

**His Power and Honor (Cancer and the Moon):** He will often be present before rulers and will attain some of what he hopes for. His soul will urge him toward a high rank. And God knows best.

**His Needs (Leo and the Sun):** He is a man of great hope and aspirations. He shall not die until he is granted happiness, prestige, and acceptance, obtaining what he hopes and prays for. He will receive a benefit from a "Grant of the Night of Power" <note>original: "Jirayat Laylat al-Qadr"—referring to a spiritual or material gift associated with the holiest night in Islam</note>. A boy will be born to him in his late fifties. And God knows best.

**His Enemies and Envious Ones (Virgo and Mercury):** We fear for him...

# Discourse on the First Face of Scorpio

<margin>
Mars (Bahram) is at the peak,
deserving of whose wrath?
</margin> <note>Bahram is the Persian name for Mars, the planet of war. This marginal note is a poetic fragment in Persian reflecting Mars's aggressive nature.</note>

<image-desc>
A large circular miniature set against an orange rectangular background. Inside the blue circle, a male figure dressed in chainmail armor and a helmet is depicted in a dynamic pose. He holds a raised sword in his right hand and grasps the tail of a large green scorpion with his left hand. Another green scorpion is positioned to his right. Below this main scene are three smaller rectangular panels:
1. Left: A seated woman in a red robe holding a small object.
2. Center: A seated figure with a sun-disk halo (representing the Sun).
3. Right: A seated man in a red and white garment playing a stringed instrument (lute/oud).
The entire composition is framed by decorative borders.
</image-desc>

<margin>
In this zodiac sign, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon each have a share of degrees, minutes, and seconds. Mars possesses full strength in this sign, Jupiter has its <term>exaltation</term> <note>original: "sharaf"; the highest point of a planet's influence</note> in this sign, the Moon has its <term>fall</term> <note>original: "hubut"; the point where a planet's influence is weakest</note> in this sign, and Venus has its <term>detriment</term> <note>original: "wabal"; a state of astrological disharmony</note> in this sign. Mars is the Lord of the House, Jupiter is the Lord of the <term>Triplicity</term> <note>original: "muthallatha"; a group of three signs of the same element</note>, Mars is the Lord of the <term>Term</term> <note>original: "hadd"; a specific subdivision of degrees</note>, and Mars is the Lord of the <term>Face</term> <note>original: "wajh"; a ten-degree subdivision</note>.
</margin>

This is the House of Mars. It consists of three <term>faces</term> and thirty <note>The OCR reads "twenty-three," but in standard astrology, each sign has thirty degrees</note> degrees. The first face belongs to Mars, the second to the Sun, and the third to Jupiter. Its nature is moist, watery, and <term>phlegmatic</term> <note>one of the four humors, associated with water and a calm or stoic temperament</note>. It is a feminine, nocturnal, and <term>fixed</term> sign, moderate in temperament, <unclear>cold</unclear> and dry, murky, and associated with <unclear>blood</unclear>, yet possessing beauty of form. Regarding the human body, it governs the male genitalia, the testicles, the bladder, the groin, and the <unclear>navel</unclear>. The first face belongs <unclear>to Mars</unclear>, the second to the Sun, the third to Jupiter, and the fifth to God—and God knows best.

# Discourse on Mars in the Ascendant

<margin>
The person born under this <term>face</term> <note>original: "wajh"; a decan, or ten-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> will be of fair or reddish complexion, with a freckled face, blue eyes, and joined eyebrows. He shall overcome all who wish him ill in his destiny, for he is like one who slays a lion. And God knows best.

# On the Third Ascendant, Under the Aspect of Venus

<margin>
It is related by the sage **Ptolemy** <note>original: "Batlamiyus"; Claudius Ptolemy was a 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian mathematician and astronomer whose works formed the basis of medieval astrology</note> that the person born under this ascendant will have a handsome and beautiful face, with pleasant speech. He will be refined, intelligent, and very fond of women. He will enjoy high status and a good position among kings. He will possess high ambition, being generous and magnanimous, with a love for fine food, drink, and luxurious clothing. However, he will have many enemies and envious people. He will generally be in good standing and remain safe from leprosy, vitiligo, and skin spots. And God knows best.
</margin>

<margin>
The sage **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>original: "Hirmis al-Haramisa," the "thrice-greatest" Hermes, a legendary figure to whom many ancient astrological and alchemical texts were attributed</note> said that the person born under this ascendant will be white-skinned with a pleasant face, black eyes, and joined eyebrows <note>a unibrow, which was often seen as a distinctive or beautiful feature in various historical periods</note>. He loves music, play, outings, joy, and pleasure. However, he is bold in his movements and does not consider the consequences of his actions, nor does he carry worries. He has a change of teeth <note>likely referring to dental health or a specific physical transition in youth</note> and is of good character. He will be long-lived and beloved by people. He loves the craft of iron and fire <note>referring to blacksmithing or perhaps alchemy and metalworking</note>. He has a mark on his leg or his head. He is not a betrayer of friends and will be granted happiness at the end of his life through a man of great stature; this occurs when he reaches forty years of age. And God knows best.
</margin>

The sage **Abu Ma'shar** said: The one born under this <term>face</term> <note>original: "wajh"; a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> will be white-skinned with a pleasant face and black eyes—it is also said he has joined eyebrows. He loves music, play, outings, joy, and pleasure, yet he is bold in his movements, does not consider consequences, and carries no worries. He has a change of teeth and is of good character. He will be long-lived and beloved by people. He loves the craft of iron and fire. He has a mark on his leg or his head and is not a betrayer of friends. He will be granted happiness at the end of his life through a man of great stature, specifically when he reaches forty years of age. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Wealth and Earning</term> <note>The 2nd House in astrology, governing finances</note> is associated with **Sagittarius** and **Jupiter**. He will be lazy in seeking money in the first part of his life, but perhaps he will be granted provision in his later days from a man of great stature. However, neither a dirham nor a dinar <note>silver and gold coins</note> will stay with him. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Siblings, Relatives, and Movements</term> <note>The 3rd House</note> is associated with **Capricorn** and **Saturn**. He will have siblings and will hold authority over them; he may part from them all and then return to them after a long time. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Fathers and Properties</term> <note>The 4th House</note> is associated with **Aquarius** <note>original: "al-Dali," a variant of "al-Dalw"</note> and **Saturn**. The house in which he was born will fall into ruin, but he will build another and will own property or real estate. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Children</term> <note>The 5th House</note> is associated with **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. If his first child is male, he should fear for him, but if it is female, she will be raised under his care for good and blessing. Most of his children will be male. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Illnesses and Thoughts</term> <note>The 6th House</note> is associated with **Aries** and **Mars**. He will be sickly in his youth but healthy in his old age. We fear for him regarding phlegm and moisture. Whatever suits him will bring him relief. One born under this ascendant will not be stung by a scorpion except that he will die, by the permission of God Almighty. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Women and Partners</term> <note>The 7th House, governing marriage and business partners</note> is associated with **Taurus** and **Venus**. His heart will love women to an extreme degree, and he will gain long life through one of them. He will marry several women in his lifetime and will leave his country because of a woman he falls in love with. He will stand before judges because of women. And God knows best. He has no luck in partnerships; if he enters a partnership, he will lose and suffer fatigue. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Fear, Death, and Calamities</term> <note>The 8th House</note> is associated with **Gemini** and **Mercury**. There is fear for him when the ascendant of the year is Gemini and Mercury; he may fall ill and suffer a relapse. Let him beware of a wind <note>likely referring to a "stroke" or respiratory ailment</note> that may strike him, or pain in the kidneys. He will be prone to many sores and boils, and we fear for him regarding nosebleeds. His death will be in a land other than his own. And God knows best. 

<term>His House of Travels and Estrangement</term> <note>The 9th House</note> is associated with **Cancer** and **the Moon**. He will be hasty in his travels and will travel much. One fears distress for him in some of his travels. The most auspicious <note>literally "coolest," implying comfort or success</note> of his travels will be toward the West and the <term>Qibla</term> <note>the direction of prayer, meaning South from the perspective of many Arabic manuscript origins</note>. And God knows best.

He will be prominent among rulers and ministers, succeeding from the beginning of his life to the end. He has a share of luck in the fire-related industries. And God knows best.
