# The Book of Observations on Mercury, Jupiter, and Mars in the Sign of Aries

<margin>
If Jupiter is in the house of the newborn under this ascendant <note>original: "tali‘"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> and this zodiac sign—which is an eastern, royal, bicorporeal <note>original: "dhu jasadayn"; literally "dual-bodied." While Aries is usually a cardinal sign, the text classifies it here as having two natures</note>, fiery, and diurnal sign—the person born under it will have a pearly complexion, a delicate brownish skin tone, a full stature, and will be slow to anger. They will possess elegance, grace, dignity, and knowledge. They love people of literature and virtue, are eloquent in speech, and have a pleasant character. They have a mole or beauty mark on their right cheek. However, the subject of this ascendant will rise in status in the early part of their life until they reach eighteen years of age; then their circumstances will decline until they reach thirty-two years. After that, their fortune will rise, their luck will appear, they will attain goodness, live happily, and engage in trade. They are inclined toward trade and shall not die except as a martyr <note>original: "shahid"; can mean a religious martyr or one who dies a noble or sudden death</note>. They will have a good life and speak what is in their heart, whether good or evil. And God knows best.
</margin>

The sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), known in Latin as Albumasar, was the most influential astrologer of the Islamic Golden Age</note> said: The person born under this ascendant and this zodiac sign—which is an eastern, royal, bicorporeal, fiery, and diurnal sign—will have a pearly complexion and a delicate brownish skin tone. They are of full stature, slow to anger, and possess elegance, grace, dignity, and knowledge. They love people of literature and virtue, are eloquent in speech, and have a pleasant character. They have a mole or beauty mark on their right cheek. However, the subject of this ascendant will rise in status in the early part of their life until they reach eighteen years of age; then their circumstances will decline until they reach thirty-two years. Then their fortune will rise, their luck will appear, they will attain goodness, live happily, and engage in trade. They are inclined toward trade and shall not die except as a martyr. They will have a good life and speak what is in their heart, whether good or evil. And God knows best. **Their house of wealth and gain** is Capricorn and Saturn; they will be a lover of trade, receive an inheritance, be blessed with money which they spend, and will manumit <note>set free</note> their slaves. They have great luck in the crafts, and their livelihood is continuous. And God knows best. **Their house of brothers, sisters, and kinsmen** is Aquarius and Saturn; they will have siblings and receive love from them. They will be brave among them, successful in their movements, generous to people, but stingy toward their own family. And God knows best. **Their house of fathers and mothers** is Pisces and Jupiter; they will find joy in their parents, who will live long lives. They will be separated from the mother before the father, and will inherit something but it will not remain with them. And God knows best. **Their house of joys and children** is Aries and Mars; if their first child is female, she will die, but if it is a male, they will find joy and happiness in him. Most of their children will be male. And God knows best. **Their house of illnesses and pains** is Taurus and Venus; there is fear for them regarding a sickness in their youth. Most of their illnesses will stem from heat and an excess of yellow bile <note>original: "safra"; one of the four humors of medieval medicine</note> and blood. They should tend to themselves with medicinal drinks in every season and avoid eating sweets, as this is better for them. There is also a fear of being struck by a stone, but if they survive that, they will live a long life. And God knows best. **Their house of women and their pleasures** is Gemini and Mercury; according to their ascendant, they will have three women, and eventually four—two virgins and a widow. And God knows best. **Their house of generosity and death** is Cancer and the Moon; the cause of their death will be a pain in the heart. There is a fear of drowning in their youth, and danger from thieves when the ascendant of the year is Cancer and the Moon. They should be cautious when venturing into <unclear>the wilderness</unclear> when they are twenty-four years old; if they survive that, they will live a long life. And God knows best. **Their house of travels and departure** is Leo and the Sun; they will be slow to travel and move. Their most fortunate travels will be toward the East and the North, where they will attain goodness and receive complete happiness from certain elders or a man of great stature. The more they avoid company, the better it will be for them, for they are envied by those who become their enemies. And God knows best.

# Discourse on the Second Face of the Moon's Sign <note>original: "al-wajh al-thani"; in astrology, a 'face' is a ten-degree segment of a zodiac sign. Since the Moon rules Cancer, this likely refers to the second decan of Cancer</note>

It is said that the subject of this ascendant <note>original: "tali‘"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, from the top of the head to the junction of the shoulders, will have hazel eyes <note>original: "shahli al-‘aynayn"; a specific color described as a mix of dark and light, often hazel or greyish-red</note>. Rukn al-Din the Sage <note>A traditional authority in medieval Islamic astrology</note> said: Such a person will be dutiful toward their parents, known for their righteousness and loyalty, and possesses sound judgment and management in all matters and things. </margin>

# The Thirty-Second Art: On General Principles

<margin>
If the ascendant <note>original: "tali‘"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is Gemini, and Mercury is in Libra and Venus is in Aries, the individual will have little luck with friends and loved ones. They may appear to be with him outwardly, but their inner feelings are contrary. God knows best. This concludes. His helpers and enviers are Scorpio and Mars; these will be his fiercest enemies and enviers, though in general, they may agree with him on certain traits. This is the end. God knows best what is right, and to Him is the return and final refuge. Finished.
</margin>

**The Sage Abu Ma'shar** <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), one of the most influential astrologers of the Islamic Golden Age</note> **said:** The person born under this "face" <note>original: "wajh"; a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> will be tawny in complexion with a handsome face and a well-proportioned stature. He will possess great dignity, and be a person of management, sound opinion, determination, gentleness, diplomacy, elegance, and wit. He loves people of knowledge, virtue, and literature, and is of good character. He will be saved from all hardships. He will have a long neck and a sharp gaze regarding everything he sees. He loves travel <note>original: "al-sayiba," likely meaning 'roaming' or 'travel' here</note>. His nature is marked by a mole <note>original: "shama"</note>, and it is feared that he may be bitten by a dog. He will have a mark on his thigh. He is a person of cunning, resourcefulness, and occasional pain, but he shall not die until he reaches a high rank. God knows best.

**His House of Wealth:** <note>The 2nd House in astrology, governing finances</note> Initially **Capricorn** and Saturn. He will have good fortune in trade. In the latter part of his life, he will associate with the elite and the leaders of the people, attaining much good. He is well-suited for plowing and agriculture. God knows best.

**His House of Siblings, Servants,** travel, and movement: Aquarius and Saturn. He has no luck regarding his siblings. There may be a scent of jasmine about him. It is feared that his siblings may harm him. He will be slow in his movements but diligent in attending to the needs of people. God knows best.

**His House of Fathers and Property:** <note>The 4th House</note> Pisces and Jupiter. He will be obedient to his parents and a blessing to them; they will see grace upon his face and live off his success for a long time. One of them may be buried <note>pass away</note> during his youth. He has good fortune in properties, and his livelihood will be found in urban development. God knows best.

**His House of Joys and Children:** <note>The 5th House</note> Aries and Mars. God will grant him male children. According to his ascendant, there are seven males and three females; a total of twelve children shall come from his loins. God knows best.

**His House of Illnesses:** <note>The 6th House</note> Though it be **Taurus and Venus**, he will generally be healthy. Most of his ailments will arise from phlegm <note>one of the four humors</note> and black bile. The most suitable drinks for him are those that are cold and moist. Of medicines, use black myrobalan <note>a fruit used in Ayurvedic and Unani medicine</note>, jujube, and turbith <note>a root used as a purgative</note>. All should be crushed and cooked until the volume is reduced by two-thirds, leaving one-third; this shall be his cure from sickness. God knows best.

**His House of Spouses and Partnership:** <note>The 7th House</note> Gemini and Mercury. He will be beloved by his wives. He will possess <note>marry</note> three women. Marriages will occur and then separations; after parting from the three, he will rule over a number of women. God knows best.

**His House of Death and Shoulders:** <note>The 8th House</note> Cancer and the Moon. It is feared he may drown or fall from a high place. If he survives these, he faces danger from "cold" diseases such as hemiplegia <note>original: "falij"; paralysis of one side of the body</note>, lethargy, and tremors when he reaches fifty-five years of age. God knows best.

**His House of Travels and Absences:** <note>The 9th House</note> Leo and the Sun. He will travel to many countries and set foot in places he never expected to see. It is feared that during his travels, he may be harmed by a companion. His most successful travels will be toward the East, which is better for him than any other direction. God knows best.

**His House of Authority and Work:** <note>The 10th House</note> Virgo and Mercury. Serving kings and the elite is suitable for him. He may experience a period of servitude or the hardship of service until Mercury descends into Virgo. God knows best.

**His House of Hope and Good Fortune:** <note>The 11th House</note> Libra and Venus. He will possess great wealth and attain a portion of it, yet he has little luck with friends and loved ones; they appear to be with him outwardly, but their inner feelings are contrary. God knows best.

**His House of Enemies and Enviers:** <note>The 12th House</note> Scorpio and Mars. These will be his fiercest enemies and enviers, though in general, they may agree with him on certain traits.

# The Second Face of the Decan Division
# Aries Upon Aries and the Second is the House of Death <note>original: "al-Mat." This is likely a phonetic spelling or a scribal variant of "al-Maut" (Death). In traditional astrology, the Eighth House is the House of Death, though the text here follows the First House (Aries) as the starting point for a physical description.</note>

The one born under this face <term>Face: A ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan.</term> and ascendant will have a reddish-fair complexion, a flat nose, thick lips, and a fierce spirit. He is quick to anger, reckless, and never settles in one place. He is daring in the face of terrors, and often begins a task or persists in folly before its completion. He is restless in all his affairs, strong-limbed, and hasty in his gait. He does not endure long in hardships. There is a fear for him regarding iron <note>likely referring to weapons or sharp tools</note>, though he shall be saved from it, or from a dog bite, from which he will also escape, and God knows best.

->**Aquarius and Saturn: Afflicted by Ailments**<-

He will not suffer long with them. Everything he buys in his own name will be cheap <note>meaning he will find good bargains or things will lose value</note>, and it is decreed for him that he shall see something of the treasures of the earth <note>a common trope in medieval astrology referring to finding buried wealth or hidden luck</note>. And God knows best.

->**Pisces and Jupiter: He will have brothers and sisters**<-

He will be the tallest among them and the highest-ranking leader over them; he does not inform them of what he is capable of doing. And God knows best.

->**Aries and Mars: He shall receive goodness from his parents and will not leave them**<-

In the House of Death <note>original: "bi-al-mat"</note>. He will be nursed on milk other than his mother's in his infancy. He shall receive an inheritance and come into possession of property or real estate. And God knows best.

->**Taurus and Venus: If his firstborn is a girl, she will be of blessed appearance**<-

A bringer of good fortune, and upon her head <note>meaning her presence</note> shall be good news and blessings. He shall be granted nine male children. And God knows best.

->**Gemini and Mercury: He shall be prone to many illnesses**<-

Regarding his pains, he has no patience for medical treatment. There is a fear for him from a disease that may strike him at twenty years of age and again at thirty years. If he survives these, he will live a long life. And God knows best.

->**Cancer and the Moon: He is granted love from his relatives, but he will leave the first one and...**<-

There is a fear for him regarding her through magic <note>original: "sihr" (sorcery/spells)</note>, and he shall be a man of many marriages to women. And God knows best.

->**Leo and the Sun: There is fear for him if...**<-

The "Lord of the Year" <note>the planet ruling the current year of his life</note> is in Leo and the Sun, concerning pains of the liver and spleen. He will be plagued by coughing, and there is fear for him of an injury to his hand or a fall from a high place. And God knows best.

->**Virgo and Mercury: He shall be a man of many travels and a high earner**<-

He will earn much money and travel to many lands, yet he will return to his family and his homeland. Be warned against traveling by water <note>literally "riding the water"</note>. He will be granted the Hajj <note>the pilgrimage to Mecca</note>. And God knows best.

->**Libra and Venus: He will be well-received by sultans, great men, and nobles**<-

He will be fortunate among them, and his life will encompass both the forbidden and the lawful <note>original: "al-haram wa-al-halal"</note>. He will move from one livelihood to another and from one profession to another. And God knows best.

->**Scorpio and Mars**<-

He is firm in his speech and will reach great honor in his old age. He is a man of great hope and aspirations; he asks for nothing except that he attains it. However, the silver coin <note>original: "dirham"</note> does not stay with him for long. And God knows best.

->**Sagittarius and Jupiter: There are many in his valley, but he does not go to them. There is a fear for him regarding "the Sultan's diseases" <note>likely referring to official troubles or stress-related illnesses from high-ranking service</note>, but he will then find relief.**<-

His best day is Saturday and the last of them is Sunday. His finest month is January <note>original: "Kanun al-Akhar"</note>. The most suitable foods for him are bird meat and fresh fruits.

# Discourse on the Third Perspective of Observation

<margin>If the rising sign <note>The "rising sign" or ascendant is the zodiac sign that was ascending on the eastern horizon at the specific time of a person's birth.</note> is Aries, the person will be fair-skinned with a handsome face, though a yellowish or reddish tint may appear on their countenance. There will be a mark or a trace of smallpox or something similar in one of their eyes, and a mark or a black mole on their chest. They are of good character and enjoy a pleasant life, yet they do not keep their promises, and their speech hides deep deceit in their heart. They shall hold no position of authority. And God knows best what is hidden and is most wise in what is correct.</margin>

<margin>If the rising sign is Taurus, the person will be fair-skinned with a handsome face, though a yellowish or reddish tint may appear on their countenance. There will be a mark or a trace of smallpox or something similar in one of their eyes, and a mark or a black mole on their chest. They are of good character and enjoy a pleasant life, yet they do not keep their promises, and their speech hides deep deceit in their heart. They shall hold no position of authority. And God knows best what is hidden and is most wise in what is correct.</margin>

The wise sage Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "Abu Ma'shar" — Referring to Ja'far ibn Muhammad Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), one of the most influential astrologers of the Islamic Golden Age.</note> said: One born under this "face" <note>A "face" or decan is a subdivision of a zodiac sign, spanning ten degrees.</note> will have a radiant, pearl-like complexion and a handsome face. They are quick to be pleased and quick to anger, indifferent to whether their actions are good or evil. Their circumstances are never stable; they are wealthy at times and poor at others. They shall be provided for in their old age, attaining leadership and a high rank toward the end of their life. They will be bold and courageous. There is a fear for them at thirty years of age from pain, and at forty years from a fall from a high place or into a pit or well—this is a critical period for them, so let them be cautious. If they reach eighty years, God knows best, for one does not know the measure of time and the world until it is gone. They will lose their inheritance, but if anything leaves their hand, it shall return to them; let them praise God for that. God knows their intentions.

Regarding their <term>Brothers</term> <note>original: "Ikhwanuhu" — In astrology, the "House of Brothers" (the 3rd house) governs siblings and short journeys.</note> and their movements under Aries and Mars: they will have few male siblings, and if they do have brothers, they will find little luck through them. The siblings will need the individual, but the individual will not need them. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Ancestors</term> <note>original: "Bayt Aba'ihi" — The 4th house, governing parents, home, and heritage.</note> under Taurus and Venus: the individual will be a blessing to their parents, who will see goodness, grace, and happiness through them. They will lose their mother before their father. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Children</term> <note>original: "Bayt Awladuhu" — The 5th house, governing offspring and creativity.</note> under Gemini and Mercury: they will have little luck with children. Their children will not be dutiful, nor will they obey their commands or follow the group. When the individual rejoices in something, their joy will not last. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Illnesses and Afflictions</term> <note>original: "Bayt Amradihi wa Awfaqihi" — The 6th house, governing health and service.</note> under Cancer and the Moon: most of their illnesses will stem from "cold winds" <note>This refers to the medieval medical theory of humors, where "wind" or "vapors" caused various ailments.</note>, dampness, phlegm, and a moist temperament. They will suffer from pain in their legs and their sides. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Spouses</term> <note>original: "Bayt Nisa'ihi" — The 7th house, governing marriage and partnerships.</note> under Leo and the Sun: they will marry a woman of noble lineage and status, finding happiness through her. She will die while with him, and then he will marry another. He will be a lover of women and will inherit from one of his wives. However, partners and financial guarantees will not suit him; if he enters a partnership, he will regret it and suffer loss. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Fear and Death</term> <note>original: "Bayt Khawfihi wa Mawtihi" — The 8th house, governing mortality and shared resources.</note> under Virgo and Mercury: there is fear for him when Virgo and Mercury are the "ascendants of the year" <note>A technique in mundane astrology where the chart of the year's beginning is analyzed.</note> due to severe exhaustion and significant losses. The cause of his death will be a pain of the heart in his stomach—or so it is said, if God wills.

Regarding the <term>House of Travel and Pursuits</term> <note>original: "Bayt Safarihi wa Qiyamihi" — The 9th house, governing long journeys and religion.</note> under Libra and Venus: he will love travel and moving from place to place. Land travel will suit him well toward Yemen, and his best travels will be toward the West or toward the "Qibla" <note>The direction of prayer; here likely meaning South or Southwest relative to the author's location.</note> from the East. God knows best.

Regarding the <term>House of Honor and Authority</term> <note>original: "Bayt 'Izzahu wa Sultanuhi" — The 10th house, governing career and public standing.</note> under Scorpio and Mars: there is fear for him regarding friendships with soldiers. Lies might be told about him to certain rulers, resulting in harm.

Regarding the <term>House of Hope and Happiness</term> <note>original: "Bayt Raja'ihi wa Sa'adatihi" — The 11th house, governing friends and aspirations.</note> under Sagittarius and Jupiter: he will have many friendships and social circles, showing a beautiful character to people. There is fear for him from those closest to him on account of a woman. He shall not die until he attains all that he hopes for and seeks. And God knows best.

# The Aspect of Venus and the Judgments Thereon

<margin>The Sage said: Whoever is born under this aspect and rising sign will be fair-skinned with a ruddy complexion, possessing a handsome face, a fine stature, and almond-shaped eyes. He is great in his own estimation, neither envious nor spiteful, and he does not consult anyone in his affairs. He bears a mark <note>original: *athar*—can mean a scar, mole, or birthmark.</note> on his face or his chest, and on his beloved <note>original: *habibihi*—this likely refers to a mole on a loved one or, more likely in this medical context, is a scribal error for a body part like the groin or flank.</note>, and a mark upon his knee. And God knows best.</margin>

<margin>His **House of Siblings**, relocations, and movements is Aries and Mars. He has no luck with siblings or relatives; they take from him but do not give to him. They consume his resources and then disparage him. A stranger is better for him than a relative. And God knows best.</margin>

<margin>His **House of Fathers** <note>The Fourth House, governing ancestry, parents, and the home.</note> is Taurus and Venus. He will be little in obedience to his parents. Most of his ailments will stem from repletion <note>original: *imtila’*—a medieval medical term for an excess of bodily humors, often treated by bloodletting or fasting.</note>. And God knows best.</margin>

<margin>His **House of Travel** is Libra and Venus. He will travel often and will be granted sustenance in the house he arrives at. He will find goodness in his travels, and his best travels will be toward the West and the North. And God knows best.</margin>

<margin>His **House of Glory** <note>The Tenth House, governing career and public status.</note> is Scorpio and Mars. There is fear for him from serving kings, yet he shall escape prison. <margin>His **House of Hope** is Sagittarius and Jupiter. He shall attain what he hopes for and desires, and he will triumph in his aims. However, he has no luck with friends and companions. And God knows best.</margin>

# Discourse on the Second Face of Mercury

<margin>Among the Arabic months is Jumada al-Akhirah <note>The sixth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.</note>; it aligns with the eleventh [day] and the eleventh [sign] from Yemen. # Jupiter in the Sphere of Saturn among the Planets

<margin>
If the ascendant is Libra and Venus is in Scorpio, or if the ascendant is Scorpio and Venus is in Libra, or if the ascendant is Sagittarius and Jupiter is in Capricorn, or if the ascendant is Capricorn and Jupiter is in Sagittarius, or if the ascendant is Aquarius and Saturn is in Pisces, or if the ascendant is Pisces and Saturn is in Aquarius—these configurations are called "Affection, Intimacy, and Perfect Agreement." And God knows best what is right, and to Him is the return and the final home. It is finished.
</margin>

One born under this face <note>A "face" or "decan" is a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign used to refine astrological predictions.</note> with the gaze of Saturn will be brown-skinned, of moderate stature, with a handsome face and an agreeable voice. He loves the company of leaders and notables, and his fame regarding his wealth will spread far and wide. He will learn a craft different from that of his family and will be far-sighted. He will have a distinguishing mark on his face and will live a good life. However, there is fear for him at twenty and thirty years of age, as he will be prone to many illnesses. If he survives these "cuttings" <note>original: *qutu'at*; an astrological term for life-threatening periods or planetary crises.</note>, he will live a long life. It is written in his destiny to perform the Hajj to the Sacred House of God <note>The pilgrimage to Mecca.</note>. And God knows best.

**Aries and Mars:** He will be granted wealth from sources he does not expect, and perhaps he will receive wealth from the authority <note>original: *al-sultan*</note>. The end of his life will be better than its beginning. And God knows best. **The House of his Siblings,** his residence, his relocations, and his movements: **Taurus and Venus:** He will lack luck regarding male siblings, but females will be a source of good for him. He may move from the house where he was born to another. And God knows best.

**Gemini and Mercury:** He will have good fortune from his father, obtaining benefit from them and inheriting property or real estate. He will bury his father before his mother; however, if Jupiter is in a weak state, he will bury the mother before the father. And God knows best.

**Cancer and the Moon:** Most of his children will be daughters. If his first child is a boy, he will be separated from him and follow after him. It is said he will be granted a son who is an ascetic <note>A religious hermit or person of extreme self-discipline.</note>, and he will live by his blessing. [Unclear] received a high and lofty rank. And God knows best. **The House of his Illnesses and Ailments:** **Leo and the Sun:** He will suffer much from pains caused by phlegm, congestion <note>original: *al-sharq*</note>, dampness, yellow bile <term>Yellow bile and phlegm were two of the "four humors" in medieval medicine believed to control health.</term>, and headaches and backaches. He should treat himself with acidic syrups and digestive electuaries <term>Jawarishnat: medicinal pastes or preserves, often used to aid digestion in Galenic medicine.</term>. Cold and soft foods will bring him benefit and relief. And God knows best.

**The House of his Partners, Virgo and Mercury:** The first woman he marries will be from his own family. He will marry "two and a half" women <note>This likely refers to two marriages and a lesser union or a concubine.</note>. If he exceeds them, he will rule over other women. He has little luck in partnerships and financial guarantees, as he tends to lose money in them. And God knows best. **The House of his Death, Libra and Venus:** There is concern for him regarding back pain. He should fear a physical affliction at eleven years of age. If he survives that, he will live a long life. And God knows best.

**The House of his Travels, Scorpio and Mars:** He will be a lover of travel and physical exercise. Travel and staying in different places are beneficial for him. His best travels are toward the West and the direction of the Qibla <note>The direction of prayer, which varies by location but often signifies the South or Southwest in this context.</note>. And God knows best. **The House of his Glory and Authority:** He will be truthful of tongue and accepted by the elite. He loves honesty and trustworthiness and hates betrayal and treachery. He will be fair in his dealings, fulfilling his duties and speaking the truth even if it is against himself. And God knows best. **The House of his Hopes and Aspirations, Capricorn and Saturn:** He will be fortunate in all his affairs and achieve his hopes through patience and deliberation. He will be of benefit to those who accompany him. He should wear a ring made of iron. And God knows best.

# Discourse on the Second Face of Libra

<margin>Regarding Saturn <note>original: "Zuhal"</note>: He shall have partners in his work and a master, yet they cannot overpower him. God grants success through his hands for others. His lot includes imprisonment, and his family shall be scattered. His garments are of linen and cotton. His fortune lies in his right hand. He deals in the melting of gold and silver. Regarding women, friends, and partners: there is a risk of death, or trouble with authority. His signs are Scorpio, and his months are September, April, October, and November. He rules both night and day. God knows best his hidden faults. He should begin his needs and leave his house facing a woman; if he wipes his head toward the North upon leaving, all his affairs will be made easy. God knows best.</margin>

The Sage said: Whoever is born under this Face shall be fair-skinned with joined eyebrows, possessing a handsome face and good character. He is a lover of knowledge, virtue, refinement, and jurisprudence <term>Fiqh: Islamic legal scholarship</term>. He is eloquent of tongue, steadfast of heart, and naturally brave. He acts according to his own intellect, and no one truly knows his inner thoughts. There shall be a mark upon his head, and a sign or a mole upon his forearm, as well as upon his leg. He loves the company of people of letters and science. He shall attain a rank from a ruler <note>original: "Sultan"</note>, and his family shall benefit from his prestige. Everyone who sees him shall love him, and they will derive benefit and profit from him. God knows best.

**The House of Wealth and Earnings (Aries and Mars):** He gathers wealth and does not care from whence he collects it, nor does he worry about how it was earned. However, when it reaches his hand, he spends it unwisely and later regrets it. Forbidden <term>Haram</term> gains will not suit him. God knows best.

**The House of Siblings, Travels, and Movements (Taurus and Venus):** He shall be fortunate in his movements, though he is slow to act. If Saturn looks upon him <note>an astrological aspect</note>, he shall be the one who remains after his brothers have passed. God knows best.

**The House of Parents and Properties (Gemini and Mercury):** He shall be a blessing to his parents, and they shall see goodness and grace in his face. He shall bury his father before his mother. He may receive an inheritance from them, but it will not last with him. He may be nursed by someone other than his mother. God knows best.

**The House of Joys and Children (Cancer and the Moon):** He shall be granted children and find happiness through them. If Jupiter looks upon him, the majority of his children will be male. A righteous son will be born to him, from whom he will see great benefit. God knows best.

**The House of Illnesses and Pains (Leo and the Sun):** Most of his ailments will stem from coldness, phlegm, and dampness. He will fall ill in the middle of his life, but if he passes that stage, he will live a long life. God knows best.

**The House of Women and Partners (Virgo and Mercury):** He shall marry three women. If he leaves the first, he shall rule over several others, and he shall have authority over a maidservant. God knows best.

**The House of Fear and Death (Libra and Venus):** Fear is held for him regarding a fall from a high place, fire, or drowning. He may be struck by a stone or wounded by an iron tool. God knows best.

**The House of Travel and Absence (Scorpio and Mars):** Travel by water suits him, though he is slow in his journeying. His best travels are toward the North, where he shall find goodness and great benefit. God knows best.

**The House of Rank and Work (Sagittarius and Jupiter):** Working for the authorities and seeking proximity to them suits him. If he is among the learned, the things he produces will be needed by kings, and he shall gain profit thereby. God knows best.

**The House of Friends and Hopes (Capricorn and Saturn):** He shall have little luck with friends, partnerships, or guarantees. However, he may receive happiness from an elderly, truthful friend. He will achieve his hopes and desires through patience and deliberation. God knows best.

**The House of Enemies and Envious Ones (Aquarius):**

<margin>
The one born under this Face is fair-skinned with joined eyebrows, handsome of face, and of good character. He loves knowledge, virtue, refinement, and jurisprudence. He is eloquent, brave, and follows his own mind. No one knows his secrets. He has a mark on his head and a mole on his arm and leg. He enjoys the company of the learned and attains high rank. God knows best.
</margin>

# The Third Face: The Aspect of Mars

<margin>The Sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD) was one of the most influential astrologers of the Islamic Golden Age.</note> said: Whoever is born under this Third Face—which belongs to a "double-bodied" sign <term>Mutable sign: signs that represent the transition between seasons; here referring to Pisces</term>, the House of Jupiter <note>original: "al-Mushtari"</note>, the Exaltation of Venus <note>original: "al-Zuhara"</note>, and the Fall of Mercury <note>original: "Utarid"</note>—shall be reddish-brown in complexion <note>original: "durdi," literally the color of dregs or sediment</note> with a hint of yellow or blonde. He is blessed in his youth. Upon his head and temple, there is a mark, and a scar or similar trace will be found on his lip. It is feared that he may suffer from a dog bite, a wound from iron, or a burn from fire, which will leave a lasting mark. He shall possess an air of authority in the eyes of others and have high ambitions. He will raise orphans from among his own family. He is fond of stories and poetry. He will suffer many ailments in his youth but will recover quickly. One should fear for him a fall or a wound in the thirty-sixth year of his life. God knows best.</margin>

**The House of Wealth:** Aries <note>original: "al-Hamal"</note> and Mars <note>original: "al-Marrikh"</note>. He will be prone to wasting his money. His best source of income is commerce, yet money does not stay with him because he squanders it on those who neither praise nor thank him. God knows best. **The House of Siblings:** Taurus <note>original: "al-Thawr"</note> and Venus. He shall be in a better state than his two brothers and more compassionate than they are. In his youth, he will be accused of a difficult crime, but he will eventually be cleared of it. God knows best.

**The House of Parents and Property:** Gemini <note>original: "al-Jawza"</note> and Mercury. His father will harbor dislike for him but will find himself in need of him in his old age. The father shall be buried before the mother. He will not inherit anything from them, and if he does inherit, it will not be blessed for him. God knows best. **The House of Children:** Cancer <note>original: "al-Saratan"</note> and the Moon <note>original: "al-Qamar"</note>. He will have few children in the early part of his life, but he will be granted them in his later years. <insert>24 15 4 5 7 1 8 3 15 7</insert> <note>These numbers likely represent horary calculations or protective numerology.</note> God knows best.

**The House of Illnesses:** Leo <note>original: "al-Asad"</note> and the Sun <note>original: "al-Shams"</note>. He will suffer many pains and diseases, especially if the Sun is in Pisces, stemming from excess heat, bitterness <note>likely referring to "yellow bile" in the humoral medical system</note>, and lack of sleep. To find relief from this, he should treat himself with medicinal drinks <note>original: "al-mashrub," likely herbal syrups or infusions</note>. God knows best. **The House of Marriage and Partnerships:** Virgo <note>original: "al-Sunbula"</note> and Mercury. He will marry two women who return to him <note>likely referring to remarriage or reconciliation</note>, and he will receive good sustenance through them. However, business partnerships and financial guarantees do not suit him. God knows best.

**The House of Death:** Libra <note>original: "al-Mizan"</note> and Venus. Danger is feared for him from a woman of <unclear>beautiful</unclear> eyes and the hardship she may cause. Every year when the ascendant is in Libra and Venus, he should avoid the company of women. For everyone who is pregnant <unclear>for that reason</unclear>, it is better for him [to keep distance]. God knows best.

**The House of Travel:** Scorpio <note>original: "al-Aqrab"</note> and Mars. He will travel frequently. He should be cautious in the early part of his life regarding his travels, as something may be taken from him, though it will later be compensated. His best travels are toward the North, where he will find goodness and profit. God knows best. **The House of Glory:** Sagittarius <note>original: "al-Qaws"</note> and Jupiter. He shall be fortunate in the presence of the elite and the great, attaining from them honor and great <unclear>prestige</unclear>. God knows best.

<margin>The treatise of Abu Ma'shar is completed by the hand of the one in need of God the Exalted, its owner... and light... <unclear>Husayn</unclear> son of <unclear>the Sheikh</unclear> on the thirteenth of the blessed month of Ramadan, in the year eight hundred <note>Approximately May 1398 AD</note>. Prayers and peace be upon the Master of Creation.</margin>

# Description of the Moon’s Descent into the Twenty-Eight <term>Lunar Mansions</term>
<note>The Lunar Mansions (Manāzil al-Qamar) are a system of 28 segments along the ecliptic, each representing the Moon's daily progress. They were used extensively in medieval Islamic astrology and magic for timing actions.</note>

<image-desc>A manuscript page featuring a grid of fourteen illustrations (seven rows in two main columns) depicting various figures, animals, and hybrid creatures associated with the lunar mansions. Each illustration is accompanied by a block of text in red and black ink. The figures include humanoids with multiple heads, seated figures, animals like lions and birds, and mythological hybrids like a fish-human or a winged creature.</image-desc>

# Discourse on the **Nightmare** and its Attendants
<note>original: "al-Kābūs wa-atbāʿihi". The word <term>Kabus</term> comes from the Arabic root meaning "to press" or "to squeeze," and was historically used to describe the phenomenon we now call sleep paralysis.</note>

<image-desc>
A full-page manuscript illustration depicting a **Nightmare** demon. In the center, a large, dark-skinned winged demon with horns is positioned upside down, hovering over a sleeping man. The demon wears green trousers and has its hand reaching toward the sleeper's chest—a literal representation of the "pressure" associated with the condition. The sleeping man lies on a patterned red and gold bed with a blue pillow. 

Surrounding the central figure are several smaller demonic or animalistic heads, representing the "attendants" or different manifestations of the nightmare: 
1. A grey, horned head at the top left breathing out vapor.
2. A donkey-like head with a bell around its neck on the right.
3. A blue-grey demonic face on the lower right.

The background is white, decorated with small floral sprigs, a ceramic vessel on a stand, and several <term>talismanic sigils</term> <note>These are "ring-letters" or "Charaktêres," magical symbols believed to hold power over the spirits depicted.</note> consisting of vertical lines topped with circles and hooked shapes. The entire scene is enclosed within a simple rectangular border.
</image-desc>

# **Discourse on the Description of the Seven Planets and the Twelve Zodiac Signs**
<note>original: "al-Qawl ʿala Sifat al-Kawakib al-Sabʿa wa-al-Buruj al-Ithnay ʿAshar". In the medieval Islamic tradition, the "Seven Planets" refer to the classical celestial bodies: the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The "Twelve Zodiac Signs" refer to the <term>Buruj</term>, the constellations that the sun appears to pass through during the year.</note>

<image-desc>
A detailed miniature painting set within an arched frame. 

At the top, a rectangular panel contains the title "Discourse on the Description of the Seven Planets and the Twelve Zodiac Signs" in black ink on a plain background. 

Below this, the main illustration is framed by an arch. The spandrels (the triangular corners outside the arch) are filled with a red floral <term>arabesque</term> pattern, a common decorative motif in Islamic art featuring intertwining vines. The arch itself is composed of a series of circular medallions. At the highest point (the apex) is a personified Sun with a human face, radiating light. To the left and right are medallions containing various animals, which likely represent specific constellations or planetary associations, including a snake, a bird, a rabbit, a dog-like creature, a horse, a duck, and a rooster.

Inside the arch, a bearded man wearing a brown hooded robe and green sleeves is seated on the ground in a field of small flowers. He is looking upwards toward a wooden book stand (<term>rahla</term>) that appears to be floating or positioned in the air, suggesting the elevated or divine nature of the knowledge he is studying. To his left, a censer emits plumes of smoke, perhaps indicating a ritualistic or meditative atmosphere. Various vessels, including a bowl and a cup, are placed on the ground around him, indicating a scholarly or ascetic life. 

The vertical borders of the frame are decorated with blue geometric patterns consisting of interlocking squares and floral motifs.
</image-desc>

<note>The scholar depicted here is likely an astronomer or astrologer. In this era, these two fields were not separate; studying the physical movement of the stars (astronomy) was essential for understanding their perceived spiritual and terrestrial influences (astrology).</note>

# Discourse on the Kindness shown to Daughters
<note>original: "al-Qawl ‘ala birr al-banat." The word <term>birr<note>A profound Arabic term for piety, devotion, and benevolent care. While often used for "filial piety" (duty to parents), here it describes the duty of a father to provide compassionate and righteous care for his daughters.</note></term> highlights the religious and moral obligation to value female children, often contrasting with pre-Islamic cultural preferences for sons.</note>

# An Account of the Lighthouse of Alexandria

<note>original: "Al-Qawl fi Manar Iskindariyya." The term "Manar" literally means a place of light or fire, from which the English word "minaret" is derived. This refers to the Great Pharos of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.</note>

<image-desc>A manuscript illustration depicting the Lighthouse of Alexandria (the Pharos) within a framed border. On the left is a tall, ornate pillar representing the lighthouse tower. It features a pinkish-red octagonal base with swirling patterns, a white central shaft decorated with a grid of red geometric square designs, and a blue flared capital with a tiered, petal-like motif. Above the capital is a red lattice railing, and at the summit sits a large, dark circular mirror or orb. A human face, wearing a white head covering, is visible behind the mirror. To the right of the tower stands a stylized dark green tree. Next to the tree is a building with a red exterior and four arches overlooking a blue interior area. A smaller square structure with red and white geometric patterns and a blue peaked roof sits atop the building. The background is white, adorned with small tufts of green grass and red flowers. The ground in the foreground is rendered as a field of black, wavy lines, likely representing the sea.</image-desc>

## The Illustration of Gog
## <unclear>and</unclear> <unclear>Magog</unclear>
<note>original: "Yajuj wa Majuj." In Islamic tradition, these are two chaotic tribes imprisoned behind a massive iron and copper wall built by Dhu al-Qarnayn (often associated with Alexander the Great). Their eventual escape is a sign of the approaching End of Days.</note>

<note>The following scene illustrates the legendary barrier and the perpetual struggle of these tribes to breach it.</note>

At the top of the scene, two sentinels on horseback stand guard atop a massive wall constructed of dark grey masonry. This instrument is used to signal a constant alarm, warning the world of the tribes' attempts to escape.</note> that stretches across the center of the frame. To the right, another rider in a reddish-purple coat plays a pair of <term>kettledrums</term> <note>original: "nakkara," small drums often mounted on horses for military or ceremonial music.</note>. They are set against a pale landscape dotted with delicate blue and red flowers.

Below the great arch of the barrier, the tribes of <term>Gog and Magog</term> are depicted as wild, dark-skinned humanoid figures. Shown in a state of frantic activity, they are almost entirely naked with unkempt hair. Some display protruding red tongues, a common artistic shorthand in medieval manuscripts for monstrous or uncivilized beings. The figures are seen desperately climbing the wall and standing on each other’s shoulders in an attempt to reach the top. 

In the bottom left corner, a winding red serpent or dragon head emerges, further emphasizing the supernatural and perilous nature of this location.

# Discourse on the Waqwaq Tree
<note>The Waqwaq tree is one of the most famous marvels in medieval Islamic folklore and geography, appearing in works like *The Wonders of Creation*. It was said to grow on a remote island (often identified with Madagascar or islands in the East Indies). The tree's most striking feature was its fruit, which resembled human beings or animal heads that would emit a "waq waq" sound upon ripening.</note>

[This page is dedicated to a full-page illustration of the tree.]

Most of the figures hang downward with their heads or upper bodies encased in the husks, while their legs and torsos are visible. One central figure is depicted standing upright, with a fruit pod positioned atop its head like a hat. To the far right, a figure appears to be falling or hanging by its feet. 

The ground beneath the tree is sparsely decorated with small green plants topped with red flowers. Two larger, triangular green shrubs flank the base of the trunk.

# The <unclear>Summer</unclear> Quarter

<image-desc>
A rectangular miniature painting illustrating the season of Summer. A young man wearing a light orange-red tunic, a green belt with a purple pouch, and a white turban is depicted on the right. He is in mid-stride, aiming a bow and arrow upwards towards birds in the trees. The landscape is an orchard or garden with several trees. One tree on the left is tall and dark green with red fruit (possibly pomegranates). Another central tree has reddish bark and sparse leaves with red fruit. A third tree on the right has lighter green leaves and red berries or fruit. In the bottom left corner, a rabbit or hare is shown leaping through the grass. Two blue birds are visible: one perched on the leftmost tree and another flying near the center. The sun's rays are visible in the top right corner.
</image-desc>

<margin>
The Sign of Cancer
The Sign of Leo
The Sign of Virgo <note>original: "al-Sunbula," literally "the Ear of Grain" or "the Spike," referring to the star Spica in the constellation Virgo.</note>
</margin>

The sun moves into the sign of Cancer. It is hot and dry, and its dominant humor is **yellow bile** <term>yellow bile: one of the four bodily humors in ancient medicine, associated with a fiery, choleric temperament</term>. It is a hot quarter of the year, and as it approaches autumn, it becomes dry. On the thirteenth of June <note>This refers to the Julian calendar, where the Summer Solstice traditionally fell around this date in various medieval traditions.</note>, the length of the day reaches its peak and the night its shortest.

In this season, the diet should consist of everything that is cold and moist. One should slightly decrease the amount of food eaten and increase the amount of drink; the drink should be heavily diluted with cold water and ice. One must also avoid the use of "hot and dry" medicines and any food of that same nature.

As for meat, one should eat black lambs. There is also no harm in eating beef or goat meat prepared with vinegar and celery. One should reduce the time spent staying in the **bathhouse** <note>original: "al-hammam," the traditional steam bath</note> and avoid the practice of induced vomiting.

These are the characteristics, the nature, the treatment, the food, and the drink of the season. Whoever follows what the physicians have mentioned shall be safe from the diseases of summer, and whoever contradicts what they have mentioned has done a wrong to themselves. God is the Healer, the Sufficient, and the Granter of health; He is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs. Praise be to God alone.

Autumn Season

Cold and Dry

<insert>
The physicians and verifying scholars said: "Indeed, it is a sign of a lack of understanding [to ignore] that this season..."

In this season is the moderation of the weather. It is cold and dry; as for its prevailing quality, its departure from Summer makes it cold, and its approach toward Winter makes it dry. On the fifteenth day of September <note>original: "Aylul," the Levantine name for September. In many medieval calendars, the Autumnal Equinox was marked around this time.</note>, the night and day are equal, just as their equality in the Spring. 

In these two seasons <note>referring to the transitional periods of Spring and Autumn</note>, the diet should consist of things moving from cold toward the slightly hot, and from the moist toward the dry, little by little. One should not increase food intake except by a small amount, and should decrease the amount of drink. During this time, one should consume hot and moist foods, eat <term>young chickens</term> <note>original: "al-farafij," referring to fledglings or young poultry which were considered easier to digest in humoral medicine</note>, and use hot and moist oils. 

One should avoid bloodletting except in cases of absolute necessity, and avoid frequenting the <term>bathhouse</term> <note>the hammam or steam bath</note> except once per week. One should also reduce sexual intercourse. 

Whoever follows what the physicians have prescribed will be safe from the diseases of Autumn, but whoever contradicts what they have mentioned has committed a wrong against himself. God is the Healer, the Sufficient, and the Granter of health; He is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs. Praise be to God alone, and may the peace and blessings of God be upon our master Muhammad and his family.

# Discourse on the Waxing and Waning of the Moon

As for the Moon’s reception of light from the Sun, the increase and decrease in its appearance occurs according to its distance from or proximity to it. This is because for any spherical body, the eye only perceives the half that faces the observer. Thus, the half of the lunar sphere facing the Sun is always illuminated, while the other half is always dark. When the half of the lunar sphere facing the Earth is the same half that faces

<image-desc>
A circular astronomical diagram showing the phases of the moon. The outer ring consists of 28 small circles representing the lunar mansions/days, each shaded to show the progression from a thin crescent to a full moon and back to a waning crescent. The center of the diagram contains a decorative golden sun-like floral motif. Radiating lines divide the circle into segments, each containing Arabic text describing the timing of the moon's rising and its illumination. The background of the diagram area is painted in a light blue wash.
</image-desc>

<note>The text within the diagram segments describes the lunar visibility and hours of light/darkness throughout the month.</note>

the Sun, we see the Moon full of light; this occurs at the midpoint of the lunar month <note>the Full Moon or 'Badr'</note>. However, when the half facing the Earth is different from the half facing the Sun, only a small portion of the sunlit half falls within our field of vision. As it moves further from the Sun after the moment of alignment <term>Conjunction: when the moon and sun are at the same celestial longitude</term>, the light increases until it stands in opposition to it. Then, it begins to decrease just as it had increased, until it vanishes at the end of the month. And God knows best.

<note>The following technical terms appear in the text: The Moon (al-Qamar), the waxing and waning of the moon (ziyadat al-qamar wa nuqsanuhu), the Sun (al-Shams), light (al-daw'), the illuminated half (al-nisf al-mudi'), the lunar month (al-shahr al-qamari), alignment/conjunction (al-muhadhah), and the crescent (hilal).</note>

# Discourse on the System of the Victor and the Vanquished

<image-desc>A miniature painting depicting a combat scene between two warriors. On the left, a fallen soldier in a red and gold tunic is being struck by a standing warrior. The standing warrior wears a chainmail shirt, a pointed helmet, and carries a circular shield with a radiating sunburst pattern. To the right, a caparisoned horse stands facing the scene. The background features stylized floral sprigs and grass.</image-desc>

<margin>Regarding even and odd numbers: in terms of their minimum and maximum values during a confrontation, the Victor overcomes the Subject <note>original: "al-Matlub," referring to the person being sought or the defendant</note> if the numbers are equal. However, when the odd numbers are equal, the Seeker <note>original: "al-Talib," the one initiating the action or the plaintiff</note> overcomes.</margin>

<image-desc>A large rectangular diagram containing diagonal rows of Arabic numerals written in words (e.g., one, two, three, five, seven, eight, nine) interspersed with patterns of dots. Some text is written in red ink, while the majority is in black.</image-desc>

<column-break/>

This is a book composed by the ancient sages <note>often referring to figures like Aristotle or Hermes Trismegistus in this context</note> by which the condition of the Victor and the Vanquished may be known. It works by calculating the name of each of the two individuals using the Great Abjad system <term>Abjad al-Kabir: a system where each Arabic letter is assigned a numerical value (e.g., Alif = 1, Ba = 2)</term>. You then subtract nine by nine <note>a mathematical process known as "casting out nines" to find the remainder</note> from the total sum of each of their names and take the remainder to the table to find the answer.

That which is written in red is the Victor, and that which is written in black is the Vanquished. If the result from both their names is a single number—for instance, if one is the "possessor of nine" and the other the "possessor of eight"—then the judgment of victory goes to the possessor of nine. However, if they are eight and one, then the possessor of eight is the Victor.

And God, glorified and exalted be He, knows best what is right; to Him is the return and the final destination in truth.

<summary>This page describes a divinatory system called "The Victor and the Vanquished," which uses numerology (Abjad) to calculate which of two opponents will prevail in a contest or battle. It provides specific rules for interpreting remainders and highlights the use of color-coded tables to determine the outcome.</summary>
<keywords>divination, numerology, Abjad al-Kabir, Victor and Vanquished, ancient sages, casting out nines, military prediction</keywords>

# Discourse on the System of Twitching
<term>Ikhtilaj: An ancient divinatory practice, common in medieval Islamic and Byzantine medicine, where involuntary muscle spasms or "twitches" were interpreted as omens of future events.</term>

# Explanation of the Selection of Days from the Arabic Months
<note>The "Arabic Months" refer to the Hijri lunar calendar. Each day of the month is assigned a character—auspicious (lucky) or inauspicious (unlucky)—often linked to Quranic events or the lives of the Prophets.</note>

<note>
The terms "Auspicious" (Mahmud) and "Inauspicious" (Madhmum) literally translate to "praiseworthy" and "blameworthy." In the context of medieval astrology, they indicate whether the cosmic energies of the Moon's current position are favorable for a specific task. "Seeking Office" (<term>طلب الولاية</term> — searching for governance or appointment) shows how these guides were used by the administrative class. "Bloodletting" (<term>الفصد والحجامة</term>) refers to the humoral medical practices of the time, where timing was considered essential to prevent health complications.
</note>

If it is ninety degrees, it is a square aspect. If it is one hundred and twenty degrees, it is a trine aspect. If it is one hundred and eighty... <note>The text likely intended to say 'opposition.'</note> They call it "combustion" <note>original: "ihtiraq"; refers to a planet being so close to the Sun that its influence is "burnt up."</note>. If two of the other planets are in one sign together, they call it a conjunction.

### Key Terms and Concepts

<term>High Price</term> (Arabic: *Ghala’*): A critical concern for the reader, indicating inflation or scarcity of essential goods like barley.

<term>Cheapness</term> (Arabic: *Rukhs*): Indicates affordability, economic stability, and a surplus of resources.

<term>Turmoil</term> (Arabic: *Fitna*): A broad term used for civil unrest, riots, or political instability within the community.

<term>Safety</term> (Arabic: *Aman*): Often used in the context of "Safety of the roads," which was vital for trade and pilgrimage in the medieval period.

<term>Lunar Mansions</term> (Arabic: *Manazil al-Qamar*): A 28-part division of the zodiac based on the moon's daily movement.
<term>Rising Mansions</term> (Arabic: *al-Tawali'*): The stars that are rising in the East at dawn on a particular date.
<term>Weather Signs</term> (Arabic: *al-Anwa'*): An ancient Arabian system where the setting of one star and the rising of another predicted rain, wind, or heat.
<term>Syriac Months</term>: The month names used (Nisan, Ayyar, etc.) are from the ancient Syriac calendar, which was standard for agricultural and liturgical use in the Middle East.

It is a good time for buying on land, for it is a sign that indicates the speed and successful completion of matters. <insert>It is disliked therein</insert> to purchase servants or slaves, and to perform bloodletting or cupping. God knows best. |
| <margin>Its entry into the sign of Taurus</margin> | <insert>Action is praised therein</insert> for that which is intended to be permanent and continuous, such as a building meant to last forever. It is also praised for therapeutic vomiting, gargling, seeking stability, purchasing ships, trimming nails, planting trees, and weaning children. <insert>It is disliked therein</insert> to cut or wear new clothing. God knows best the unseen and the judgments. |
| <margin>Its entry into the sign of Gemini</margin> | <insert>It is praised therein</insert> to enter the bathhouse, build fortresses, and settle financial matters brought before <unclear>kings</unclear>. The use of adornment and engravings is praised, and moving or relocating is beneficial. Movement and travel are also praised therein. God knows best. |

God knows best the unseen and the judgments. |

It is praised for treating the liver and ailments of the heart. <insert>It is disliked therein</insert> to tailor or wear new clothes, for it is considered unfavorable. Since it is among the fixed signs <note>signs associated with stability and resistance to change</note> which change very little, the purchase of servants and slaves is favored. God [knows best]. |

In this sign, it is praised to approach leaders among the scribes and masters of accounting and the pen. It is also praised for tailoring, wearing new clothes, trade, and the purchase of grain. God knows best the unseen and is the Most Wise. |

<meta>This page transitions from the general astrological influences of the Zodiac signs (Libra through Scorpio) to a specific system of twenty-eight Lunar Mansions (Manāzil al-Qamar). It focuses specifically on the first seven mansions associated with the transition from Spring into the early heat of Summer. The text blends Hermetic astrological advice (attributed to "Hermes") with the practical "Anwā'" system—a traditional Arab method of tracking seasons, weather, and agriculture by the rising and setting of stars.</meta>

# Explanation of the Seven Mansions that Rise in the Spring Season

<margin>
Image of al-Naṭḥ <note>The Butting Horns of Aries</note>
Image of al-Buṭayn <note>The Little Belly of Aries</note>
Image of al-Thurayyā <note>The Pleiades</note>
Image of al-Dabarān <note>The Follower</note>
Image of al-Haq‘ah <note>The White Spot</note>
Image of al-Han‘ah <note>The Brand</note>
Image of al-Dhirā‘ <note>The Arm</note>
</margin>

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 1: al-Sharaṭān / al-Naṭḥ</note>
It is fixed, fiery, and struck with good fortune. Do not wear new clothes, nor enter the presence of kings. Marriage is disliked during this time. Do not transport grain or travel south or to estates. One may purchase slaves and riding animals. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 2: al-Buṭayn</note>
It is auspicious, hot, and dry. Hermes said: Move quickly to foster love, affection, and the connection of brothers between two people. Act with compassion through friendliness. Do not wear new clothes unless the Moon is in an exceptionally fortunate position. Enter the presence of kings and nobles. God [knows].

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 3: al-Thurayyā / The Pleiades</note>
It is auspicious and mixed. Hermes said: It is proper to strive for love between two people. It is suitable for travel, movement, relocation, and entering the presence of kings and nobles. Conduct marriage contracts and purchase slaves, riding animals, and livestock. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 4: al-Dabarān</note>
It is earthy, dry, and malefic <note>unlucky</note>. Hermes said: Move quickly to sow enmity and hatred between two people. Entering the presence of kings is favored, but do not commit to any [lasting] matter. Do not plant, do not measure out grain, and do not purchase animals. Avoid appearing before kings unless absolutely necessary. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 5: al-Haq‘ah</note>
It is dry, cold, and mixed with good fortune. Hermes said: It is suitable for the making of talismans <note>original: "tamūmāt," likely meaning amulets or charms</note> and treating spirits. Do not plant dye-crops, nor sow, nor plant trees, nor marry. It is suitable for entering the presence of kings and nobles and for giving gifts. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 6: al-Han‘ah</note>
It is glassy and auspicious. Hermes said: Move quickly to foster love, peace, and affection between two people. Connect with brothers, enter the presence of kings to seek fulfillment of needs, and make friends with brethren. It is suitable for travel and movement. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion <note>Mansion 7: al-Dhirā‘</note>
It is auspicious, watery, and malefic <note>possibly meaning a mix of qualities</note>. Hermes said: Move quickly regarding matters of nearby food <note>likely meaning local trade or short-term provisions</note>. Do not wear new clothes unless the Moon is in an exceptionally fortunate position. Travel, enter the presence of kings, connect with nobles, and maintain ties with brothers. Socializing is favored. God [knows].

<column-break/>

### The First Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 23rd of Barmūdah and ends on the 5th of Bashans <note>Late April to early May. These are Coptic months used in the Egyptian agricultural calendar.</note>. The mansion of al-Ghafr sets <note>The "setting" of a star at dawn was used to mark the date</note>. It has a weather period <term>Naw’: a period of expected weather, usually wind or rain, associated with a star's setting</term> characterized by wind and rain. Upon its rising, the pomegranate ripens, the fruit sets, and barley is harvested. An aphorism says: "When al-Sharaṭān rises, the season becomes even."

### The Second Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 6th of Bashans and ends on the 18th. al-Zubānā sets. Its weather period is reliable. During this time, the last of the barley and the first of the wheat are harvested. This completes the mansion's influence. An aphorism says: "When al-Buṭayn rises, the earth is adorned with every rank <note>of plant life</note>."

### The Third Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 19th of Bashans and ends on the 1st of Ba’ūnah <note>Late May to early June</note>. al-Iklīl sets. It has a hot weather period, and the springs of water recede into the earth. An aphorism says: "When al-Thurayyā <note>The Pleiades</note> rises, the shepherd seeks the *shakīyah*"—a *shakīyah* is a small water skin—"because water can no longer be done without."

### The Fourth Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 2nd of Ba’ūnah and ends on the 14th. al-Qalb sets. During this time, there are winds and haze. An aphorism says: "When al-Dabarān rises, fires are hated, bodies suffer, and the ponds dry up." God knows best the truth of judgment.

### The Third Mansion of the Spring Season <note>Note: The manuscript repeats "Third" but it is numerically the fifth section.</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 15th of Ba’ūnah and ends on the 27th. al-Shawlah sets. The *samūm* <note>scorching desert winds</note> and hot gusts blow. The sun-scorched ground burns, fruits ripen, and figs are eaten. An aphorism says: "When al-Haq‘ah rises, it pulls up for us the worst of the tent-pegs," <note>meaning people flee the heat of their tents</note> and they are driven out of the tents.

### The Sixth Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 28th of Ba’ūnah and ends at the conclusion of the 10th of Abīb <note>Late June to early July</note>. al-Na‘ā’im sets. At this time, the heat intensifies. Its rising coincides with the rising of al-Jawzā’ <note>Gemini or Orion</note>. An aphorism says: "When al-Jawzā’ rises, the goats are scorched and the gazelles seek shade in their coverts."

### The Seventh Mansion of the Spring Season
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 11th of Abīb and ends on the 23rd. al-Baldah sets. This time is the limit of heat and its greatest intensity. An aphorism says: "When al-Dhirā‘ rises, the summer fruit turns red, the rays of light blaze on the horizon, and the drinkers disperse from the watering holes."

# Explanation of the Seven Mansions that Rise in the Summer Season

<margin>
When al-Fargh <note>The Spout of the Bucket</note> rises
When al-Jabha <note>The Forehead of the Lion</note> rises
When al-Zubra <note>The Mane</note> rises
When al-Ṣarfa <note>The Diverter</note> rises
When al-‘Awwā’ <note>The Barker</note> rises
When al-Simāk <note>The Unarmed</note> rises
</margin>

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ <note>The Slaughterer’s Luck; the text here identifies the Moon's position by the setting star rather than the rising mansion</note>. Hermes said: Love and affection spread between two people during this time. Know that it is good to wear new clothes, visit kings, and make friends with brothers. It is a suitable time for striving to fulfill needs, seeking rights, and making legal claims. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the space between the mansions. Hermes said: Enmity and hatred spread between two people during this time. Do not wear new clothes. Stay inside your home, for brothers may find the company oppressive. It is a busy time for settling needs, seeking debts, and claiming rights. God knows the unseen best and is most wise.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the space between it and the Forehead of Heat <note>al-Jabha</note>. Hermes said: Visit kings, nobles, and great men; strive to fulfill their needs and connect with them. Sow seeds and plant trees, but do not measure out grain in bulk. God knows the unseen best and informs with truth.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is cold, dry, and auspicious. Hermes said: Love and affection spread between two people. It is a time for craftsmanship. Visit kings, nobles, and sultans; strive in their service and works. Travel during this time and manage the affairs of war and combat. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is a mixture of fiery and earthy elements. Hermes said: Do not visit kings, nor intercede for the needs of others or their works. Do not connect with them, do not marry, and do not buy slaves. All of that is neither praised nor thanked; avoid doing it and be cautious. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is cold, dry, auspicious, yet potentially harmful and deficient in... <note>text cuts off</note>. Hermes said: Love and affection spread between two people. Visit kings, nobles, and the elite; strive to fulfill their needs and works. Wear new clothes. God knows best and is most wise.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is watery and dry. Hermes said: Hatred, separation, and enmity spread between two people. Do not begin any important work, do not visit kings or sultans, do not plan for war, and do not buy slaves, for all of that is greatly condemned. God knows best.

<margin>
Illustration of al-Nathra <note>The Tip of the Nose</note>
Illustration of al-Ṭarf <note>The Eye</note>
Illustration of al-Jabha <note>The Forehead</note>

### The First Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Nathra</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 24th of Abīb <note>Late July</note> and ends on the 6th of Misrā <note>Early August</note>. Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ sets at this time. At this time, the intensity of the heat breaks. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Nathra rises, the vision is keen every morning, cattle seek their shelters, and none are left in...*

### The Second Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Ṭarf</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 7th of Misrā and ends on the 19th of it. Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ continues to set. In this season, fresh dates are eaten and grapes are harvested in Iraq. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Ṭarfa rises, the burning heat increases, and the guest’s burden becomes light.*

### The Third Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Jabha</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 20th of Misrā and ends on the 3rd of Tūt <note>The Coptic New Year, early September</note>. Sa‘d al-Su‘ūd <note>The Luck of Lucks</note> sets. Then the heat departs, the nights grow cool, and the trees turn green without rain. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Jabha rises, the grieving woman is distracted, the lip becomes sweet, and [the heat] diminishes.*

### The Fourth Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Zubra</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 4th of Tūt and ends on the 11th of Tūt <note>The dates here imply a shorter window, likely a scribal error in the day count</note>. Sa‘d al-Akhbiya <note>The Luck of the Tents</note> sets. In it, dates become soft in Egypt, the heat subsides, the nights cool, and the harm of the scorching winds <term>Samūm</term> <note>Hot, dry desert winds</note> departs. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Zubra rises, the lioness is roused...*

### The Fifth Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Ṣarfa</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 19th of Tūt and ends on the 27th of it. Al-Fargh al-Muqaddam <note>The Front Spout</note> sets. At that time, winds blow and the night grows cold. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Ṣarfa rises, the craftsman uses his skill, the man of seed protects his own, and the one near the waters is safe from drowning.*

### The Sixth Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-‘Awwā’</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 25th of Tūt and ends on the 7th of Bābah <note>October</note>. Al-Fargh al-Mu’akhkhar <note>The Rear Spout</note> sets. On this day, planting is promised; this is the time for the call to Hajj and the arrival of... The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-‘Awwā’ rises, the tent is pitched, summer retreats, and winter approaches.*

### The Seventh Mansion of the Summer Season <note>al-Simāk</note>
Its duration is thirteen days. It begins on the 8th of Bābah and ends on the 20th of it. Baṭn al-Ḥūt <note>The Belly of the Fish</note> sets. At this time, the scarcity of water ends. The rhyming aphorism says: *When al-Simāk rises, the stifling heat <term>Akkāk</term> <note>Humid summer heat</note> vanishes, the imagination is mended, disputes are found, and fighting is favored.*

# Explanation of the Seven Mansions that Rise in the Autumn Season

<margin>
The Image of the Barker <note>al-‘Awwā’</note>
The Image of the Unarmed <note>al-Simāk</note>
The Image of the Covering <note>al-Ghafr</note>
The Image of the Claws <note>al-Zubānā</note>
The Image of the Crown <note>al-Iklīl</note>
The Image of the Heart <note>al-Qalb</note>
The Image of the Sting <note>al-Shawla</note>
The Image of the Ostriches <note>al-Na‘ām</note>
The Image of the City <note>al-Balda</note>
</margin>

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the Slaughterer’s Luck <note>Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ</note>. Hermes the Wise said: In this time, strive to reconcile two people with love. Every action that leads to benefit is favored. Enter the presence of kings and nobles, for all of that is praised and auspicious. God knows best what is right.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the Swallower <note>al-Bula‘</note>. Hermes the Wise said: Sowing and harvesting are auspicious. Do not travel during this time. Enter into the presence of kings, sultans, and judges; offer them counsel and fulfill your needs. Do not wear a new garment. God knows best what is right.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the Blown Slaughterer <note>Dhābiḥ Manfūkh</note>. Hermes the Wise said: Strive in it between two people for both love and enmity or hatred <note>original: "al-‘adāwa wa-l-baghḍa"</note>. It is a good time for entering the presence of kings, but do not strive to fulfill your personal needs through them. Do not travel or move from one place to another, for all of that is blameworthy. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the space between the Slaughters <note>mā bayna dhabḥ</note>. Hermes the Wise said: Cast affection and love between two people. Enter into the presence of kings, nobles, and brothers. Sow and harvest during this time, and carry out the tasks in which you seek strength and permanence. God knows best and is most wise.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the space between its exit by fire <note>mā bayna makhrajuhu bi-l-nār</note>. Hermes the Wise said: Do not travel during this time. Sowing and harvesting are praised. Do not enter the presence of kings, sultans, or nobles, for it is blameworthy. One should not marry during this time, nor enter into a partnership with a companion. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is the Second Luck <note>Mānī Sa‘d</note>. Hermes the Wise said: Begin all works in this time. Associate with kings, sultans, and nobles. Marry, travel, engage in war, and mobilize the armies, for all of that has a praised outcome. God knows best.

### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
This is a fiery and malignant mansion. Hermes the Wise said: Do not strive to seek movement or manage a craft. Do not travel, do not enter the presence of kings or sultans, do not marry, do not take a partner, and do not wear new clothes. God knows best and is most wise.
