### The First Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 21st day of Paope <note>Egyptian month: Bābah, roughly October</note> and the last is the end of the 3rd day of Hathor <note>Egyptian month: Hatūr, roughly November</note>. During this time, the Belly <note>al-Baṭān</note> sets. Then the night becomes cold and the merit of the horseman appears. Its rain causes truffles <note>al-kamā’ah</note> to grow.
The rhymer says: "When the Covering <note>al-Ghafr</note> rises..."

### The Second Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 4th day of Hathor and its last is the 16th day. During this time, the Little Belly <note>al-Buṭayn</note> sets. Then the western sea is agitated with currents, and the carob tree and the ants' nest emerge, along with the winged creatures among the vermin and the belly of the earth.
The rhymer says...

### The Third Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 17th day of Hathor and the last is the 29th day. The Pleiades <note>al-Thurayyā</note>, which is the Star, sets. It brings storms and rain. When the Pleiades is opposite the evening time, it is a sign of winter to the Arabs.
The rhymer says: "When the Star rises in the evening, follow the..."

### The Fourth Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 30th day of Hathor and the last is the 12th day of Koiak <note>Egyptian month: Kiyahk, roughly December</note>. The Follower <note>al-Dabarān</note> sets. In this time, there is a scarcity of milk and oil.
The rhymer says: "When the Heart <note>al-Qalb</note> comes, winter arrives like a dog, and the desert folk are in distress."

### The Fifth Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 13th day of Koiak and the last is the 25th day. The Hair-Tuft <note>al-Haq‘a</note> sets. It has a severe storm and frequent drizzle <note>radhādh</note>, which is fine rain.
The rhymer says: "When the Sting <note>al-Shawla</note> rises, the old man's ailment is cleared, but it intensifies for..."

### The Sixth Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 26th day of Koiak and the last is the 8th day of Tobi <note>Egyptian month: Ṭūbah, roughly January</note>. The Mark <note>al-Han‘a</note> sets, and it has a storm of severe cold.
The rhymer says: "When the Ostriches <note>al-Na‘ā’im</note> rise, the cattle are gathered, and the mothers meet the young, and the night weakens for the one who stands in prayer."

### The Seventh Mansion of the Autumn Season
Its duration is thirteen days. The first is the 9th day of Tobi and the last is the 21st day of Tobi. The Arm <note>al-Dhirā‘</note> sets, and it has the "storm of the successor" <note>naww al-khalf</note>. In it is the peak of the cold.
The rhymer says: "When the City <note>al-Balda</note> rises, the skin is protected and cream is eaten." God knows best.

# Explanation of the Eight Mansions that Rise in the Winter Season

<margin>The Image of the Slaughterer’s Luck <note>Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ; the first mansion of winter</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is earthy and malefic, though touched with luck. Hermes the Wise said: In this time, do not enter the presence of kings or nobles, nor should you bond with your brothers. Sow your crops and eat pickled foods <note>original: "al-mukhallalāt"</note>. Do not travel during this time, for it is feared that whoever travels will not return, or their absence will be long. God knows best.

<margin>The Image of the Swallower’s Luck <note>Sa‘d Bula‘</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is earthy and struck by maleficence. Hermes the Wise said: In this time, enter the presence of kings and nobles, bond with your brothers, sow crops, and increase your intake of pickled things. Do not marry, nor should you buy slaves or any beasts of burden. Wear whatever new clothes you desire, for it is a blessed time, God willing.

<margin>The Image of the Luck of Lucks <note>Sa‘d al-Su‘ūd</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is of mixed nature, like earth and winds, and is auspicious. Hermes the Wise said: Mingle with kings, sultans, nobles, and brothers. Wear new clothes and travel. Engage in any works of affection that are hidden from sight, for all of that is praiseworthy. God is all-knowing and most wise.

<margin>The Image of the Luck of the Tents <note>Sa‘d al-Akhbiya</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is earthy and malefic. Hermes the Wise said: Do not travel, marry, or buy slaves. Do not eat pickles, mingle with kings, begin a craft, or wear new clothes. In general, all movement is stagnant <note>original: "mūqūf al-ḥarakāt," meaning actions will not progress</note>. God knows best.

<margin>The Image of the Front Spout <note>al-Fargh al-Muqaddam</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is airy and auspicious. Hermes the Wise said: Eat your food, wear your clothes, and enter the presence of kings, nobles, leaders, and elders. Be joyful <note>original: "wa-l-bashar," likely meaning to show a cheerful face</note> in your new clothes and do whatever you wish, for it is a praiseworthy and lucky form for all movements. God knows best.

<margin>The Image of the Rear Spout <note>al-Fargh al-Mu’akhar</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is watery and auspicious, yet touched by maleficence. Hermes the Wise said: Enter the presence of kings and nobles and wage war against enemies and opponents. Avoid wearing new clothes; for whoever wears a new garment is feared to suffer from stabbing <note>original: "al-ṭi‘ān," which could mean literal wounds or sharp insults</note>. God knows best.

<margin>The Image of the Belly of the Fish <note>Baṭn al-Ḥūt</note></margin>
### When the Moon resides in this Mansion
It is watery and auspicious. Hermes the Wise said: Strive among the people with love and affection. Travel and enter the presence of kings, sultans, elders, and nobles. Be joyful as well, for all of that has a praiseworthy outcome and is lucky in all matters. God knows best.

<column-break/>

<margin>When the Front Spout rises</margin>
### The First Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 22nd day of Tubah <note>January 30th/31st</note> and its end is the 4th day of Amshir <note>February 11th/12th</note>. The constellation of the Nuthra <note>the Nose/Cancer</note> becomes active. At this time, the sap flows in the wood, and the blossoms of the peach trees begin to spark into light. When the Slaughterer’s Luck <note>Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ</note> rises, the people of the snow carry their burdens, the cold winds blow, and the barking living thing is purified.

<margin>When the Rear Spout rises</margin>
### The Second Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 5th of Amshir and its end is the 17th day of the same month. The roads become straight. Upon its rising, frogs croak, birds mate, and the hoopoe lays its eggs. The swimming trees sprout. When the Swallower’s Luck <note>Sa‘d Bula‘</note> rises, the ember <note>heat</note> reaches the core of the earth, though the water may still freeze and the cold intensify.

<margin>When the Belly of the Fish rises</margin>
### The Third Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 18th day of Amshir and its end is the 30th. The "Forehead" <note>al-Jabha, a mansion in Leo</note> straightens. It has a famous storm <note>term: "Naw," a traditional Mediterranean/Red Sea storm period</note> in which winds rage, sheep give birth, the first pigeons are found, and the grass of the earth flourishes. When the Luck of Lucks <note>Sa‘d al-Su‘ūd</note> rises, the branches turn green, skins soften, and life stirs.

<margin>When the Butting rises <note>al-Naṭḥ</note></margin>
### The Fourth Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 1st day of Baramhat <note>March 10th/11th</note> and its end is the 13th day. The two embers <note>stages of seasonal warming</note> fall. It has a famous storm. During this time, the vines leaf out and greenery increases across the land. When the Tents <note>al-Akhbiya</note> rise, the valleys turn green and the cellars <note>aqbiya</note> become pleasant. God knows best.

<margin>When the Belly rises <note>al-Buṭayn</note></margin>
### The Fifth Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 14th of Baramhat and its end is the 26th. The "Change" <note>al-Ṣarfa, the star Denebola</note> falls. At that time, the cold departs, and the almonds, apples, and apricots set their fruit. When the Front of the Bucket <note>Muqaddam al-Dalw</note> rises, spring and dew speak.

<margin>When the Pleiades rise <note>al-Thurayyā</note></margin>
### The Sixth Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 27th of Baramhat and its end is the 9th of Barmuda <note>April 17th/18th</note>. The "Barker" <note>al-‘Awwā</note> falls. In this time, pests emerge from the earth and the jujube fruit <note>al-nabq</note> ripens. When the Rear of the Bucket <note>Mu’akhar al-Dalw</note> rises, goodness surrounds it; I ask God for forgiveness. God knows best.

<margin>When the Follower rises <note>al-Dabarān</note></margin>
### The Seventh Mansion of the Winter Season
Its duration is thirteen days. Its beginning is the 10th day of Barmuda and its end is the 22nd. They call these "The Nights." It has a storm and perhaps a hot wind. When the Fish <note>al-Samakah</note> rises, movement becomes possible, the fishing net is cast, and the time becomes pleasant for partnership.

# Explanation of the Judgments of Coming Events According to the Sciences of al-Muwaffaq <note>Al-Muwaffaq likely refers to a specific medieval scholar or a title meaning "The Favored One" or "The Successful One" to whom these astrological sciences are attributed.</note>

This is a principle established by the sages and mentioned by the ancient philosophers regarding the judgment of the lunar crescents—whether upright or reclined—and the eclipses of the Two Lights <note>original: "an-nayyarayn"; a common Arabic term for the Sun and the Moon</note> during the lunar months. It details what these events signify regarding worldly affairs. I have transcribed this from their books, relying on the truth of their words, and have arranged it as a refined table and a fixed principle for whoever seeks to guard against these four types of events during any month of the year.

| Events | Month of Muharram | Month of Safar | Month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal | Month of Rabi‘ al-Akhir | Month of Jumada al-Ula |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **If the crescent is upright** <note>meaning the "horns" of the new moon point directly upward</note> | Crops will be plentiful this year, and rain will fall during this month and in the pastures. | One of the Two Lights <note>the sun or moon</note> will be eclipsed this year, a great cloud will appear in the sky, and sores and boils will break out on people’s bodies. God knows best. | Fear of a wind upon the earth, or death. | High prices for sheep will become apparent this year; wool and illness will be plentiful. God is most knowing of the correct judgment of the unseen. | Crops and plants will be plentiful this year. |
| **If the crescent is reclined** <note>meaning the moon appears to be "lying on its back" with the tips tilted</note> | Fear of fighting and civil strife; the Sultan <note>the ruler</note> will be angry with his subjects, and stomach ailments will appear in the West <note>original: "al-Maghrib"</note>. | It indicates a descent of affliction upon the people and stomach pain for the Sultan; there will be light rain at the end of the year. God knows best. | It indicates good understanding, generosity, and a lessening of rain. | It indicates the death of many women during this month, specifically elderly women and those advanced in years. God is the wisest judge of the unseen. | Frost will destroy the plants this year. |
| **Lunar Eclipse** | Evil will befall the people of the West, and killing will occur among them. | It indicates a scarcity of rain this year, to the point that it will be apparent even in the palaces of the Hijaz <note>The western region of the Arabian Peninsula</note>. To God belongs the greatness and the truth. | It indicates plague, epidemic, and a multitude of wars and spear-clashing. | It indicates a great death among the prominent people and fear of the Great One. God knows best the unseen. | Rain, snow, cold, and wind will afflict the people. |
| **Solar Eclipse** | <unclear>There will be fighting and war during the harvest days</unclear> | It indicates wars, rain, and fighting among the people; they will leave their homes and head toward Jerusalem <note>original: "al-Quds"</note>. God knows best. | <unclear>There will be fighting and war during the harvest days</unclear> | It indicates a bounty of food, the manifestation of cities in the lands, a multitude of blessings, and an expansion of good things. God knows best. | A great misfortune will strike the world, and fighting will break out between kings. |

# Section
# Explanation of Determining the New Year regarding the Rulings of the Seven Days
<note>The text uses the term "Nowruz," the Persian New Year, which was widely used by medieval Arab astrologers to calculate the "Revolution of the Year" to predict seasonal trends, crop yields, and political events.</note>

<margin>That is: Sunday</margin>
| |
| :--- |
| <insert>God</insert> |
| <term>If the ascendant on this day is<gloss>al-tali'; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of the year</gloss></term> winter [will be] <unclear>humid</unclear> and there will be |
| a sharp wind with <term>heatwaves<gloss>samum; a scorching, dry, and often dusty desert wind</gloss></term>. Coughing, eye inflammation, and deaths among women will increase. Crops will be |
| abundant, and the King will triumph over his enemies and opponents, and God will grant him victory over them. And God knows best. |

<margin>That is: Monday</margin>
| |
| :--- |
| <term>If the New Year falls on this day, the winter will be mild</term>, and |
| the season and the summer will be cold. Shortages will increase, many diseases will afflict people, and the plague and death will increase. |
| Honey will be scarce, crops will be fertile, the populace will migrate from country to country, and discord will occur between people. |

<margin>That is: Tuesday</margin>
| |

<meta>Following the previous page’s historical and genealogical records of the Prophet’s family and the early Caliphate, the manuscript now shifts into a section of "Fal" (divination or omens). This was a common practice where seekers would look for spiritual guidance or predictions for their future, often using numbers, days of the week, or randomly selected verses.</meta>

# The Omen of the One <note>original: "al-Ahad," referring to both the number one and Sunday</note>

Rejoice, O seeker! Your endeavor is successful, your movements are virtuous, and your trade is profitable. Happiness shines upon you, and the signs of good news are clear. The seas of goodness are overflowing, the breezes of union are fragrant with ambergris, and the birds of proximity sing upon the trees of joy. Your friends are sincere to you, while the eyes of your enemies are averted and their faces are grim. The good days will return to you; for this night is not like the nights of the past. Fear no calamities, for I have sought protection for you through the Chapter of the Opening <note>The "Fatiha," the first chapter of the Quran</note>. <gloss>The author of this verse</gloss>

->An omen comes with guidance, goodness, and affection<-
->So trust in the One Lord; He shall suffice you against the evil of distress<-
->Take my words and follow this arranged table<-
->You struck me with the "One," and I answered with the "One"<-

***

# The Omen of the Two <note>original: "al-Ithnayn," referring to the number two and Monday</note>

Rejoice, O seeker! Happiness for you is steadfast <note>original: "hadid," literally iron, meaning strong or perhaps a misspelling of "jadid," new</note>, and the troublesome envier is far removed from you. Your status is upright, your condition is stable, and you and those you love are in bliss, while your enemies are in misery. Your generosity is immense, and the Noble God has taken you by the hand. Whatever you have intended, its outcome leads to contentment and submission. The one who journeys is not like the one who is sound, nor is the deprived like the one who is truly barred. As for marriage, it is as fine as silk; and travel to Zamzam and the Hateem <note>Sacred sites within the Great Mosque of Mecca</note> is auspicious. God has saved you from every ignorant oppressor; I have sought protection for you through the Seven Oft-Repeated verses and the Great Quran <note>A reference to the Al-Fatiha and the Quran as a whole</note>. <gloss>The author of these stringed pearls</gloss>

->Rejoice in a life of plenty and the goodness of a happy union<-
->In elevation and lordship, glory shall make you happy<-
->Your might is eternal; do not turn back, but rather begin<-
->You struck me with the "Two," and I have tripled it with the "One"<-

<vocab>
**Fal:** An omen or a practice of seeking a good augury.
**Qara'at:** Literally "knocking" or "striking," referring here to the act of casting a lot or selecting a number in divination.
**The Seven Oft-Repeated (Al-Sab' al-Mathani):** A title for the seven verses of the Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Quran.
**The Stringed Pearls (Al-Durr al-Nazim):** A metaphorical way of describing high-quality poetry or prose; also a common title for books on divination and secrets of the Quran.
**Bishara:** Glad tidings or good news.
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains divinatory readings (fal) for someone who has "struck" or selected the numbers One or Two, offering auspicious predictions for trade, marriage, and travel. The text uses rhymed prose and poetry to provide a "warm" and encouraging spiritual forecast, common in popular medieval Islamic literature.</summary>
<keywords>divination, omens, fal, Arabic poetry, Fatiha, pilgrimage, Meccan sites, spiritual guidance</keywords>

**Technical Terms:**
*   **Omen/Lot:** <term>Fal</term> - A practice of seeking an augury or good-luck reading from a text.
*   **The Strike:** <term>Qar'ah</term> - The act of casting dice or drawing lots to determine which section of the book to read.
*   **Geomancy:** <term>Al-Raml</term> - "Science of the Sand," a divination system using patterns of dots.
*   **The Seeker:** <term>Al-Sa'il</term> - The person asking the question of the book.
*   **Good Fortunes:** <term>Al-Su'ud</term> - Auspicious stars or lucky timings.
*   **The Worshiped:** <term>Al-Ma'bud</term> - One of the names of God.
*   **The Goal:** <term>Al-Maqsud</term> - The intended outcome or desire of the seeker.
*   **The Creator:** <term>Al-Sani'</term> - Literally "The Artisan" or "Maker," referring to God.

# The Strike of Five ⁂ The Strike of Two

Be patient, O seeker <term>al-sa'il</term>, for "How excellent is the patient servant." Do not approach this secret intention <note>original: "al-damir"—in divination, this refers to the unspoken question or hidden matter in the seeker's heart</note>, for you will fall into peril. If you are determined to marry, then delay the crossing and the transaction. Do not act with haste, for effort at this time is not rewarded. So be patient until the best outcome appears through His wisdom, and the suns and full moons shine forth. For darkness is not like light, nor is shade like the scorching heat <note>A reference to Quran 35:19-21, emphasizing the ontological difference between good and evil, or success and failure</note>, nor are thorns like flowers, nor graves like palaces. Be patient, for patience is a trade that will never fail <term>lan tabur</term>, and its practitioner is rewarded by God. Time may be oppressive and the celestial spheres revolve, but the final outcome of all matters belongs to God.

<margin>Wait out the thorns of the henna plant</margin>

Indeed, patience is the harvest of the saints. Delay what you intended and remain patient, for your anxiety is like being cast into a fire. Be steadfast in every matter with the firmest possible contentment. Five [dots] have struck for me, and my discourse met you on Wednesday. Completed with the praise of God and His gracious guidance.

# Turkish Works

O space that fashioned this rectangular earth <note>A poetic reference to the physical world, often described in Islamic cosmology as having four corners or being a vast expanse under the celestial dome</note>, where the play of life begins! O soul, this is a dusty dwelling. Do not hide within this <term>Zij</term> <note>original: "Zij" — a set of astronomical tables used to calculate the positions of the sun, moon, and planets</note>, for you are the very light of sight. Are those the people you awakened with your morning sighs?

Pure are your feet, though your heart is scorched with fire. One day you shall say to me, "Is this the dust of the road?" In this rose-garden, those of salt-like form stand tall. In this station, the heart seeks its remedy.

Become a companion to your own breast; let no stranger enter. Sometimes you shall perform acts of kindness, and other times you shall deny tyranny and cruelty. Sometimes you shall fulfill your promises. In this world, memory is the true alchemy for the clever.

A graceful stature and eyes like a king's <note>original: "Gözü şehla"—describing a dark, slightly drooping, or almond-shaped eye considered a mark of supreme beauty and authority</note>. May that person reach God and find his beloved. He would find fortune and a long life indeed. Praise be to God, for the people of happiness are overflowing with grace.

Our gathering is bound; if you are joyful, it does not make the onlooker joyful. The crown is like a throne in the valley of kings. The group of those in the monastery has become purified. The cupbearer of the feast of pleasure is the very essence of joy.

The word of those who come for wine, whose law is healing—it is the tradition that the stroke of the plectrum is the medicine for silver-colored pain. With strength and opportunity, this jurist <term>faqih</term> stands particularly as the leader in the King's council.

The cup of the banquet is the wine of the pure essence of the grape. He is the Darius of Alexander, the Emperor of discernment, the Tahmuras of majesty, and the Hoshang of wisdom <note>These are legendary kings from the Persian *Shahnameh*, representing the ultimate archetypes of power, demon-conquering, and civilizing wisdom</note>. He is Bahram the hunter, and the Zal and Jamshid of politics.

He is the one who speaks of the forty and the seven heavens. Yahya of generosity, the slayer and the slain of the sword. The Sultan of the world, the Shah of the age, the judge of the world, the Victorious, the Triumphant, the tower of religion: **Muhammad**.

From the Truth <note>original: "Hakk"—one of the 99 names of God, meaning the Absolute Truth</note>, eternal fortune was granted to him. He who follows his word was accepted from pre-eternity. He who turns from his path remained rejected forever. In his presence, bounty and generosity are always praised.

Through him, the garden of the world is joyful and green. Through his life, he is like Jamshid, and in his justice, he is like Khosrow. In your era, tyranny is forgotten and its name is hidden. Wherever there is turmoil, it is extinguished by your authority.

The lion of the state is draped in honor. Helping the state and its prosperity is his sign. Since he became the dust of your path, his rank has become supreme. O King of the world, Khosrow Parviz of the age!

You are the soul of the world, from the sky to the body of the sun. You are the scatterer of gold, the pourer of jewels, and the spreader of silver. In the time of battle, you are the brave lion. You are the hope of the people and their ultimate purpose.

May your gate be the furthest goal for all. Wherever you resolve to go, the Great Creator and Fortune shall be your companions. Victory is the elder of the conquering world and the victorious King.

The seven kingdoms read your titles with devotion. Through the grace of God, they become servants at your gate. With majesty, you are Firdaws, and with splendor, you are Darius. Through your justice, the world has become the rose-garden of Iram <note>A legendary lost city or paradise mentioned in the Quran, symbolizing ultimate earthly beauty and luxury</note>.

With your good thoughts and treasury, with your bounty and grace, no word can be found to match your speech. Through your benevolence, the kingdom of the world is sustained. O star and moon of religion and the world!

As long as the love of the heavens is manifest in the heart, as long as the five fingers of the earth revolve with the turning of the firmament, as long as the courtyard of the sky makes the sun turn crimson, as long as the horizon scatters the darkness of night—

May the morning launch its raid upon your year. May the evening and morning be yours by the decree of the Inscrutable One. May your festival be blessed, and may you be victorious and powerful. O you, who are the master of all the world's creatures!

As the heavens turn, let your horses be shod. Like Ahmad the Messenger and the father of Qasim <note>Referring to the Prophet Muhammad</note>, may your existence be joyful, eternal, and steadfast. May your fortune be awake while others sleep.

May all the means of your desire be prepared.

->The traveler Benjamin Efendi<-

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O God, send blessings upon our master Muhammad.

Praise be to God, the Gatherer of the dead, the Lifter of good deeds, and the Warder of afflictions; the All-Powerful, the Wise, the All-Aware; the Apportioner of life-spans, the Knower of circumstances, and the Accepter of deeds; the Originator of forms <note>original: "al-astal," likely a variation of "ashkal" (forms/shapes) or referring to the "vessels" of creation.</note>; the Merciful, the Generous, the Provider; the Decorator of the heaven with the beauty of the stars, adorning it with the luminaries that rise and set, bringing them forth from their rising-points like stars; the Discloser of their lights by the inspiration of the darknesses; the Measurer of their paths by hours, degrees, and minutes.

It is as if the sky over the earth is a <term>musajrad</term><note>A term describing something intricately patterned or vaulted, often used to describe the "brocade" of the heavens.</note> dome, draped in azure robes; and the stars were of various ruby-like shapes, masterfully fashioned by Divine power. The dome has never been defiled by the hands of time, nor has it been struck by hammers. Its curtains rise with the stars of the dark, and its light appears in the dusk after the twilight. 

The light vanishes at its peak, and the "mouths" of the stars laugh with wide smiles. One might think it safe from vanishing and free from calamities, as its dazzling radiance overwhelms the eyes. Thoughts wander among its heights, and the fluttering of gazes follows the swiftness of its motion. In its centers, the flowers of plants bloom for the observer, and the stars of Gemini <note>original: "al-Jawza." In traditional Arabic astronomy, al-Jawza often referred to Orion, though it later became the standard name for Gemini.</note> are arranged among them like necklaces. 

Jealous forces turned against them from the spheres of the day, and the dawn rose up seeking vengeance. The moon grew jealous and fell away after sinking. Its "receding stars" <note>original: "khunus," a reference to the Quranic term for planets that appear to retreat or hide.</note> began their defeat and flight. The herald of parting cried out from longing, and their lights departed on their journey and dimmed. Their horses stumbled through sheer determination and fell. The swords of their radiance scattered and vanished, fleeing from the Sultan of the Sun like a runaway slave. 

The army of the darkness camped at the horizons. The **Two Signs** <note>original: "al-Sharatayn." The first lunar mansion, consisting of the two "horns" of Aries.</note> imposed conditions upon the moon that it should not appear. **The Little Belly** <note>original: "al-Butayn." The second lunar mansion, located in the "belly" of Aries.</note> hid between **The Pleiades** <note>original: "al-Thurayya." The third lunar mansion, one of the most famous star clusters.</note> and **The Follower** <note>original: "al-Dabaran." The fourth lunar mansion, the bright star Aldebaran which "follows" the Pleiades.</note> so as to be concealed. **The Hair Whorl** <note>original: "al-Haq’ah." The fifth lunar mansion, located in the head of Orion.</note> appeared, hurrying on its transit, while **The Mark** <note>original: "al-Han’ah." The sixth lunar mansion, in Gemini.</note> retreated, its connections severed. The breeze of the breath of **The Mark** blew pleasantly, and **The Arm** <note>original: "al-Dhira’." The seventh lunar mansion, referring to the outstretched arm of a metaphorical "lion" in ancient Arabic star lore.</note> bid farewell to the path of flight and departure.

# Astronomical Tables for the Month of Tuba (January)

### Solar Altitudes, Shadows, and Prayer Timing

This table provides daily coordinates for the Sun’s position and the resulting timings for prayers and daylight. The "Fingers of the Noon Shadow" were a primary method for determining the time of the noon (<term>Dhuhr</term>) and afternoon (<term>Asr</term>) prayers before the advent of mechanical clocks.

->The rulings of the tables composed according to the Coptic months are completed<-

Understand then what I have told you, O student <note>literally "one who is served," a respectful term for a pupil</note>. For example, the first day of the Coptic month of <term>Tout</term> <note>the first month of the Coptic calendar</note> is the twenty-ninth day of the Roman month of August, and it is the third day from the dawn of June <note>this likely refers to a specific seasonal or agricultural marker used in the region</note>. At this time, the sun has traversed fourteen degrees of the <term>Zodiac sign of Virgo</term> <note>original: Burj al-Sunbulah, "The Ear of Grain"</note>. The maximum altitude of the sun is sixty-six degrees and thirty minutes—which is half a degree—and the shadow at noon <note>meridian shadow</note> measures five <term>fingers</term> <note>a traditional unit where a vertical rod is divided into twelve equal parts or "fingers"</note>. The altitude at the time of the Afternoon prayer <note>Asr</note> is thirty-five degrees.

The <term>arc of the day</term> <note>the path the sun travels above the horizon</note> for that day is one hundred and eighty-eight degrees, and the arc of the night for that day is one hundred and seventy-two degrees. The <term>direction of the Qibla</term> <note>Samt al-Qibla; the direction of Mecca for prayer</note> is fifty-two degrees, and the shadow cast when the sun is in that direction is eight fingers. The portion of the dawn is twenty-four degrees. Understand this well, as we have explained it in Arabic so that no error may occur.

**Section** Know that the <term>Lunar Mansions</term> <note>Manazil al-Qamar; the 28 divisions of the sky the moon passes through each month</note> are twenty-eight in number. The first is *al-Sharatan* <note>The Two Signs, located in Aries</note> and the last is *al-Risha*, which is also called the *Belly of the Whale* <note>Batn al-Hut; located in the constellation of Pisces</note>. These mansions have a specific width toward the North and South directions; that is to say, the distance of their degrees from the rising points of the "Head of Aries" and the "Head of Libra" <note>the equinox points</note>. I shall illustrate for you in these books the mansions, their directions, and their degrees at the top of the tables in this registry.

### The rules for the tables of the rising, culminating, and
### setting mansions in the Coptic months are completed; God is the grantor of success. **Section**

Know—may God guide us and you—that these <term>Lunar Mansions</term> <note>original: al-manazil; 28 segments of the sky through which the moon passes</note> have specific boundaries within the twelve <term>Zodiac Signs</term> <note>original: al-buruj</note> measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds. They rise with these signs when they appear from the eastern horizon and set with them when they disappear in the western horizon. They have a calculated position within the Zodiac and a constellation form by which you can identify them during their rising and setting. 

I shall mention to you the names of the mansions and which Zodiac signs they belong to, along with their degrees, minutes, and seconds, the limit of each mansion, how much of the Zodiac sign it traverses, and which of the twenty-eight mansions correspond to each of the twelve Zodiac signs through calculation and observation.

**An example:** the mansion of <term>The Two Signs</term> <note>original: al-Sharatayn; the horns of Aries</note> is the first of the mansions, and the sign of <term>Aries</term> <note>original: al-Hamal</note> is the first of the Zodiac signs. Know that when the mansion of The Two Signs rises, its limit within the sign of Aries is **12 11 26** <note>These are Abjad numerals: 12 degrees, 11 minutes, 26 seconds</note>, which is twelve degrees, eleven minutes, and twenty-six seconds. 

When the second mansion rises, which is <term>The Little Belly</term> <note>original: al-Butayn; three small stars in Aries</note>, its limit within the signs of Aries and <term>Taurus</term> <note>original: al-Thawr</note> is **26 42 11** <note>26 degrees, 42 minutes, 11 seconds</note>, which is twenty-six degrees, forty-two minutes, and eleven seconds. 

When the third mansion rises, which is <term>The Pleiades</term> <note>original: al-Thurayya</note>, its limit within the sign of Taurus is **8 37 6** <note>The text provides the numerical shorthand as 8° 37' 06", but the prose description varies slightly</note>, which is eight degrees, thirty-four minutes, and seventeen seconds. 

When the fourth mansion rises, which is <term>The Follower</term> <note>original: al-Dabaran; the bright red star in Taurus</note>, its limit within the signs of Taurus and <term>Gemini</term> <note>original: al-Jawza'</note> is **21 35 6** <note>21 degrees, 35 minutes, 6 seconds</note>, which is twenty-one degrees, thirty-five minutes, and six seconds. 

When the fifth mansion rises, which is <term>The Hair Tuft</term> <note>original: al-Haq'ah; stars in the head of Orion/Gemini</note>, its limit within the sign of Gemini is **4 17 9** <note>4 degrees, 17 minutes, 9 seconds</note>, which is four degrees, seventeen minutes, and nine seconds. 

When the sixth mansion rises, which is <term>The Brand</term> <note>original: al-Han'ah; stars in the feet of Gemini</note>, its limit is **17 30** <note>17 degrees, 30 minutes</note> in the house of Gemini. Note that the second part of The Follower and its limit extend to the end of the sign of Gemini. This constitutes the **Spring Season** from its beginning to its end. I shall mention the rest of the Zodiac signs and all the mansions and their forms in the tables that follow this list.

<meta>This page continues the astronomical instructions from page 108. Having provided the reference table for the four celestial pivots, the author now transitions into the practical application of these mansions—specifically how their positions relate to the Coptic solar calendar, which was used throughout the medieval Islamic world for agricultural and meteorological timing.</meta>

These rising, culminating, and setting mansions, as well as the Pivot of the Earth <note>The *Imum Coeli* or the lowest point of the sky</note>, are now completed. Know—may God guide us and you—that when the mansion of **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> rises, the culminating mansion in the middle of the sky is **Fortune of the Sacrificer** <note>original: *Sa'd al-Dhabih*</note>, the setting mansion on the western horizon is **The Covering** <note>original: *al-Ghafr*</note>, and the mansion beneath the Pivot of the Earth is **The Gap** <note>original: *al-Nathrah*</note>. Perform your timing based on this observation and understand it; you shall be guided, God willing.

### Section
Know—may God guide us and you—that among these twenty-eight mansions, there are those that culminate at the zenith <note>the point directly overhead</note> on the meridian line at the break of dawn, according to observed and calculated measurements. I shall mention to you the days of their culmination within the Coptic months <note>The Coptic calendar was favored by medieval astronomers for its fixed solar year, unlike the shifting lunar Hijri calendar</note>, which never deviate from those observed calculations in their months and days. **For example**, the mansion of **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> always culminates at the zenith at dawn on the twelfth day of the month of **Amshir** <note>roughly February/March</note>. I shall record this for you in tables, writing their names at the top along with the time of their appearance by Coptic days and months, observed and verified. I will write them in what follows this page.

### Section
Know—may God guide us and you—that among these twenty-eight mansions, from **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> to the mansion of **The Rope** <note>original: *al-Rasha*, also known as the Belly of the Fish</note>, there are those that rise from the eastern horizon at the disappearance of the red twilight <note>dusk</note>, observed and calculated according to the nights of the Coptic months. I shall mention their names and their rising times in the Coptic months and nights. **For example**, the mansion of **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> rises from the eastern horizon at the disappearance of the red twilight on a night that precedes the morning of the third day of the month of **Tut** <note>the first month of the Coptic year, roughly September</note>. The mansion of **The Little Belly** <note>original: *al-Butayn*</note> rises from the eastern horizon at the disappearance of the red twilight on a night that precedes the morning of the sixteenth day of the month of **Tut**. The mansion of **The Pleiades** <note>original: *al-Thurayya*</note> rises from the eastern horizon at the disappearance of the red twilight on a night that precedes the morning of the eighth day of the month of **Babah** <note>roughly October</note>. Know that the explanation is lengthy, so I shall record that for you in tables following this second page. I will write at the head of the tables the names of the mansions, the disappearance of the twilight, and the rising of the mansions on nights preceding the elapsed days of the Coptic months. Understand, and you shall be guided.

--- Page 223 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of the 28 Lunar Mansions—the stations where the moon resides each night of its cycle. While the previous page focused on the zenith positions in the month of Amshir, this page expands the system to account for various points throughout the night (rising, culminating, and setting) and introduces the month of Parmouti (Barmudah) as a primary example for the mansion of The Two Signs.</meta>

### Section
Know—may God guide us and you—that the passage of the moon through its mansions, from the mansion of **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> to the mansion of **The Rope** <note>original: *al-Rasha*, also known as the Belly of the Fish</note>, comprising the twenty-eight mansions, follows specific patterns. **Among them are those that rise** with the dawn; **among them are those that rise** at the beginning of the night; **among them are those that culminate** <note>reach the highest point in the sky</note> at the beginning of the night; and **among them are those that set** at the beginning of the night.

**Among them are those that rise** in the first quarter of the night; **among them are those that culminate** in the first quarter of the night; and **among them are those that set** in the first quarter of the night. **Among them are those that rise** in the first third of the night; **among them are those that culminate** in the first third of the night; and **among them are those that set** in the first third of the night. **Among them are those that rise** at midnight; **among them are those that culminate** at midnight; and **among them are those that set** at midnight.

**Among them are those that rise** at two-thirds of the night; **among them are those that culminate** at two-thirds of the night; and **among them are those that set** at two-thirds of the night. **Among them are those that rise** at three-quarters of the night; **among them are those that culminate** at three-quarters of the night; and **among them are those that set** at three-quarters of the night. **Among them are those that culminate** at the break of dawn, and **among them are those that set** at the break of dawn.

I shall mention this for you according to the days of the **Coptic months** <note>The Coptic calendar was used for its precision in tracking the solar year and seasons</note> and I will illustrate it for you in tables as well, to make it easy for you to memorize what I record. **An example** of this is that the mansion of **The Two Signs** <note>original: *al-Sharatayn*</note> rises at dawn on the twenty-third day of the month of **Parmouti** <note>original: *Barmudah*, a month in the Coptic calendar roughly corresponding to April</note>. At that time, the mansion culminating at dawn is **Fortune of the Sacrificer** <note>original: *Sa’d al-Dhabih*</note>, and the mansion setting at dawn is **The Covering** <note>original: *al-Ghafr*</note>. 

The mansion rising at the beginning of the night is **The Crown** <note>original: *al-Iklil*</note>, the mansion culminating at the beginning of the night is **The Forehead** <note>original: *al-Jabhah*</note>, and the mansion setting at the beginning of the night is **The Pleiades** <note>original: *al-Thurayya*</note>.

The mansion rising in the first quarter of the night is **The Ostriches** <note>original: *al-Na'ayim*</note>, the mansion culminating in the first quarter of the night is **The Mark** <note>original: *al-Han'ah*</note>, and the mansion setting in the first quarter of the night is **The Mark** <note>original: *al-Han'ah*</note>. <note>The scribe repeated "The Mark" likely by mistake or referring to a specific position</note> 

The mansion rising in the first third of the night is **The Town** <note>original: *al-Baldah*</note>, the mansion culminating in the first third of the night is **The Unarmed** <note>original: *al-Simak*</note>, and the mansion setting in the first third of the night is **The Arm** <note>original: *al-Dhira’*</note>.

The mansion rising at midnight is **Fortune of the Devourer** <note>original: *Sa'd Bula'*</note>, the mansion culminating at midnight is **The Claws** <note>original: *al-Zubanan*</note>, and the mansion setting at midnight is **The Glance** <note>original: *al-Tarf*</note>.

The mansion rising at two-thirds of the night is **Fortune of the Tents** <note>original: *Sa'd al-Akhbiyah*</note>, the mansion culminating at two-thirds of the night is **The Heart** <note>original: *al-Qalb*</note>, and the mansion setting at two-thirds of the night is **The Mane** <note>original: *al-Zubrah*</note>.

The mansion rising at three-quarters of the night is **The First Spout** <note>original: *al-Fargh al-Muqaddam*</note>, the mansion culminating at three-quarters of the night is **The Tail** <note>original: *al-Shulah*</note>, and the mansion setting at three-quarters of the night is **The Changer** <note>original: *al-Sarfah*</note>.

This is the rule for the dawn rising of **The Two Signs**. If I were to explain all the mansions in this way, it would be too much for you to handle, so I will instead illustrate them in tables and write their rules at the head of each on the following page.

He promises to present the remaining data in structured tables for easier memorization.</summary>

# Table of the Illustrations of the Mansions: Rising, Culminating, Setting, and the Pivot of the Earth

Section 7. Know—may God guide us and you—that among the twenty-eight <term>Mansions</term> <note>the 28 stations of the moon</note>, some are rising, some are culminating, some are setting, and some are beneath the <term>Pivot of the Earth</term> <note>the Nadir, or the lowest point of the sky below the horizon</note>, according to what was previously mentioned in the tables. I have depicted them in this circle so that it may also be easier for you to observe.

->[Diagram of the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions]<-

<note>The diagram is a circle divided into 28 segments. At the four cardinal points of the axes, the following labels are written:</note>
**Line of the East** (Rising)
**Line of the Midheaven** (Culminating)
**Line of the West** (Setting)
**Pivot of the Earth** (Nadir)

<margin>
If it is in the East
</margin>

<margin>
The Covering <note>original: al-Ghafr</note> is the pivot of the remainder
</margin>

The relationship between them is calculated by the movement. For example: know that if the rising mansion on the eastern horizon is <term>al-Sharaṭayn</term> <note>The Two Signs; the horns of Aries</note>, then the culminating mansion on the line of the Midheaven is <term>Sa‘d al-Dhābiḥ</term> <note>The Lucky Star of the Slaughterer; in Capricorn</note>, and the setting mansion on the western horizon is <term>al-Ghafr</term> <note>The Covering; in Virgo</note>, and the <term>Dar-bakht</term> <note>a Persian astrological term for the fourth house/lot</note> or Pivot of the Earth is the mansion of <term>al-Nathrah</term> <note>The Sneeze; in Cancer</note>. This is the illustration of what I have described to you. Understand it, and you shall be guided, God the Exalted willing.

### Section 8: Know—may God guide us and you—that the twelve zodiac signs, from the sign of Aries to the sign of Pisces, contain fixed stars.

These stars are used to take <term>elevation</term> <note>altitude measurements using an astrolabe or quadrant</note> so that one may know what has passed of the night, as well as the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>the highest point of the sun or stars' path</note>, the <term>Descendant</term> <note>the point setting in the west</note>, the point that is under the <term>Pivot of the Earth</term> <note>the Nadir, or lowest point below the horizon</note>, and other such things. I have placed twenty-two stars in this book; they are the largest ones and they assist in keeping track of the times of day and night.

I shall mention them to you. Know that every zodiac sign has fixed stars specific to it. Every star has a "limit" within that sign in terms of degrees and minutes, and a "magnitude"—meaning the measure of its size—and a "temperament"—meaning its color and which of the seven <term>wandering planets</term> <note>the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> it resembles.

I will provide examples for you. **His example:** The first of the zodiac signs is Aries. In it is a <unclear>fixed</unclear> star called **The Stained Hand** <note>original: Kaff al-Khadib; the star Beta Cassiopeiae</note>. It is of the third magnitude. Its position in the <unclear>sign</unclear> of Aries is at this **degree** and minute: twenty-four degrees and forty-seven minutes. Its temperament—meaning its color—is the temperament of Saturn and Venus. This means that if you were to mix those two planets, the color of the star "The Stained Hand" would be like theirs.

In the sign of Taurus, there is a star called **The Ghoul's Head** <note>original: Ra's al-Ghul; the star Algol</note>. It is of the second magnitude. Its position in the sign of Taurus is **16 degrees, 37 minutes** <note>original uses Abjad numerals: yw (16) and lz (37)</note>, which is sixteen degrees and thirty-seven minutes. Its temperament—in the sense of its color—is the temperament of Mars and Mercury. This means if you mixed the light of those two planets, it would be its color.

In the sign of Taurus also is a star called **The Bearer of the Ghoul's Head**, and it is also called **The Side of the Bearer of the Ghoul's Head** <note>the star Mirfak in the constellation Perseus</note>. It is of the second magnitude. Its position in the sign of Taurus is <unclear>21</unclear> degrees and [some] minutes, specifically twenty-one degrees and forty-seven minutes. Its temperament is the temperament of Mars and Mercury; if you mixed the light of those two planets, they would resemble the Side of the Bearer of the Ghoul's Head.

In the sign of Taurus also is a star called **The Eye of the Bull** <note>original: 'Ain al-Thaur; the star Aldebaran</note>. It is of the first magnitude. Its position is **21 degrees, 37 minutes**.

The explanation would be long, so I will arrange them in a table to make it easy for you. I will write at the top of the columns how to identify them, just as the tables appear on the following page.

# The Order of the Ten Celestial Spheres

**Chapter** Know—may God guide us and you—that the celestial spheres are ten revolving spheres spanning from horizon to horizon, meaning from the eastern horizon to the western horizon. **Among them** is the Greatest Sphere <note>the *Primum Mobile*, the outermost sphere that moves all others</note>, which is the highest and greatest of them. **Among them** is the Sphere of the Zodiac, which contains the twelve signs. At the time of this observation in our present age, the first of their names are: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo <note>original: *al-Sunbula*; literally "the Ear of Grain"</note>, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius <note>original: *al-Dali*; "the Water-Drawer"</note>, and Pisces. These are their names.

**Among them** is the Sphere of the Fixed Stars, which contains the fixed stars, the desert-navigation stars <term>al-Biyabaniya; from the Persian 'biyaban' meaning desert—stars used for orientation in the wilderness</term>, and the Capellae <term>al-‘Ayuqat; a group of bright stars used as markers, named after the star Capella</term>.

**Among them** is the sphere that is the first of the seven [wandering stars], which is the sphere of the "Piercing Star" <note>a reference to its sharp brightness</note>; it is *Kaiwan* and is called **Saturn**.

**Among them** is the sphere of the "Judge," which is called **Jupiter**, and it is located below the sphere of Saturn.

**Among them** is the sphere of *Bahram*, who is the "Swordsman" <margin>and is called</margin> **Mars**, and it is below the sphere of Jupiter.

**Among them** is the sphere of the **Sun**; it is the middle of the seven, and its position is the <unclear>central</unclear> one, and for that reason, its light outshines <note>literally: "pierces" or "breaks through"</note> all the other planets.

**Among them** is the sphere of the "Songstress," which is **Venus**, and it is below the sphere of the Sun.

**Among them** is the sphere of the "Vizier" <note>the Minister</note>, which is called **Mercury**, and it is below the sphere of Venus.

**Among them** is the sphere of the "Messenger," which is the **Moon**. These comprise the total of the ten spheres. I shall depict them for you in a circle, showing their characteristics, and I will write their names upon them and what follows these lists.

# On the Fixed Stars and the Capellae

**Chapter** Know—may God guide us and you—that the stars called the Capellae <term>al-‘Ayuqat</term> have boundaries, magnitudes, descriptions, forms, positions <note>lunar mansions</note>, and names. I have set down for you in this book that which will make any other [source] unnecessary, all observed and defined. 

Their names are: the Weapon, which is the Lancer <note>Arcturus</note>; the Bier <note>stars of the Big Dipper</note>; the Northern Bowl <note>Alphecca in the Northern Crown</note>; the Head of the Ghoul <note>Algol</note>; the Capella of the Pleiades; the Daughters <note>likely *Banat Na‘sh*, part of Ursa Major</note> and their eagles; the Horsemen; the Finger of Zainab; the Falling Eagle <note>Vega</note>; the Flying Eagle <note>Altair</note>; the Follower <note>Deneb</note>; the Syrian Arm <note>Procyon</note>; the Stained Hand <note>Beta Cassiopeiae</note>; the Beast of the Sea <note>Cetus</note>; the Heart of the Great Change <note>possibly a corruption of *Qalb al-Asad*, Regulus</note>; the Great Wolf and the Small Wolf; the Kid <note>here referring to Polaris, the North Star</note>; the Knee; the Four Returning Camels <note>stars in Draco</note>; and the Two Calves <note>stars in Ursa Minor</note>.

I shall illustrate for you the form of what I have mentioned, as well as the Straight Sphere <term>Sphaera Recta</term>, the pole, the southern declination, the northern declination, their magnitudes, the zodiac signs, and the East, West, South, and North. Therefore, apply yourself to the eternal [study].

<meta>This page continues the discussion of celestial mechanics from the previous description of the spheres, moving from the general structure of the cosmos to the specific mathematical and physical properties of the twelve zodiac signs.</meta>

**Section** Know—may God guide us and you—that the twelve zodiac signs previously mentioned, from the sign of Aries to the sign of Pisces, each has an "inclination" <note>original: "mayl," referring to celestial declination—the distance of a point on the ecliptic from the celestial equator</note>, meaning the inclination of the beginning of the sign from the Equator. Each also has a sine and degrees of sine used by the timekeeper <term>Timekeeper</term> <note>original: "al-miqati," a specialist in spherical astronomy and mathematical timekeeping, often responsible for calculating prayer times</note> on instruments to determine the altitude and the daylight hours when the sun resides in that sign. Furthermore, each has degrees of altitude—meaning the altitude at the start of the sign—and "ascensions" <note>original: "matali’," the degrees of the equator that rise with a specific part of the zodiac in a given latitude</note> of the degrees in the "Right Sphere" <note>the celestial equator</note>, as well as "descensions" <note>original: "magharib"</note> meaning when it sets. It also has an "eastern amplitude" <note>original: "sa‘at mashriq," the angular distance of a rising body from the true East</note> of the degrees when it rises, and a "western amplitude" of the degrees when it sets. Finally, each sign has its "nature"—whether it is fiery, airy, watery, or earthy. I shall provide an example for you so that it may be easy for you to memorize.

**Example:** The sign of Aries:
Its inclination is <term>12</term> <note>Abjad: "YB"</note> degrees, which is twelve degrees. Its sine is <term>30</term> <note>Abjad: "L"</note> degrees, which is thirty degrees. Its daylight hours when the sun resides in this sign are <term>12</term> <note>Abjad: "YB"</note> hours, which is <unclear>twelve</unclear>. Its altitude <unclear>when</unclear> the sun enters this sign: the altitude of its <unclear>beginning</unclear> is <term>60</term> <note>Abjad: "S"</note> degrees, which is sixty degrees. Its ascension is <term>21</term> <note>Abjad: "KA"</note> degrees, which is twenty <note>The text says twenty, though the Abjad numeral "KA" represents 21</note> degrees. Its descension is <term>35</term> <note>Abjad: "LH"</note> degrees, which is thirty-five degrees. Its eastern amplitude is <term>0</term> <note>Abjad: "A" with a mark</note>, meaning nothing—no degrees or anything else. Its western amplitude is <term>0</term> <note>Abjad: "A" with a mark</note>, zero—meaning nothing, no degrees or otherwise. This mark is called "zero" <note>original: "sifr," the origin of the English word "cipher"</note>, meaning "nothing" here.

Know that if this zero is in the place of degrees, then there are no degrees there. If it is in the place of minutes, then there are no minutes there. If it is in the place of hours, then there are no hours there. Use this same logic: wherever this zero <unclear>falls</unclear>, nothing exists in its place. Know that this sign is fiery.

This explanation covers the sign of Aries alone. Explaining the rest of the signs at length would be tedious, so I shall <unclear>draw</unclear> a circle for you and write within it the twelve zodiac signs and what pertains to each sign. Take this from the circumference of the circle so that it may be easy for the beginner to memorize without exhaustion or toil. I have only placed this circle out of a desire for this noble science—so understand, and you shall be guided. The charted circle follows on the next page.

# Section

**Know—may God guide us and you—** that regarding the ten celestial spheres <note>In medieval Islamic astronomy, these typically included the spheres of the seven known planets, the fixed stars, the zodiac, and the "Atlas" or "Starless" outer sphere.</note> mentioned previously, I intended to illustrate them in another place and add to them what I shall now mention. I have chosen to draw them as seven spheres for the seven wandering planets <term>planets: original: "al-kawakib al-sayyara," literally 'the wandering stars'</term>, the sphere of the twelve zodiac signs, the sphere of the fixed stars mentioned before, and the Greatest Sphere <note>The "Falak al-A‘zam," believed to be the outermost sphere that drives the daily rotation of the entire universe.</note>, in the manner previously described. I have set within the sphere of the zodiac twelve signs, writing their names within it and dividing it into three hundred and sixty degrees—thirty degrees for each sign. I have also placed what belongs to each sign from the twenty-eight Lunar Mansions <note>The "Manazil al-Qamar," a system of dividing the sky based on the moon's daily progress.</note> and the forms of their stars as well, so that it may be easier for you to memorize them when you look upon them. I have placed in the center of it—and for whichever sphere of fixed stars—their two forms <unclear>in a great image</unclear>. I shall <unclear>set out</unclear> to mention to you examples of that.

**The example** is that I <unclear>begin</unclear> with the sign of **Aries** <note>original: "al-Hamal"</note>. I have assigned to it the Lunar Mansions of *al-Sharatayn* <note>The "Two Signs," identified with the stars Beta and Gamma Arietis.</note>, *al-Butayn* <note>The "Little Belly," identified with Delta and Epsilon Arietis.</note>, and *al-Thurayya* <note>The Pleiades star cluster.</note>. Among the fixed stars, there is a star called *Kaff al-Khadib* <note>The "Stained Hand," referring to the star Beta Cassiopeiae.</note>, which is of the first magnitude <note>A measurement of a star's brightness; "first magnitude" denotes the brightest stars.</note>. 

Know that the stars of *al-Sharatayn* consist of two bright stars, and below and to the left of them is a small star. The stars of *al-Butayn* consist of three bright stars that resemble the head of a steelyard balance <note>original: "sab‘at al-qabban," a type of weighing scale with a beam and a sliding weight.</note> when opened equally, with no other stars near them. 

As for the stars of *al-Thurayya* (the Pleiades), they are six stars: three bright ones in a single horizontal row, two below them of lesser light, and one below those two which is the brightest of them all. This brightest star is of the second magnitude and is called by the masters of timekeeping <term>timekeeping: original: "arbab al-mawaqit," astronomers responsible for determining prayer times</term> the *‘Ayyuq* of the Pleiades <note>Likely referring to the star Alcyone, here distinguished from the more famous 'Ayyuq (Capella).</note>. It resembles a *sanbusakah* <note>A triangular pastry similar to a modern samosa.</note> with three corners; the corner containing the bright star—which is the *‘Ayyuq* of the Pleiades—tilts toward the right. 

This is the explanation of the sign of Aries and its three mansions, an explanation in full detail; if I were to explain it all [at once], it would be difficult for you to memorize. However, I intended to simplify it so that its memorization might be easy <unclear>in what follows in this list</unclear>.

### Section: Know—may God guide us and you—that the Moon traverses one mansion every day,
and it traverses a zodiac sign in approximately two and one-third days. This has been mentioned previously—
meaning the mansions and their boundaries within the Zodiac. I shall now mention the twelve signs of the Zodiac
and the twenty-eight mansions <term>al-manazil: the 28 divisions of the sky through which the Moon passes in its monthly cycle</term>, and how the Moon traverses them during its course over a period of 
approximately thirty days. I have detailed this in tables to make it easier for you 
to memorize when you look at them. I will give you an example of this. **The example:** should the 
Moon be in the mansion of *al-Sharatayn* <note>original: "the two signs" — located in the constellation Aries</note>, which is the first of the mansions of the sign of Aries, it remains 
before setting for **1** and **11** sevenths <note>The text uses Abjad numerals where "Alif" is 1 and "Ya-Alif" is 11; the "sevenths" refer to a specific medieval division of the hour</note>. It then sets, which is one hour, one-sixth of 
an hour, and one-sixtieth of an hour. On the second night, it will be in the mansion of *al-Butayn* <note>original: "the little belly" — also in Aries</note>; 
it remains before setting for **2** and **8** sevenths and then sets <unclear>two hours</unclear> 
<unclear>and a sixth</unclear> <unclear>of an hour</unclear> <unclear>and quarters</unclear> <unclear>of an hour</unclear>. On the third night, it will 
be in the mansion of *al-Thurayya* <note>The Pleiades</note>, as it leaves Taurus and remains before 
setting for **3** and **9** sevenths, and then it sets, which is three hours 
and three-quarters of a fifth of an hour. Follow this calculation and you will be guided.

**And know**, may God guide us and you, that the Moon rises on the first night of the second 
half of the month after **1** and **11** sevenths of the night has passed—which is one hour, 
one-sixth of an hour, and one-sixtieth of an hour. It continues its cycle until the end of that night, 
when it will be in the mansion of *al-Ghafr* <note>original: "the covering" — a mansion in the constellation Libra</note> at the beginning of the sign of Libra, approximately. And God knows best what is right. 
The explanation here would be long, and I only omitted the full explanation so that the burden of memorization would not be too heavy. I shall 
draw tables for you and write headings for them to make it easier for you to memorize them when 
you look into them. You can follow this calculation, which is made accessible to the mind, as 
others have <unclear>recorded</unclear> it before me, so that you may understand it without fatigue or hardship. The 
twelve signs of the Zodiac and the twenty-eight mansions have been mentioned previously as they 
should be; I mention them here again so that the time for memorizing the [astronomical] structures is near at hand.

<margin>On knowing the <term>Terms</term> <note>original: *al-hudud*; these are specific segments of a Zodiac sign ruled by a planet</note> of the seven planets, God willing</margin>
...of the twelve [signs]. Know—may God guide us and you—that there are seven wandering planets. Their names, the first of them being: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. Now, the Sun and the Moon have no "Terms" within the Zodiac signs. As for the other five, each one of them has a "Term" within the twelve signs. Each sign consists of thirty degrees, and these thirty degrees are divided among these five planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury. These are the "Owners of the Terms."

Know that for the sign of Aries, Saturn’s term is five degrees, Jupiter’s term is six degrees, Mars’s term is five degrees, Venus’s term is six degrees, and Mercury’s term is eight degrees. Thus, the total becomes thirty degrees, and they have their degrees within Aries. I have already set this out for you in tables on the face of this leaf <note>Referring to the table on the previous page</note> before this explanation. I only placed these tables in this book because you might be asked about a person’s <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: *tali'*; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, its specific term, and its degree; therefore, let this be in your memory, that you may be guided.

### Chapter on Knowing the <term>Watchers</term> of the Ascendants and the <term>Faces</term>

Know—may God guide us and you—that the Zodiac signs are based on the number of degrees in the celestial sphere, which is 360 degrees. These constitute 36 <term>Faces</term> <note>original: *wujuh*; also known in Western astrology as "Decans," which are 10-degree subdivisions of a sign</note>. Each "Face" is ten degrees. Every "Face" has a "Watcher" <note>original: *nazir*; the planetary regent or ruler of that specific decan</note> that looks upon it. 

**Example**: The sign of Aries is thirty degrees and consists of three "Faces," meaning it has three "Watchers." 
The First Face—meaning the first ten degrees—is under the watch of Mars, because he is the Lord of the House <note>Mars is the primary ruler of Aries</note>. 
The Second Face—meaning the second ten degrees—is under the watch of the Sun, because what lies beneath the sphere of Mars is the sphere of the Sun. 
The Third Face—meaning the third ten degrees—is under the watch of Venus, because what lies beneath the sphere of the Sun is the sphere of Venus. 

Following this calculation, take every "Watcher" and every "Face" one by one. Any degree that does not complete a set of ten is considered a degree within that Face. **Example**: You might say to a person whose Ascendant is Aries and whose Mars is at the eighth degree: "[It is] under the watch of Mars, within the Term of Venus." Understand, and you shall be guided. I will illustrate tables for you to make it easier for you to memorize what follows on this leaf.

# Tables of the Great <term>Abjad</term> Calculation System
<note>The Abjad system is a decimal alphabetic numeral system in which the 28 letters of the Arabic alphabet are assigned numerical values. It was widely used by scientists, astronomers, and diviners in the medieval Islamic world.</note>

| Alif (ا) | Ba (ب) | Jim (ج) | Dal (د) | Ha (هـ) | Waw (و) | Zay (ز) | Ha (ح) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| One | Two | Three | Four | Five | Six | Seven | Eight |

| Ta (ط) | Ya (ي) | Kaf (ك) | Lam (ل) | Mim (م) | Nun (ن) | Sin (س) | 'Ayn (ع) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nine | Ten | Twenty | Thirty | Forty | Fifty | Sixty | Seventy |

| Fa (ف) | Sad (ص) | Qaf (ق) | Ra (ر) | Shin (ش) | Ta (ت) | Tha (ث) | Kha (خ) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eighty | Ninety | One Hundred | Two Hundred | Three Hundred | Four Hundred | Five Hundred | Six Hundred |

| Dhal (ذ) | Dad (ض) | Za (ظ) | Ghayn (غ) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seven Hundred | Eight Hundred | Nine Hundred | One Thousand |

Know—may God guide us and you—that the values of this Great <term>Abjad</term> <note>original: *al-Jumal al-Kabir*</note> range from the number one to one thousand. Understand this calculation system, for it is the standard relied upon for arithmetic counts. These numbers are used in all <term>timekeeping operations</term> <note>original: *al-miqatiyat*; refers to astronomical calculations for prayer times, calendars, and planetary positions</note>. It is also the system used to calculate the value of the questioner’s name and their mother’s name <note>A common practice in horary astrology to determine a person's "ascendant" or "fortune" when their exact birth time is unknown</note>, through which one reaches the ultimate degree. 

Know that every letter and its corresponding number is written in a cell <note>original: *bayt*; literally "house," meaning the table cell</note> beneath it. However, for these last four letters, their numbers are in the cells following them. **Example:** the letter *Alif* <note>OCR text reads *Dhal*, likely a transcription error for *Alif*</note> stands for one, while the letter *Ghayn* <note>OCR reads *'Ayn*</note> stands for one thousand. The symbol for *Alif* is placed below it, and the symbol for *Ghayn* is placed behind it. This <term>Abjad</term> sequence is read as follows: *Ab-jad, Ha-waz, Hut-ti, Kal-man, Sa'-fas, Qa-ra-shat, Tha-khidh, Da-dagh* <note>original: *abjad hawwaz hutta kalman sa'fas qarashat thakhidh dadagh*; these are meaningless mnemonic words used to remember the order of the letters</note>. This is the standard alphabetic form; understand it, and you shall be guided.

**Chapter**

Know—may God guide us and you—that the sun traverses one degree every day. It traverses a single zodiac sign over a period of one month, consisting of thirty days. Thus, the total number of zodiac signs is twelve, and the total number of degrees in the celestial sphere is three hundred and sixty. It completes its journey through the sphere in one full year.

This is according to an approximate calculation. Scholars observed and calculated this based on the number of days in the Coptic months because the Coptic year consists of three hundred and sixty days, with each Coptic month lasting thirty days. However, they added five or six days to the Coptic year, and these are called the <term>Nasi</term> <note>The "Epagomenal" or intercalary days added at the end of the year to keep the calendar in sync with the solar cycle.</note>. 

The reason for this is that the Arabic months <note>The Hijri or Islamic lunar calendar.</note> begin with the month of al-Muharram, which is thirty days, followed by the second month, Safar, which is twenty-nine days. Thus, one month is "complete" and the next is "deficient" based on the sighting of the crescent moon. This is what is called the "Arabic Year."

<warning>Water damage/staining obscuring parts of the middle lines</warning>

<unclear>...ry</unclear> and its months; one month is completed and one is decreased from the month of al-Muharram until the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. They added what remained of these deficient days to the Coptic months and called them <unclear>the Nasi</unclear>. They then applied this "intercalary" addition to the zodiac signs and aligned the days of dawn and the basis of the degrees of the signs with these Coptic intercalary days. At that point, the calculation of the dawn and the sun’s degrees was completed, as was previously mentioned at the beginning of this book regarding the rules of the tables.

**Know**—may God guide us and you—that I wished to compile for you in this book the Coptic months, the zodiac signs, and the sun's degrees through an approximate calculation. This is to make it easier for you to memorize than the previous method. I shall write them at the headers of the tables, and I will mention examples of this for you.

**An example:** On the first day of the month of Thout <note>The first month of the Coptic calendar, roughly September.</note>, the sun is at the <term>14th</term> <note>original: "يد" - Arabic Abjad numerals where Yā' = 10 and Dāl = 4.</note> degree, and it is in the <term>6th</term> <note>original: "و" - Abjad numeral for 6.</note> zodiac sign—meaning the sign of Virgo—having already traversed fourteen degrees of it. 

On the first day of the month of Babah <note>The second Coptic month, roughly October.</note>, the sun is at the <term>14th</term> <note>original: "يد"</note> degree, and it is in the <term>7th</term> <note>original: "زا" - Abjad numeral for 7.</note> sign—meaning the sign of Libra—and it has traversed fourteen dawns according to this calculation. A full explanation would be too long for a beginner to memorize.

<margin>If you wish to know the maximum altitude <note>The highest point the sun reaches in the sky at midday.</note>, add the partial declination <term>the sun's angular distance north or south of the celestial equator</term> to the complement of the latitude <note>90 degrees minus the observer's latitude</note>, and the requirement will be fulfilled.</margin>

**Chapter on knowing the beginning of the time of the Afternoon Prayer, if you wish for that**

Subtract the maximum altitude of your day from 90 degrees and eighty-three degrees <note original="وثلاثة وثمانون درجه">The mention of "83 degrees" here is likely a scribal error or a specific regional constant; the subsequent example follows the standard method of subtracting from 90.</note>. From what remains of the 90 degrees, take one-tenth and add it to half of the day's maximum altitude. The resulting sum is the altitude for the beginning of the time of the Afternoon Prayer (Asr).

**An example** of that: On the first day of the month of Tut <term>the first month of the Coptic calendar, roughly September</term>, the sun has traversed fourteen degrees of the sign of Virgo. The maximum altitude on that day is 64 degrees and 1 minute <note>The text adds "which is sixty-six degrees and thirty minutes," which may be a clarification of a different calculation or a transcription error in the original manuscript.</note>. We subtract 64 from 90, and 26 remains. We take one-tenth of it, which is 2 and 36 minutes <note original="آو لآ">Written in Abjad numerals as 1 and 31, though the math suggests 2.6.</note>, and add it to half of the day’s altitude, which is 32 degrees and 1 minute. The total sum is **34 degrees and 54 minutes**. We rounded it by approximation to **35** degrees, which is the value placed in the beginning of the table for the degrees of the Afternoon Prayer altitude on the first day of the month of Tut. This rule is constant and eternal.

**Chapter on knowing which zodiac sign the Moon is in and how many degrees it has traversed within it**

If you wish for that, take the days of the crescent moon—meaning from the start of the [lunar] month you are in up to the current day. Whatever number of days you have, multiply them by 2 days. From the resulting sum of days, assign one zodiac sign for every 30 days. Begin counting from the sign in which the Sun is currently located. The sign where the count ends is the one the Moon is in. The remaining number of days, which did not reach 30, represents the degrees the Moon has covered in that sign. Understand, and you shall be guided.

**Chapter on knowing the Ascendant sign and degree, if you wish**

For that, assign one zodiac sign for every two hours. For any duration less than two hours, calculate the proportional share of the sign and degrees. **An example** of this: one hour is 15 degrees, two hours is 30 degrees, and one zodiac sign is 30 degrees. Thus, every thirty degrees corresponds to two hours, and every zodiac sign is thirty degrees. Increase your calculation based on this, and understand, and you shall be guided.

### Chapter 8: On knowing which sign the sun is in and how many degrees it has traveled through it
If you wish to know this, take the days of the **Coptic year** <note>The Coptic calendar was widely used by medieval Egyptian astronomers and farmers for its solar consistency.</note> from the first day of the month of **Thoth** <note original="توت">Tut</note> until the day you are currently in. Always add 163 days to it (one hundred and sixty-three days). From the total you have gathered, always subtract 30 days for each sign (thirty days). Begin your count from the first sign, **Aries** <note original="الحمل">al-Hamal</note>. The sign where the count ends is the sign the sun is currently in, and it has traveled through that sign by the number of days remaining with you.

**An example of this:**
If ten days have passed in the month of **Thoth** (which is 10), we add one hundred and sixty-three days (163) to it. The total becomes one hundred and seventy-three days (173). We then subtract thirty days for each sign (represented by the letter *L* <note original="ل">The Abjad numeral for 30.</note>), which results in a division of five signs (5). There remains a remainder of twenty-three days (23). Thus, the sun is in the sixth sign, which is **Virgo**, and it has traveled through it by twenty-three degrees (23 degrees). The accuracy of this has been previously established in the tables and elsewhere. Understand, and you will find your way.

### Chapter on the Knowledge of Multiplication, Division, and Calculation

### On Knowing Miles and the Four Quarters; Know—May God Guide Us and You

Know that the <term>Mile <gloss>Al-Mil</gloss></term> is 4,000 <term>Cubits <gloss>Dira'</gloss></term>, and the Cubit is 24 <term>Fingers <gloss>Isba'</gloss></term>. The Finger is 6 <note>original: ٦</note> <term>Barleycorns <gloss>Sha'ira</gloss></term>—meaning twelve <note>original: اثني عشر</note> barleycorns—and the Barleycorn is 6 <note>original: ٦</note> hairs—meaning ten <note>original: عشرة</note> hairs <note>These discrepancies between the numerals (6) and the written words (12 and 10) may reflect different regional standards or a scribal error in the original manuscript.</note>. These hairs are to be taken from the middle of a horse's tail.

Know that the circumference of the Earth is 24,000 miles <note>original: ٢٤٠٠٠</note>, which is <unclear>twenty-four thousand</unclear> <note>The OCR text "الفين واربعة" suggests "two thousand and four," but this is a likely error for the standard scientific value of 24,000 used in this period.</note> miles of the type previously mentioned. One degree of the degrees of the Earth is 66 2/3 miles—which is sixty-six miles and two-thirds of a mile. God knows best; understand, and you shall be guided.

### On Knowing the First Day of the Great Month of Ramadan and the First Day of Arafat

Regarding the Arabic months, know—may God guide us and you—that the fifth day of the month of <term>al-Muharram <gloss>The first month of the Islamic calendar.</gloss></term> will be the <term>Day of Standing <gloss>Yawm al-Waqfa</gloss></term> <note>The pivotal day of the Hajj pilgrimage at Mount Arafat.</note>, and the sixth day of it will be the first day of the month of Ramadan. I will mention an example for you.

**Example:** If the first day of the month of al-Muharram is a Thursday, then its fifth day is Monday, which will be the Day of Standing at Arafat. Its sixth day from the third of Muharram <note>The text likely refers to the sixth day relative to the start of the week.</note> will be the first day of the Great Month of Ramadan.
