### On Knowing Certain Meanings and Inquiries into the Science of Timekeeping

This knowledge is beneficial before entering [the study of] the <term>Azimuth <gloss>Al-Samt</gloss></term>. The Azimuth is an arc of the circle of the horizon between the eastern point of the equinox to the degree reached by the azimuth from the circle of...

--- Page 263 ---
<meta>This page serves as the concluding section of the manuscript. It transitions from the geographic measurements of the previous page back to the celestial sphere, providing formal geometric and astronomical definitions. The text concludes with a formal colophon, naming the scribe and the date of completion.</meta>

[the horizon] either to the north or to the south. This measure reached by the azimuth never exceeds ninety degrees.

**As for the azimuthal circle**, it is the circle that passes through the <term>Zenith <gloss>Samt al-Ra’s</gloss></term>, the <term>Nadir <gloss>Samt al-Rijl</gloss></term>, the body of the star, and the point on the horizon reached by the azimuth.

**As for the arc of altitude**, it is an arc of this azimuthal circle between the body of the star and the location on the horizon reached by the azimuth.

**As for the arc of complementary altitude**, it is the remainder of the arc of altitude on this circle, between the body of the star and the zenith. <note>In modern astronomy, this is often called the 'zenith distance'.</note>

**As for the arc of complementary azimuth**, it is a segment of the horizon circle between the point reached by the azimuth on the horizon and where it ends at ninety degrees.

**As for the sphere**, it is a solid enclosed by a single surface, within which is a point such that all lines drawn from it to the surface are equal; that point is called the center of the sphere.

**As for the diameter of the sphere**, it is the straight line that passes through the center of the sphere and ends at both sides of the surface surrounding the sphere.

**As for the axis of the sphere**, it is the diameter upon which the sphere rotates and which divides the sphere into two halves.

**As for the zone**, it is the great parallel circles perpendicular to the axis at right angles.

**As for the time circles**, they are the temporal circles for the region of the <term>Celestial Equator <gloss>Mu‘addil al-Nahar</gloss></term> from the region of the highest sphere, containing the poles of the world and the poles of the highest sphere.

**As for the circle** which the sun traces by its motion from the east to the west: if its plane is imagined to intersect the world, it creates a great circle on the surface of the highest sphere. This circle is called the <term>Zodiac <gloss>Mintaqat Falak al-Buruj</gloss></term> <note>Known today as the Ecliptic.</note>, and its poles are the poles of the Zodiac.

God knows best. The chapters and sections are finished; they are twenty chapters and twenty sections, following one after another. This is the science, and God is the Granter of success in reaching the truth.

The book *The Pearls and Rubies of the Science of Observation and Timekeeping* <note>original: "al-Durar wa al-Yawaqit fi ‘Ilm al-Rasd wa al-Mawaqit"</note> was completed by the hand of the humble servant **Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sabir**, by the praise of God, His help, His good success, and His favor. This was in the latter part of the honored month of <term>Sha‘ban <gloss>The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.</gloss></term> in the year seven hundred and thirty-four. <note>This date, late Sha‘ban 734 AH, corresponds to approximately late April or early May 1334 CE.</note> May God bless our master Muhammad, his family, and his companions, and grant them peace.

O God, what You have bestowed, complete it; what You have given, do not take it away; what You have concealed, do not expose it; and what You have known [of my sins], forgive it, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy. May God bless our master Muhammad the Prophet, and all his family and companions.

Do not carry the anxiety of one who does not carry your anxiety, and be patient, for perhaps your grief will fade. # The Omen of Warning and Conduct

He has told you in this omen <note>Arabic: *fal*—a method of divination or seeking an augury</note> that all evil and misery come from you, so do not be ill-natured. Do not occupy yourself with carrying tales, for everyone who strives in slander <note>Arabic: *namima*—malicious gossip intended to sow discord</note> possesses despicable traits. You have transgressed against them, leaving nothing behind and sparing no one. Therefore, be patient and do not hurry, for with the hasty comes the slip <note>original: *al-zalal*—a mistake or moral lapse caused by rushing</note>. Do not listen to your adversary, nor obey his words. You have begun to dig up things that were and things that never were; you will fall into evil from every direction. Avoid the enmity of your neighbors and beware of misery in your own place. Others have opposed you in your path, and you have become distressed because of your seeking. You have spoken to yourself of traveling because of the harm that has occurred. Evil does not last, so do not carry worries and put your trust in the Living, the Eternal <note>Arabic: *al-Hayy al-Qayyum*—two of the Beautiful Names of God in Islamic tradition</note>. For there is not one of you except that he has a known station. Do not oppose the people of knowledge <note>referring to scholars or those with spiritual insight</note>, or you will fall and never rise again.

It has been written for you in your omen <note>The word 'fal' refers to a divination or a prognostic reading of one's fortune</note>, my brother, that you will face confrontations with them. # The Omen of the Letters Ayn, Jim, and Ra

It is written in your omen: make your words the best they can be and improve your circumstances. Be attentive to your affairs and do not be deceived by others, lest your goodness be wasted upon the children of the ignoble <note>The "ignoble" or "base-born" refers to those lacking in character or gratitude.</note>. Listen, O seeker of the omen, to your warning: avoid your [current] aim and do not be stubborn <term>Azuwar: a person who is difficult, stubborn, or turns away from the truth</term>. Do not lean upon false speech, and be cautious regarding yourself. 

There is no avoiding what has been divinely decreed <note>original: "al-maqdur" — the destiny already written by God</note>. Comply with what has been judged for you, for this is what the warner has prescribed for you. I see that you have placed yourself in a state of deficiency <note>The text here is partially obscured by a paper repair; "ikhtilal" suggests a state of disorder or lack</note>, yet you have acted kindly toward others and spoken of their good qualities behind their backs. 

The paths of this world are wondrous and its conditions are ordered, yet at all times the son of Adam <note>A common poetic term for humanity</note> is afflicted by it; rarely does he land upon what is right. The wise person is one who walks the safe paths so that their affairs remain straight. Therefore, O seeker of the omen, ask your Lord for safety, for how quickly the days of time <term>Dahr: fate or cyclical time</term> turn over! Listen to this speech and its rulings:

# Discourse on the Letter Alif
# Discourse on the Letter Ba

Rejoice, for you have been given glad tidings of blessings, happiness, joy, and ease.
The one whose station is above the North <note>Likely referring to a high celestial or spiritual rank</note> has appeared; do not weary yourself with grief, O you who sit in toil.
If you have come to ask about the fulfillment of needs, they shall be granted without hardship or fatigue.
If you fear the outcome of affairs, do not be afraid, for you have sought the path of the fortunate.
If you have come to ask about a sick person, the Lord of Heaven has singled them out for healing.
Whether you are engaged in a legal case or traveling, O youth, you are victorious over your enemies.
Whether you enter a partnership, or sell and buy, rise up to attain happiness and your goals.
If you seek the interpretation of a dream, it is good, a guidance, and a beautiful light.
If you have come to ask about a blessed marriage, rejoice in the union with a beautiful person.
the Omen <note>original: *al-Fāl*</note> has informed us with a truthful promise in the text of a chapter of great brilliance.
**Alif** is the first of the letters that brought good news, so thank the God of the Throne, the Owner of Blessings.

<column-break/>

Good news for you! You have attained all your requests and goals, and your efforts lead to happiness and achievement.
The star of luck has risen, its precursors have appeared, its justice has been made manifest, and it is evident in every trial.
Hasten to the Chosen One <note>original: *al-Mukhtār*; a title for the Prophet Muhammad</note> when you ask; what you have sought is the truth, without a lie.
The signs of glory and success have appeared to you, so rise for them, O you of pure lineage.
Buy and sell, enter partnerships, litigate, and move, for you have attained what you hope for without any exhaustion.
By God, do not hesitate in a legal matter, and do not fall short of your resolve and your objective.
The suns of the forenoon have risen with luck, turning like a wheel that never fails.
Why stop at a matter you are pursuing? Rise to a rank that towers above all other ranks.
The Generous Lord has created a path for you, so take the omen and see its judgment—it is the most wondrous of wonders.
Through it, you shall find acceptance and then honor from all the Turks, the Persians, and the Arabs. <note>This triad was a common literary way of saying "the whole world."</note>
The letter **Ba** brings glad tidings, and it is worthy of being written on scrolls of silk and gold.

---

# Discourse on the Letter Ta
# Discourse on the Letter Tha

The hand of justice is established among all beings, and your envious opponent is struck with loss.
Goodness is abundant and happiness has arrived, as luck hastens from all directions.
Blessed is God the Almighty, who gave you beautiful qualities in this world.
Trade, marry, perform the pilgrimage, travel, grow, dwell, and move—do not fear any separation.
In this year, you shall visit the tomb of the Prophet Muhammad, greetings to the one of miracles.
You shall recite the chapters "The Morning Brightness" and "Praise" <note>original: *al-Duḥā* and *al-Ḥamd*; refers to Surahs 93 and 1 of the Quran</note> when you see your enemies and the envious in the throes of defeat.
You shall find acceptance from all people and rise to the highest stations.
You shall be happy, honored, promoted, and successful; you shall build, find joy, and rejoice in the arrival of daughters.
You shall begin a life by attaining your desires; the intent in these words is like the falling of rain.
You shall decide, judge, command, find, rule, attain, be guided, and be upright; you shall be elevated by receiving blessings.
The letter **Ta** of the script has brought good news, so give thanks to Him who revives the decayed bones.

<column-break/>

Trust in your affairs with God, the Inheritor <note>original: *al-Wārith*; one of the Names of God in Islam</note>; do not fear the plot of the treacherous, envious person.
The light of the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> is tripled by a moon-like appearance; so take your gain from it as a third party.
Your eyes are cooled <note>An Arabic idiom for being deeply happy and satisfied</note> when they are settled on your desires, and you are safe from the evil of the trifling envious one.
Your foundations are firm in happiness and high status; you have remained in glory, and what a fine dweller you are.
You have worn the garment of happiness anew; so rise with determination, O brave lion <note>original: *al-Hazabr al-Ḥārith*</note>.
I have refined my script... <unclear>happening</unclear> or a disaster.
Their heads have been submitted to you as if they swore an oath and then came with a false testimony.
The swords of the attackers have been blunted, so do not fear, and place your certainty in God, the Inheritor.
Mothers have lost your rivals, for they desired madness even if it were in the growing child.
The letter **Tha** of the alphabet is said to be excellent, in a poetic arrangement from an eloquent, inspired breath.

# Discourse on the Letter Jim
# Discourse on the Letter Ha <note>These two headings appear together in the source, though the following verses specifically emphasize the letter Jim.</note>

Beautify your patience so that you may escape from distress, if you fear burning or the descent into hardship.
The worries of time have oppressed you, so endure them; be steadfast and do not be disturbed.
The neighbors of your heart in all matters have come forth, appearing to mankind <note>original: "lūri," likely a transcription error for "al-warā" meaning mankind</note> in the midst of the bustle of distress.
The beautiful veil of the God of the Throne is lowered, so do not trouble your day with thoughts of deep waters.
You unsheathed your sword with the beloved in passion; turn back, for how many souls have been lost in love.
You have committed a sin, so repent for it; if you return to it, you will be in loss and low standing.
You have gathered wealth, so do not hope for mere dealings; do you expect to sell pearls for black stone <note>term: "sabaj" refers to jet or a black bead of little value, contrasted here with "durr" or pearls</note>?
Avoid the company of the base and be thrifty; you will rise by attaining your desires to the highest ranks.
Strive in your journey toward beautiful patience; perhaps your era, once crooked, will become straight.
I have polished the pearls of this arrangement upon the pages, and they have become clear to me in the Omen <note>original: "al-Fāl"</note> and clear in the pilgrimage.
The letter **Jim** has come as a messenger to the heart, and soon God will bring relief.

# Discourse on the Letter Kha

Fear God with a heart in which worry has grown old; how many a close one has set a trap for the lover?
O my friend, the fires of rejection have been kindled, and the bellows have blown the embers within.
Take counsel from my words and be steadfast, for the stagnation of thought within you is fading.
The gardens of the nights of rejection have grown long, and the dawns of the days of happiness are looming.
The betrayal of enemies and the cunning of the envious—by His success, the elders have untied these knots.
The poverty of the possessors of intellect is their patience, when the cries of calamity break at dawn.
Lost is the one who does not make patience a shield, while noble and lofty lineages rise above him.
Take heed of the warning and the advice, and listen to what has been inscribed by the pens, rooted in the pages.
The tables of God’s kindness are beautiful; wine for its meaning is found in the lofty peaks of beauty.
One who is expert in the measures of this arrangement has set the rows of pearl necklaces, and he is proficient in knowledge.
The hidden nature of the letter **Kha** is the increase of its expansion; its richness appears in the brilliant pages.

<column-break/>

A good omen <note>original: "fāl"</note> has come to you with delight, with the persistence of success and joys.
The rule of the omen is that you should make your intellect a sharp sword of character in the forehead of the morning.
Perform the pilgrimage, enter a partnership, set your intention, marry, and depart; take legal action or settle, and you shall proceed by attaining success.
Far be it from a namesake or a worker to be indebted; you are not watched with any blame in what you take.
Wherever you are, you shall live happily; so thank God, the splitter of the dawn.
Your purpose and desire have been achieved, so rejoice, and be filled with every goodness and wine <note>The mention of "rāḥ" (wine) often symbolizes spiritual intoxication or pure joy in this context.</note>.
The cup of bliss has been struck by the evening cup; for you is the evening drink and the morning draught.
The resolve of the enemies has been undone, and in their pride they died, with hearts weighted down by wounds.
Good fortune has judged, so listen to it as poetry, and enjoy yourself in both seriousness and jest.
May God guard this threshold, and may it never cease to be like the full moon of the dark and the sun of the morning.
The ruling of the letter **Ha** indicates the goal, the attainment of desires, and union with the beautiful.

# Discourse on the Letter Dal

The persistence of joys and a new happiness, the decrease of worry and the increase of gladness.
The caller of goodness has summoned you, so respond to him; the omen has called to it, seeking the elevation you desire.
May blessings and happiness endure for you, through gratitude to God, the All-Powerful, the Glorious.
The celestial spheres <note>term: "dawā'ir al-aflāk" refers to the movement of the planets and stars believed to influence human fate</note> have turned with what you choose, so resolve with a sound opinion.
The beloved has drawn near to you after estrangement, writing from the station of the lowest of servants.
Lend, marry, perform the pilgrimage, settle, read, take legal action, and trade; every deed is praiseworthy.
Plan, for in planning is all satisfaction; and strive, for in striving are matters that bring benefit.
The circles of evil have turned upon the necks of your enemies until the Day of Promise.
May blessings and happiness endure for you in all that you live, with a new lightning-flash of brilliance.
I have arranged the pearls of my system for you; in every house of it is a "house of poetry" <note>A pun on the word "bayt," which means both a house/home and a verse of poetry.</note>.
The letter **Dal** has brought tidings of goodness and joy; so rejoice, for this omen is a happy omen.

# Discourse on the Letter Dhal <note>Though the heading says "Dal," the following verses all begin with the letter "Dhal" (ذ), a common orthographic variation in divinatory manuscripts.</note>

You have humbled your enemies and attained your desires, and you shall live your whole life in pleasure.
Taste the sweetness of a pure life in grace, and rejoice in a provision that never runs out.
You have approached goodness and attained it like a torrential rain, while the envious one has met with reversal.
That which you feared, you have now overcome, and your steel sword is effective in its execution.
You have conquered your enemies and made them endure; the time of their defeat has come, and they have become as broken husks.
You have walked in the valley of piety; blessed is the one, my friend, who takes refuge in goodness.
The hearts of your enemies have melted, so rejoice in this; you have triumphed, while the envious one seeks refuge from you.
The Possessor of Bounty has granted you your wishes; so take His gift and thank Him for what you have received.
That is the bounty of God bestowed upon you, for you are in the protection of God the Most High.
This is a brief token of gratitude for His signs, which have caused the one who began [enmity] to be cast aside.
The peak of the letter **Dhal** has brought good tidings; so praise be to God for this outcome.

# Discourse on the Letter Ra

Discipline the souls and leave reports aside; be cautious, then be cautious!
Turn back from your opinion regarding what you aimed for, and be patient, for the consequence of patience is victory.
Relieve the heart from the causes of ruin, and gather the fruits of the most youthful thoughts.
Relief has appeared, yet worry has also come, along with a turning away from a beloved who has departed.
The thoughts of his days are spent in sorrow, and the night is filled with tears and sleeplessness.
The Lord of the Separation, my Lord is His name; He brought me trouble after a period of purity.
Time has returned with sorrowful thoughts, and then a gazelle <note>A common poetic metaphor for a beautiful beloved.</note> appeared and then fled.
You sought union with a blooming maiden; she will soon be revealed like the sun and the moon.
Give rest to your hearing with what I have said, and be patient, for patience is the best storehouse.
May God have mercy on a youth who hears what the Omen <note>original: "al-Fāl"</note> speaks as a warning and takes heed.
I have repeated the letter **Ra** for the seeker in its fragrance; thus the pearl of this full moon is completed.

# Discourse on the Letter Za

The flower of union has signaled uniqueness and appeared in a robe of continuous beauty.
Choose the flower you wish, for satisfaction has drawn near, and the return of loved ones is being fulfilled.
Marry, settle, move, or take a partner; join the tiller of the land or depart for the Hijaz.
You have visited the quarter of high status, so continue to ascend the ranks of dignity with pride.
The singers hummed with the best melodies when the celebration of good fortune was cut short <note>possibly meaning "reached its peak"</note>.
The ranks of beauty have adorned a bride; hasten to the sweetness of her union with speed.
Lead her home and do not fear the plot of a watcher, nor the plot of a whispering envious person.
The flower of the garden of desires has approached, and the truth of this word is literal, not metaphorical.
You have triumphed over those who oppose you; so listen to the resolution of the knots of symbols and riddles.
May God increase His bounty upon you, a grace and blessing without any confusion.
A messenger of glad tidings has come to the one visiting from sorrow; a transformation performed with eloquent meter.

<column-break/>

# Discourse on the Letter Sin

Ask your inner conscience about me, for I have been striking five against six <note>term: "ḍarb al-akhmās fī al-as dās," an idiom meaning to be deeply perplexed, confused, or calculating all possibilities.</note>.
They are distracted by their own forms and shapes; avoid in your mind the "six-sided" form <note>likely a reference to the material world or a specific geomantic figure.</note>.
Be at peace with people, be patient, and pause; avoid an oath that leads to bankruptcy.
Secure the door and do not be hasty; do not travel and do not build upon this foundation.
Walk in the secret of God in every matter; do not complain and do not strive in darkness.
Ask the worries to leave your heart for a while, away from these wanderings and the turning of the cup.
Aid your time with patience, and you will be safe from a strange flame and the hardship of trembling.
Be easy-going and do not be hasty; be patient regarding promises and struggles.
The Salsabil <note>term: "Salsabīl," a river in Paradise; here used to mean the purest, sweetest water.</note> of union will surely be revealed in cups that circulate in the darkness of night.
He who is patient shall rule with good fortune, until he reaches happiness among all people.
The examination of the letter **Sin** contains a warning; and with this, the paper has spoken. The Omen is currently pending.

# Discourse on the Letter Fa (ف)
# Discourse on the Letter Kaf (ك)

The moon of your desire is near; your union is slight, so leave it be. Like the shining moon that was once split <note>A reference to a miracle attributed to the Prophet Muhammad.</note> | Be as you wish, for there is no fault there; good fortune has appeared and your moon has brightened.
Your omen has come announcing auspiciousness; your signs are as clear as the twilight. | Whatever you aimed for, you have attained; so thank the Lord who fashioned you.
Tell the pigeon to sing in the pulpits of its thicket, reciting songs while the dew clothes the leaves. | What was has been; do not ask me about a beloved whose abandonment has changed you.
The sun of union has dawned with an appearance that shimmered, and the fragrance of morning became evident from— | The beautiful maidens have been adorned, so gaze upon them and polish your sight with them.
-> Love ['Ayn] <- | The clouds of the sky crowned the flowers of the hills; so enjoy the cup of bliss amidst your blooms.
May your eyes be cooled and settled with bliss; so praise the One who created mankind and provided sustenance. | Tell everyone who opposed you in ignorance: "Far be it! Glory to the Lord who raised you from your stumble."

# Discourse on the Letter Nun (ن)
Victory comes from God, the Powerful, the Firm; with might and triumph comes a clear opening.
May God grant you what you hope for, and may your enemies and the envious be disappointed.
The light of guidance has dawned in the East, so rejoice; visit the tomb of the Tihami, the Master of the Messengers. <note>al-Tihami: A title for the Prophet Muhammad, referring to the Tihamah region of the Arabian Peninsula.</note>

Your companion for victory in the struggle <note>original: "al-khumsha," possibly referring to a physical struggle or a specific legal dispute.</note> is a judgment in the council of the judges.

# Discourse on the Letter Waw (و)
I trusted people who were prone to evil; they made intentions, but their necks were bound by a firm bond.
Your omen has reached you, informing you that the branches of union have withered through patience.
Be patient, stay steadfast, and endure; you will reach your goals, for many souls have been scorched by wandering and separation.
Reach out, do not be hasty, and remain firm; for the devils among the slandering whisperers have gone astray.
How many lovers have they surrendered to destruction, and how many hearts have fallen in love's passion?
-> Concerning the Youth <-
Patience in all things is nothing but a gift, even if human intimacy seems to have folded away from you.
In a short while, resentment will clear away and be replaced by satisfaction, even if the enemies have settled near you.

This is the testament of a wise companion, so preserve it; it comes to you from the masters of knowledge who understood it.
Do not let hesitation move within your conscience; this is the advice of people who are the best for you.
The warning of the letter Waw has come to caution; it directs the affairs of the people of merit who have shown concern.

# Discourse on the Letter Ba (ب)

God accepts you, and by the Prophet’s sake, He relieves the calamities of a misbehaving fate.
It shows that this omen is auspicious, bringing signs of a delightful life.
The beloved shall connect with you, so rise quickly to attain the state of Joseph. <note>Refers to the "Josephic state" (al-hal al-Yusufi), symbolizing a transition from hardship or isolation to beauty, power, and reunion, as in the story of the Prophet Joseph.</note>
Marriage suits you; propose and marry to reveal the countenance of the radiant moon.
Good fortune has come toward wealth, seeking to bring you to the truth and a full purse.
His praise spreads through all of creation like the scent of musk and fragrant aloeswood.
The Lord helps you with every good, with bounty and hidden grace.
The year repairs its Kaaba; hasten to the House and visit the tomb of the Prophet. <note>This suggests a successful pilgrimage (Hajj) or a spiritual restoration.</note>
May He return to you the blessings of the Best of Creation, the Intercessor of Zamzam. <note>The "Intercessor of Zamzam" is a title for the Prophet Muhammad.</note>
May God prolong your life in virtue and protect you from the evil of the wicked and envious.
The script of the letter Ba brings good tidings, so rejoice in the arrival of sustenance and a clever child.
Completed with the praise of God the Almighty and His gracious success; praise be to God alone.

### Discourse on the Sign of Aries and Mars
A woman born under this sign will have beautiful skin, face, and eyes. She will have children and marry two husbands, finding much goodness and blessing from the second. She is quick to anger but quick to forgive. Her best days are Sunday and Monday, while her most harmful day is Friday. Most of her ailments will stem from "winds" <note>original: "ar-riyah," referring to bodily humors, gases, or rheumatic pains in medieval medicine</note>, and her remedy is red sugar, jujube, and rose water. She should remain obedient to her husband. A period of danger is feared for her at sixty <note>original: "thalathin," which could be thirty, but in this context likely means sixty (sitteen) or a specific age-related turning point</note> years of age, though her horoscope suggests she may live to eighty. One born under this sign should not cease the remembrance of God and should carry an amulet <note>original: "hirz"</note> because she has many enemies and there is fear for her from the Evil Eye. And God knows best the unseen and is the Most Wise.

### Discourse on the Sign of Taurus and Venus
A woman born under this sign will have a beautiful body and face. She loves conversing with people and will have "joined eyebrows" <note>considered a mark of beauty and strong character in various historical traditions</note>, large eyes, and a fine stature. Female livestock are favorable to her. She will have one husband and many children. Most of her ailments will be in the gut. She is sharp-tongued and quick to respond, though generally approachable. Her best day is Saturday, while her most harmful are Friday and certain months. It is preferable that her husband’s sign be Pisces or Cancer. Most of her ailments come from coldness, and her horoscope indicates she may die from a gut ailment. Her remedy is mastic <note>a resin from the pistachio tree used for digestion</note>. If she suffers from migraines, she should inhale the scent of Nile water <note>original: "ma' al-nil," likely referring to indigo-infused water or a specific herbal preparation</note> and must not sleep until sunrise. She has a mole on her chest or back; if there is a mole on her leg, she will be granted the Hajj pilgrimage. Danger is feared for her at seven years and twenty years; if she survives these, she may live to seventy years. And God knows best the unseen.

### On the Judgment of the Discourse on the Sign of Gemini and Mercury
As for a woman born under this sign, she will be tall with a beautiful face, but <unclear>impulsive</unclear> <note>original: "fajura," which can mean immoral or licentious, but here likely implies a bold or reckless temperament</note> and having little patience during times of joy. She is quick to answer, sharp-tempered, and possesses good fortune. She will hold sway over her husband and has a secret <unclear>concerning</unclear> a mole or a mark. She experiences fear <unclear>at night</unclear> because she sees dreams that frighten her; thus, she needs to have an amulet written for her containing the names of God the Almighty, and a protection ritual for the constant <unclear>remembrance</unclear>. She may suffer from "winds" in her gut; she should use "cat-remedy" suppositories <note>original: "ashyaf al-shananir," likely a technical term for a specific herbal suppository</note> and mallow seeds if she wishes to conceive. She should drink a concoction to induce menstruation if her flow is light. Her children will be male. She loves only what is right for her, her guardian, and her wealth, yet she has no luck with people. Death is feared for her when she is one year old; if she survives, then until eleven years; if she survives that, then until seventy years, four months, and nine hours. And God knows best.

### Discourse on the Sign of Cancer and the Moon
As for a woman born under this sign, she will have a radiant face, a beautiful image, and a sound mind. She must marry a man through whom she will find great happiness. She will be blessed with many children. When the new moon rises, she suffers from headaches; if it is summer, she should apply sandalwood paste to her head. In the world <note>or "In the medicine"</note>, "Devil’s Heads" <note>original: "ru’us al-shayatin," a common name for the herb Stachys or similar thorny plants</note> and garden cress will <unclear>benefit them</unclear> and cause the pain to cease. She should be careful during pregnancy, as heavy <unclear>eating</unclear> and <unclear>movement</unclear> do not suit her. She should have an amulet for "the falling" <note>likely referring to epilepsy or sudden fainting</note> and rebellious spirits, for there is fear for her from displacement and the "accidents of the year." It is not possible for her to have a husband unless he is completely satisfied with her. She is at risk of falling from a high place or from a difficult <unclear>affliction</unclear> in her youth. She has a mole or mark on her body. She has no luck with anyone and loves only the work she does and her own regrets. She has enemies, and her parents will be in a state of worry, though her mother is more beloved and honored by her.

### Statement on the Sign of Scorpio and Mars
->The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this rising sign will have a beautiful face<-
She has a pleasant character, a medium build, black eyes, a wide forehead, and strong forearms. She is introspective and has a strong heart. She carries herself like royalty and is soft-hearted, yet she has little patience and does not remain in one state for long. She has a sharp temperament, is quick to answer, quick to anger, and quick to be appeased. She loves herself and only loves those who provide for her. Regarding her sustenance and wealth, she has no luck from anyone else; however, as she grows older, her status and value increase. She has moles or birthmarks on her body. She loves fragrances, leisure, and joking. Cold weather does not suit her; heat is better for her. Most of her pains occur in her lower body, and vapors from her stomach rise to her head, causing a feeling of heaviness. She should be caught off guard <note>The text suggests a folk remedy of surprising a patient during a fainting spell or seizure</note> when she faints. Fear for her from the Evil Eye and the "look" of the envious. She has enemies and those who envy her. The Chapter of the Opening <note>Surah al-Fatiha</note> should be written for her. I seek refuge for the bearer of this, my writing, in God, besides whom there is no other god, the Lord of the Great Throne. I seek refuge for her by the Lord of Gabriel and Israfel <note>The archangels Jibra'il and Israfil</note> and the proximate angels of God, and by the right of these noble names: **O Living, I am that I am, Lord of Hosts, God Almighty** <note>original: "Ya Hayy, Ashrahiya, Adonai, Asba'ut, El Shaddai"; these are Arabic transliterations of Hebrew Divine Names used in Islamic theurgic traditions</note>. I protect her from the evil of every possessor of evil, from the Eye, the envious look, and from the evil of accidents, infirmities, and calamities, by the power of "There is no change or power except by God, the High, the Great." She faces a trial at four years of age. If she survives, then until fifteen; if she survives that, then until forty. If she passes that, she shall live for ninety-five years, and God knows best.

### Statement on the Sign of Sagittarius and Jupiter
The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this rising sign will have a beautiful face, a pleasant character, and a tall stature. She has thick limbs, beautiful eyes and eyebrows, and is well-spoken. She has prominent teeth <note>original: "fakhula al-sinn"; literally "masculine teeth," likely implying they are large or strong</note>, performs good deeds, and is humble in her needs. She has little greed, possesses wide-reaching sustenance, and keeps her clothes and body clean. She is blessed with luck and is known for her goodness. She will receive compassion and love from a man of great status. The slightest thing breaks her heart, yet she continues to endure hardships. She has no luck from anyone and remains modest even regarding the shirt she wears. As time passes, God Almighty gives her more than they have. In this month, she shall have a great joy and an increase in wealth.

### **The Discourse on the Sign of Capricorn and Saturn**

->The sage Abu Ma'shar said:<- The woman born under this rising sign <term>tali'</term> <note>original: "tali'"; the astrological sign ascending on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> will be of brown complexion, with a lovely gait and a fleshy face. She has a small nose and head, is patient during hardships, possesses much goodness, and loves guests. She is pleasant in speech and will have many children; she will find great comfort from some of them while being exhausted by others. They [the children] will listen to her, but she will encounter some strife regarding her livelihood. She will be like a queen regarding hidden matters, and she will not be under anyone's thumb. Everyone who sees her will envy her for her status. She is destined to perform the pilgrimage to the House of God <note>The Hajj to Mecca</note> and visit the grave of Muhammad, upon him be the best of peace. As she grows older, her status and influence will increase. She will have good luck with her husband, except for enemies who turn their faces from her. She should not be careless with her soul and should perform something to nullify their plots, for their nature is like water flowing beneath her while she treats them well. She has a mole or a beauty mark on her body. Anyone who approaches them with kindness, she will offer them her garments [in generosity], but whoever approaches them with force will gain nothing from her. She will suffer from many illnesses; for her, one should take bamboo silica <term>tabasheer</term> <note>original: "tabasheer"; a translucent white substance composed mainly of silica and water, obtained from the nodal joints of some species of bamboo, used in ancient medicine</note> and anise <term>anisun</term> on an empty stomach. If she persists with this in hot water, she will be cured, God willing. She faces a danger at night; the Name of God should be worn by them for protection. She also faces a danger at twenty-five years of age; if she survives, she will live seventy years. And God knows best.

### **The Discourse on the Sign of Aquarius and Saturn**

->The sage Abu Ma'shar said:<- The woman born under this rising sign <note>The text uses "al-Dalla," a common manuscript corruption of "al-Dalw," meaning the Water-Bearer or Aquarius</note> will have a fleshy face, thin eyebrows, and a good nature. She has long hair, light bones, and a round face. She always prefers to hide her secrets. She may be of little religious devotion but is pleasant in her talk with people. She will have few children. Most of her pains come from backaches. Her temperament is hot and moist; her remedy is anything moderate and soft. She should use *murrah* <term>murrah</term> <note>original: "al-murrah"; myrrh, used for its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties</note>... <unclear>for males and females</unclear>. Back pain consumes them, and she must set her back right. If she experiences a lack of affection, she should drink the medicine of "the end of the summer" <note>original: "dabr al-qayth"; likely a seasonal herbal preparation</note>. If she desires children, she should carry a pouch <term>sufa</term> <note>original: "sufa"; a small medicinal or aromatic sachet worn or used internally</note> and fumigate herself. She should not sleep by her husband's side on Sunday nights or Wednesday nights. At the moment of intimacy with her husband, she should say these three words: *“No effort has patience regarding them, and he shall not lie with any other.”* And she repeats: *“Go, go, go, the love and affection of [Name] into her heart.”* A charm against magic and the Follower <term>al-tabi'a</term> <note>original: "al-tabi'a"; a female spirit or jinn in folklore believed to follow women and cause miscarriages or marital strife</note> should be hung upon her.

### **The Discourse on the Sign of Pisces and Jupiter**

The sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi (787–886 CE), known in the West as Albumasar, the most influential astrologer of the Middle Ages</note> said: The woman born under this rising sign <term>tali'</term> shall be beautiful of face and good in character. She loves amusement, play, and laughter. She has a broad forehead, a long neck, a rounded face, and beautiful eyes. There shall be <unclear>...</unclear> and a mark on her stomach as well. She is of moderate means between <unclear>...</unclear> they do not know her as one who fulfills the needs of the people. One who covets a need from her soul <unclear>...</unclear> from her. She should wear an iron ring on her hand <unclear>...</unclear> except that enemies may enter upon her until she performs a deed that turns their faces back toward her. Her "arrow of fate" <note>an astrological calculation for significant life events</note> falls at twenty years and thirty years; if she passes these, she shall live a long life. God knows best the unseen and the most sublime.

The completion of its transcription was by the hand of Sheikh Haydar, son of al-Hajji Abd al-Karim, son of al-Jwad, from Mosul <note>A major city in modern-day Iraq</note>, the righteous and lawful, in the city of Aleppo the Guarded <note>original: "Halab al-mahrusa"; a traditional honorific for the city of Aleppo, Syria</note>. This was at the end of Monday, the fourth of the month of Ramadan the Magnified, in the year 839 Hijri <note>Approximately March 23, 1436 CE</note>. May God have mercy on whoever looks upon this and prays for forgiveness for its owner, for his parents, and for all Muslims together. Abu Ubayd Allah al-Mahalli <note>A scholar likely referencing traditional lore regarding the Arabic alphabet</note> said: Abujad, Hawwaz, Hutti, Kaliman, Sa'fas, and Qarasht <note>These are mnemonic words used to remember the order of the Arabic alphabet; here, they are personified as historical figures</note> were the Kings of Midian. Their kingdom existed during the time of the Prophet Shuaib <note>A prophet mentioned in the Quran, often identified with the biblical Jethro</note>. On the "Day of the Shadow" <note>A reference to the divine punishment of Midian mentioned in the Quran (Surah Ash-Shu'ara), where a dark cloud brought fire or a scorching heat</note>, King Kalimun perished. When he died, his daughter wept for him, saying:

"Kalimun has demolished my pillar;
He perished in the heart of the settlement, the master of the people.
Death came to him, calling from beneath his canopy;
Fire was cast upon them, and their home vanished away;
So they became prostrate in their dwellings."
